Re-anchored or updated: the France protests card (BBC; 70,000 police), the Singapore haze card (CNA's 2pm update, matching NEA data on data.gov.sg), and the Jordan, West Bank and migrant-worker cards (new details from ST, CNA, Al Jazeera and Mothership).

Top Stories: BBC World and regional feeds, CNA (World/Asia), ST World, Al Jazeera, Ukrinform and the Kyiv Independent. Single-outlet items are attributed in the card text; the US embassy drawdown over Iranian attack plans rests on unnamed US officials via ST. Skipped: analysis, interview, video and feature items (including ST's 'signs point to renewed US ops' analysis, a BBC interview with a former border patrol chief, Al Jazeera on Netanyahu and Israeli institutions, and a Reuters report on past US requests to SpaceX over Starlink), and light items such as New York's mayor and his bidets.

Singapore: CNA and ST Singapore feeds, NEA PSI and weather and LTA COE data on data.gov.sg (COE table unchanged; the Oct 2nd exercise matches the API), and a Mothership homepage scrape (nine new links; article clock timestamps). The Indonesian gas-export cut rests on Mothership citing SKK Migas and CNBC Indonesia; a web search found no second report, so the card is attributed and hedged. Outbreaks: WHO's DON API still lists DON622 (23 Oct) as the newest notice, ECDC's multi-country Ebola page is unchanged since 23 Oct 16:45 CEST, and the ECDC CDTR feed had nothing new, so the tiles are unchanged. The BBC's report of Kenya's second Ebola death was added as a source to the existing card.

Cybersecurity: BleepingComputer feed and /news/security/ listing via WebFetch (nothing newer than the 09:00 edition; newest item 23 Oct 16:55 ET) and The Hacker News RSS (nothing newer than 24 Oct 00:20 IST, already covered). top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: The Iran standoff sharpened on Saturday, as Tehran's military chief said US warships would never be allowed into the Gulf, a day after Trump hinted at renewed strikes. Washington is behaving as if it expects trouble, cutting embassy staff across the region over intelligence that Iran is planning attacks on Americans, though that account rests on unnamed officials. The Oleshky ceasefire and November talks in Abu Dhabi remain the week's one diplomatic opening on Ukraine. Elsewhere the focus is security at home, with France putting 70,000 police on the streets for a new day of protests and Jordan tightening security after the church funeral attack. The next 48 hours test whether Trump's weekend threat turns into strikes, and whether France gets through Saturday without a repeat of last week's riots.

stories.headline: Trump hints at 'another little Epic Fury' against Iran as a US envoy says a strike could come this weekend
stories.summary: 'We may do another little Epic Fury,' Trump told a rally in Fort Myers, Florida, on 23 Oct, using the US military's name for its war on Iran, The Straits Times reports; he did not elaborate. Tom Barrack, the US ambassador to Turkey, who has no direct role on Iran, answered 'Absolutely' when asked on a podcast whether there could be a strike this weekend, CNA reports. Turkey's foreign minister Hakan Fidan, after meeting counterparts from Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Germany, France, Britain and Italy in Istanbul, said they agreed a new attack on Iran would widen the war.

stories.headline: Iran says US warships will not be allowed into the Gulf 'under any circumstances' as strike threats mount
stories.summary: 'We will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances and at any time,' Iran's armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi said on 24 Oct, according to Iranian state television cited by The Straits Times; Al Jazeera's live page carried the same statement. It came a day after Trump hinted at renewed strikes and US envoy Tom Barrack said one could come this weekend. Iran has restricted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz since the war began on 28 Feb.

stories.headline: US cuts embassy staff in the Middle East over intelligence that Iran is planning attacks on Americans, officials say
stories.summary: US officials said on 23 Oct that the government had put employees on heightened alert across the Middle East and moved to reduce staff at embassies and consulates, after intelligence showed Iran was in the 'advanced stages' of planning attacks on Americans, The Straits Times reports. A memo to Secretary of State Marco Rubio said agencies had 'received intelligence that Iran has substantially increased efforts to target US personnel'. The account rests on unnamed officials and has not been independently confirmed; Iran has not responded.

stories.headline: Iran has plans to target Gulf undersea internet cables if attacked again, two Iranian officials tell Reuters
stories.summary: Two senior Iranian security officials, speaking anonymously, told Reuters that Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to hit undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the US and Israel attack Iran again, CNA and The Straits Times report; they gave few details. Iranian officials had earlier warned the cables could become targets if diplomacy with Washington collapses. The claim has not been independently verified.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree a local ceasefire in occupied Oleshky, and peace negotiators will meet in Abu Dhabi in November
stories.summary: The White House said US First Lady Melania Trump secured the truce for the Russian-occupied town in Kherson region, which it called 'on the brink of disaster' without medicine, food and clean water, the BBC reports. Ukraine's General Staff and the Kremlin both confirmed it, and both sides say firing stops at 02:00 GMT on 27 Oct to allow aid deliveries and evacuations; the White House had given 29 Oct. Separately, Zelensky said Ukrainian, Russian and US negotiators agreed to technical-level talks in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November, The Straits Times reports (Reuters).
stories.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Reuters), Ukrinform, CNA

stories.headline: France deploys 70,000 police for a new day of nationwide protests, a week after its worst riots in years
stories.summary: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said about 70,000 security personnel would be deployed on 24 Oct, warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media, The Straits Times reports; the BBC says sweeping restrictions have been imposed on demonstrations but hundreds of thousands are still expected in Paris and elsewhere. The protests, started by high-school students over learning conditions, have widened into anger over the cost of living. Luxury boutiques boarded up windows and some planned to stay shut after shops were looted last weekend, ST reports.

stories.headline: Gunmen kill seven at a church funeral in Jordan; the government calls it terrorism and declares three days of mourning
stories.summary: Gunmen opened fire during a funeral procession at a Greek Orthodox church in Hammoud village, Karak governorate, on 23 Oct, killing seven people, CNA (AFP) and The Straits Times (Reuters) report; the BBC cites state media for the same toll. Interior Minister Mazen Al-Faraya said 'a terrorist group' carried out the attack and security services were hunting the attackers, and Prime Minister Jafar Hassan ordered three days of national mourning. CNA reports that King Abdullah vowed retaliation. There has been no claim of responsibility. On 24 Oct the US embassy in Amman said security had been stepped up at malls, embassies and other sites across Jordan, The Straits Times reports.
stories.source: CNA (AFP), BBC, The Straits Times (Reuters), The Straits Times

stories.headline: Netanyahu launches a major West Bank operation after two Israeli soldiers are killed near Hebron
stories.summary: Netanyahu announced the operation on 23 Oct after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three Israelis at a checkpoint near Hebron before being shot dead, according to the Israeli military, The Straits Times and the BBC report. Israeli forces began a 'targeted' operation in Hebron, Al Jazeera reports, and Netanyahu had ordered the army to prepare a full closure of the occupied West Bank. Security is a central issue in Tuesday's election, in which Netanyahu faces a tight race. The military said the operation would last several days and include searches and demolitions, CNA reports, and Al Jazeera correspondents said forces raided at least 15 northern West Bank towns on 24 Oct, detaining dozens of Palestinians.
stories.source: The Straits Times, BBC, Al Jazeera, CNA, Al Jazeera

stories.headline: Macron calls a drive-by shooting near Paris that killed one and wounded five a 'racist terrorist attack'
stories.summary: A gunman firing from a car killed one person and wounded five, including a 12-year-old girl, in Trappes and La Verrière south-west of Paris on 23 Oct, CNA (AFP) reports; he was arrested. Most of the victims were from foreign backgrounds, and anti-terror prosecutors are investigating whether they were targeted for their real or supposed race, ethnicity, nationality or religion. 'What happened here today was a racist terrorist attack,' Macron said on a visit to Trappes.

stories.headline: Ship attacks around the Strait of Hormuz hit a record in October, and an oil slick from a damaged tanker reaches UAE beaches
stories.summary: A Washington Institute for Near East Policy tracker has logged 28 confirmed and reported attacks on shipping in and around the strait in October, the most on record, and 113 since the war began on 28 Feb, The Straits Times reports. BBC Verify says satellite images show an oil slick from a tanker matching the Gem No.2, damaged on 9-10 Oct, spreading more than 35km along the UAE coast; UAE authorities said beaches near Umm Al Quwain were affected and some were closed.

stories.headline: Fire guts Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat in Bavaria, and police detain a suspect
stories.summary: Firefighters found the Kehlsteinhaus above Berchtesgaden 'completely ablaze' after an alarm at 21:15 local time on 23 Oct, and it was still burning on Saturday morning, Bavarian police said, according to the BBC and The Straits Times. About 200 emergency workers were deployed, difficult terrain slowed the response and nobody was hurt. Police said a 'suspicious person' was taken into temporary custody; no motive has been given.

stories.headline: US lifts some tariffs on Canadian goods two weeks before the midterms, after Senator Susan Collins lobbied for it
stories.summary: From 30 Oct, the 50% tariffs will be eased on goods including plywood, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment, the White House said, the BBC reports. Collins, a Republican in a tight race in Maine, first announced the exemptions. Trump also said Canada was 'working very hard' to reach a trade deal, CNA reports.

stories.headline: Rubio urges Cubans seeking change to work with the CIA, as Trump says Cuba comes 'on our way back from Iran'
stories.summary: 'To those who seek to create positive change in Cuba - now is the time,' Secretary of State Marco Rubio wrote on X on 23 Oct, urging those disappointed by Cuba's government to partner with the CIA, The Straits Times reports (Reuters); Al Jazeera also carried the remarks. At a Florida rally the same day, Trump said 'We'll take care of Cuba on our way back from Iran' and that Rubio would then 'finish up the deal'. Havana's response was not reported.

stories.headline: Pentagon designates US campuses' Confucius Institutes a national security threat
stories.summary: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said in a video on 23 Oct that the Chinese-funded cultural centres had been added to the Pentagon's list of institutions that threaten US national security, alleging they operate 'under disguise' at US universities, The Straits Times reports. Washington has long accused the institutes of serving as Chinese propaganda tools.
stories.source: The Straits Times, CNA, Al Jazeera

stories.headline: Trump administration sues to block certification of Alaska's Senate race if Republican Dan Sullivan loses
stories.summary: The Justice Department's lawsuit, filed on 22 Oct, argues that a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot could confuse voters, the BBC reports. Polls show Democrat Mary Peltola narrowly ahead of Senator Sullivan before the 3 Nov vote. Al Jazeera also reports the suit.

stories.headline: Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro trade attacks over living costs and corruption in the last debate before Brazil's runoff
stories.summary: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, sparred for over two hours on Globo on 23 Oct ahead of Sunday's runoff, The Straits Times reports (Reuters). Bolsonaro led the first round earlier this month, but polls this week show the two about even. Both focused on the cost of living, and traded accusations of corruption.

stories.headline: Typhoon Champi kills one and injures about 350 in Taiwan before heading towards China and Japan
stories.summary: The storm swept past Taiwan's north-east on 23 Oct, toppling trees, closing schools and shops, cutting power to thousands of households and forcing more than 4,300 people from their homes, Al Jazeera (AFP) reports, citing one death and at least 350 injured. Earlier official figures cited by the BBC were 171 injured. Hundreds of flights in the region were cancelled as Champi moves towards China and Japan.

stories.headline: Moldova expels a Russian diplomat after a Russian Geran drone falls near homes
stories.summary: President Maia Sandu said on 23 Oct that the drone came down near family homes and an energy facility in central Moldova, and a member of the Russian embassy was declared persona non grata, the Kyiv Independent reports. 'Russia's war keeps putting Moldovan lives at risk,' she said.

stories.headline: Drone strike sinks a cargo ship off Romania, killing one sailor with three missing; Romania blames Russia
stories.summary: The Comoros-flagged Khoryv, with 13 Ukrainian and Azerbaijani crew, sank 13 nautical miles off Constanța, just outside Romanian territorial waters, on 23 Oct; nine sailors were rescued, one body was recovered and three are missing, Romania's naval authority said, The Straits Times reports (Reuters). President Nicușor Dan said the ship was hit by a drone and called it 'part of Russia's escalation process in its war in Ukraine'. At least seven cargo ships have been hit off Romania and Bulgaria in the past two weeks, ST reports.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine swap 270 prisoners each in their first exchange in two months
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said 270 Ukrainians, including nine civilians, came home on 23 Oct, most of them held since 2022 and many captured at Mariupol, while 270 people were returned to Russia, The Straits Times and the Kyiv Independent report. Five of those freed had been believed killed in the 2022 explosion at the Olenivka detention site, ST reports. The swap followed talks with US negotiators earlier this week.

stories.headline: Trump says he will call Musk if Ukraine's Starshield problems persist, as Ukraine reports continuing signal losses
stories.summary: 'If there is a problem, I will get it straightened out,' Trump told reporters on 23 Oct, saying he had not yet spoken to Musk, The Straits Times reports; Ukraine's Defence Ministry said signal losses on the military-grade service were still being observed. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham stressed in a call with Trump that Ukraine needs full Starlink access, Downing Street said. Zelensky has announced plans for an independent satellite system, Al Jazeera reports (DPA).
stories.source: The Straits Times, Al Jazeera (DPA), Kyiv Independent

stories.headline: Argentine judge drops the criminal case against President Milei and his sister over the $Libra crypto collapse
stories.summary: Federal judge Marcelo Martínez de Giorgi dismissed the case at prosecutors' request, court records show, the BBC reports. Milei had denied promoting the coin, which collapsed shortly after he posted about it in February 2025, and said he acted 'in good faith'. The Straits Times also reports the ruling.
stories.source: BBC, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

stories.headline: Ecuador judge orders former presidential candidate Luisa González held in pre-trial detention
stories.summary: The order on 23 Oct came a day after González, who ran against President Daniel Noboa in 2023, was arrested in a money-laundering investigation, Al Jazeera reports (AFP).

stories.headline: UN warns time is running out to reach Yemen's Taiz after almost three weeks of a Houthi siege
stories.summary: The Houthis have encircled the city since early October, cutting the road to Aden, the seat of the internationally recognised government, and blocking supplies, the UN said, according to Al Jazeera (AFP).

stories.headline: Tigray official urges rebels to disarm after the TPLF lost Mekelle; a rebel commander vows to keep fighting
stories.summary: An official in Tigray's new federally backed administration called on fighters to lay down their weapons on 23 Oct, hours after a TPLF commander told them to keep resisting, Al Jazeera reports. TPLF forces withdrew from Mekelle, the regional capital, in early October.

stories.headline: US charges a government contractor with leaking classified reports to his girlfriend's Substack
stories.summary: The FBI arrested Ian Brinksman, 42, at his Washington home on 23 Oct, and prosecutors charged him with unlawfully transmitting national defence information, a Justice Department statement said, The Straits Times reports. The FBI alleges he repeatedly accessed classified intelligence reports outside his duties and passed them to a romantic partner who intended to publish them. He has not yet entered a plea.

stories.headline: Australian MP Helen Haines improves to serious but stable after an alleged deliberate car attack
stories.summary: The independent MP, 65, whose legs were amputated after she was hit by a car outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday, is now in a serious but stable condition, Melbourne's Alfred Hospital said on Saturday morning, the BBC reports. It is the first improvement since she was airlifted there. A 43-year-old man has been charged over what authorities say was a deliberate attack.

stories.headline: Austria expels four Russian diplomats over suspected spying
stories.summary: Austria's foreign ministry declared four Vienna-based Russian diplomats personae non gratae on 23 Oct over 'activities incompatible with their diplomatic status', a term usually used for spying; three worked at the embassy and one at Russia's OSCE delegation on military security and arms control, The Straits Times and the Kyiv Independent report. Moscow vowed a response, the Kyiv Independent reports.

stories.headline: Kremlin denies freeing US citizen Stephen Hubbard in exchange for a Russian war blogger
stories.summary: The Kremlin said on 23 Oct that Russia's release of Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired teacher held since 2022, was not a swap for a Russian war blogger recently freed in Montenegro, The Straits Times reports. Putin announced the release on 21 Oct as a humanitarian gesture, and Trump said Russia had not asked for anything in return.

stories.headline: British jets join a French nuclear-deterrent exercise for the first time
stories.summary: British and French jets flew together over the Mediterranean in the first joint exercise involving France's airborne nuclear capability, Paris said on 23 Oct, CNA reports. The two countries agreed in July 2025 to reinforce cooperation over their nuclear arsenals in response to growing threats to Europe.

stories.headline: China urges the US to end 'discriminatory' measures against Chinese research institutions
stories.summary: China's commerce ministry said on 23 Oct that the US should 'respect the facts' and immediately end the measures, after the US Department of Defense put research-funding restrictions on dozens of Chinese universities, CNA reports.

stories.headline: Storm Austen cuts power to nearly 300,000 homes in France and about 12,000 in Britain
stories.summary: Winds of up to 179km/h and heavy rain disrupted trains and flights on 23 Oct, utility Enedis said, according to The Straits Times.

stories.headline: US consumer sentiment falls to a near-record low before the midterms
stories.summary: The University of Michigan's index fell in its final reading before the 3 Nov elections, as tensions with Iran pushed up prices, Al Jazeera reports (Reuters).

stories.headline: Two former FBI agents are charged with lying to Congress over the 2020 Hunter Biden laptop probe
stories.summary: Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides made their first court appearance in Washington on 23 Oct, Al Jazeera reports (AP).

stories.headline: Several people missing after a multistorey building under construction collapses in Nairobi
stories.summary: The building came down at about 1pm local time on 23 Oct on a busy commercial street in Eastleigh, and rescuers were digging through the rubble for several missing people, Al Jazeera reports (AFP, AP). The Nairobi governor's office had said its ground floor was occupied. The cause is not yet known.
stories.source: Al Jazeera (AFP, AP), The Straits Times (Reuters)

stories.headline: UK quietly advises households to keep three days of emergency supplies
stories.summary: Guidance published on a government website on 22 Oct, with a written statement to Parliament by Security Minister Dan Jarvis, tells households to be able to look after themselves for three days in a national emergency, The Straits Times reports. ST describes it as a shift towards more urgent messaging amid concern about Russian hybrid attacks, AI-driven cyber attacks and climate change.

stories.headline: Trump's diesel relief efforts grow costlier as US prices keep rising before the midterms
stories.summary: US diesel prices rose nearly 10 cents a gallon last week to an average of US$6.28, The Straits Times reports, despite aid to farmers, relaxed trucking rules and eased sanctions on Russian fuel. The first tanker carrying Russian diesel under a deal Trump announced on 9 Oct, with about 40,000 tonnes aboard, is heading to New York, the Kyiv Independent reports, citing LSEG ship-tracking data.

stories.headline: Pope Leo cancels an Assisi visit to aid his recovery from lung cancer surgery
stories.summary: The Vatican said on 23 Oct that the 71-year-old pope would skip the planned 27 Oct trip to avoid a helicopter flight, on doctors' advice, while his doctors said a chest examination showed excellent progress, The Straits Times reports. He had the lower lobe of his right lung removed on 13 Oct.

stories.headline: Cyprus police open an investigation into Roman Abramovich's financial affairs
stories.summary: The police Financial Intelligence Unit will examine the findings of a BBC Panorama and Bureau of Investigative Journalism report alleging that accountancy firm Deloitte helped falsify documents to hide his wealth and evade tax, a Cypriot justice ministry official told MPs, the BBC reports. Abramovich's lawyers say he denies concealing his fortune.

stories.headline: Sarawak's state assembly will be dissolved on 26 Oct, opening the way to an election within 60 days
stories.summary: Sarawak Premier Abang Johari Openg announced the dissolution on 23 Oct after obtaining the state governor's consent, CNA reports. It follows a run of Malaysian state elections over the past year, with Melaka due to vote on 14 November.

stories.headline: Indonesia seizes 1.1 tonnes of ketamine from a foreign tanker off Sumatra
stories.summary: Police said on 23 Oct the drugs were found on a foreign vessel in Sumatran waters, the country's second major drug bust in two months, CNA reports. An AFP photo caption says methamphetamine was also displayed from the haul aboard the Mongolian-flagged tanker MT Global 168.

stories.headline: El Niño-driven drought raises a new famine risk in war-torn Sudan
stories.summary: Higher temperatures and drought linked to El Niño are hurting crops and livestock across Sudan's rain-fed southern farming belt, where pockets of famine have already emerged during more than three years of war, The Straits Times reports (Reuters).

stories.headline: Malawi's opposition demands answers over President Mutharika's long stay in South Africa
stories.summary: The 86-year-old president left Malawi on 6 Oct for what officials called a private visit, his fifth trip to South Africa this year, with little information released, the BBC reports. The opposition says the country needs decisive action as it struggles with fuel shortages, power cuts and economic difficulties.

stories.headline: Czech government fast-tracks a public media overhaul that critics call a power grab
stories.summary: Andrej Babiš's ruling coalition moved on 23 Oct to fast-track legislation that would move public broadcasters' financing into the state budget and cut their funding, The Straits Times reports (Reuters); critics say it threatens press independence.

stories.headline: Foreign diplomats in Brasília discuss quickly recognising the winner of Sunday's runoff
stories.summary: Four ambassadors said missions are discussing rapid recognition of whoever wins Brazil's presidential runoff, to ward off attempts from outside the country to call the result prematurely, The Straits Times reports (Reuters); no plan has been formalised yet.

stories.headline: Denmark will phase out mink farming by 2029 after dropping its bid for an EU exemption
stories.summary: The ban takes effect on 7 August 2027, followed by a two-year transition, after the government decided not to pursue an exemption from an EU-wide ban, the BBC reports. Denmark was once the world's largest producer of mink fur.

stories.headline: Wildfire heat and smoke threaten the world's oldest known cave paintings in Sulawesi
stories.summary: Heat and smoke from Indonesia's worst wildfires in more than a decade risk speeding up the decay of rock art in Maros-Pangkep, South Sulawesi, including a scene dated by Griffith University researchers to at least 51,200 years old, CNA reports.

stories.headline: Hundreds of Ethiopians flee into Kenya after fighting in the border town of Moyale
stories.summary: Kenyan police said hundreds of people, mostly women and children, crossed at several points in Moyale, fleeing fighting between forces from Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regions that Ethiopian media say began over the raising of the Somali regional state's flag, Al Jazeera reports (AP, Reuters). The Kenya Red Cross is setting up support for them. The Kenya Red Cross said on 23 Oct it was sending supplies that would initially reach 1,000 households, The Straits Times reports.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Reuters), Al Jazeera (AP, Reuters)

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Haze stayed unhealthy across the island through Saturday afternoon, and NEA closed part of East Coast Park's beach after oil patches were found. Energy has become the new pressure point with Jakarta: Indonesia's upstream regulator says it is cutting pipeline gas to Singapore from today, though so far only Mothership has reported the figures and Singapore has not responded. Online safety moved forward as well, with laws on age checks for teens on social media due in early 2027 and IMDA's first app store audit removing 65 harmful apps. The buzz is haze-flavoured, from a minister's reassurance that tap water is safe despite videos of dark rainwater to tourists rerouting their plans. Winds are expected to shift from Sunday and could thin the haze, so keep checking NEA readings, and watch for Singapore's reply on gas.

stories.headline: Haze stays unhealthy across Singapore, with the 24-hour PSI at 113 to 153 at 2pm
stories.summary: At 2pm on 24 Oct the 24-hour PSI ranged from 113 in the south to 153 in the west, all in the unhealthy band (101-200), CNA reports; NEA data on data.gov.sg show the same readings. Hourly PM2.5 readings fluctuated between 52 and 88, and the south returned to the normal band at 11am. NEA forecasts a 24-hour PSI of 90 to 140 for Saturday and says conditions could improve from Sunday, when winds are expected to shift to the southwest or west and carry less smoke from Sumatra.

stories.headline: Part of East Coast Park's beach is closed after oil patches are found, and NEA advises against swimming
stories.summary: The National Environment Agency said on 24 Oct that the beach section of East Coast Park Area D would be temporarily closed while oil patches are cleaned up, and advised the public not to swim or take part in water activities there, The Straits Times reports. NEA did not say where the oil came from.

stories.headline: Indonesia's upstream regulator says it will cut pipeline gas exports to Singapore from 24 Oct, Mothership reports
stories.summary: SKK Migas chief Djoko Siswanto said on 23 Oct that gas exports to Singapore would be cut by 31 billion British thermal units a day from 24 Oct, 15 from Natuna and 16 from Sumatra, Mothership reports, citing CNBC Indonesia; he said only Singapore would be affected because the pipelines run directly to it. The announcement came a day after Energy Minister Bahlil Lahadalia threatened to stop exports to countries that 'disrespect' Indonesia, remarks CNA also reported. Indonesia had planned lower volumes for years under a supply deal running to 2028. No second outlet had confirmed the cut figures by publication, and Singapore had not commented.

stories.headline: NEA serves legal notices on 10 Singapore-based firms under the haze law for the first time, including Asia Pulp & Paper
stories.summary: The palm oil and forestry companies own land concessions in Indonesia or have related companies that do, and must provide information on those links, the locations of the concessions, and their fire prevention and firefighting measures, NEA said on 23 Oct, CNA, The Straits Times and Mothership report. It is the first time NEA has issued such notices to Singapore companies since the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act took effect. Firms' representatives who fail to comply face a fine of up to S$5,000, a month in jail, or both, ST reports. NEA is also seeking more from 10 Indonesian firms served notices in the past week.

stories.headline: Singapore will set up a specialist panel of law, audit and investigative firms to probe companies linked to the haze
stories.summary: The Ministry of Law said on 23 Oct that the panel will trace corporate relationships and supply chains across jurisdictions to establish whether local and foreign companies caused or condoned the fires, CNA and The Straits Times report. Davinder Singh Chambers has been appointed to advise the government on coordinating its work, ST reports.

stories.headline: Singapore will legislate in early 2027 for age checks and safer design on social media for teens
stories.summary: The Ministry of Digital Development and Information said on 24 Oct that about 80 per cent of parents and nearly 70 per cent of youths it consulted, out of more than 2,000, prefer tiered access to social media over an outright ban, CNA reports. It plans legislation early next year requiring platforms to apply effective age assurance so that protections for young users can be enforced, along with safer platform features, Mothership reports.

stories.headline: IMDA's first app store audit finds 65 harmful apps, including nudification tools, and 24 wrongly age-rated ones
stories.summary: A review of more than 7,000 apps across the Apple, Google, Huawei, Microsoft and Samsung stores found 65 with harmful content and 24 not rated 18+ as the stores' own rules require, the Infocomm Media Development Authority said on 24 Oct, CNA and The Straits Times report. Sexual and violent content and apps facilitating vice and organised crime were the most common; ST says the flagged apps included AI nudification tools and murder- and gambling-themed games with payouts. IMDA said all have since been removed or re-rated.

stories.headline: Grace Fu says tap water is still safe to drink after videos of blackish rainwater collected during the haze
stories.summary: Environment Minister Grace Fu said on Instagram on 24 Oct, after visiting PUB's water quality lab, that rainwater collected in hazy conditions can contain more particles but 'our tap water remains safe and clean to drink', Mothership reports. Photos and videos of dark rainwater in pails had been circulating online.

stories.headline: PUB warned motorists to avoid Punggol Way at the TPE slip road for an hour over flash-flood risk
stories.summary: PUB posted the advisory on X at 1.48pm on 24 Oct, after NEA warned of heavy rain over many parts of Singapore from 1.30pm to 2.30pm, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Nearly 240 migrant workers have gone unpaid for up to two months, and NTUC is helping with daily needs
stories.summary: The process-sector workers are affected by alleged salary issues at Process Maintenance Solutions and Jurong Technical & Construction, NTUC deputy secretary-general Desmond Choo said on 23 Oct, CNA reports. The Migrant Workers' Centre says it has met 230 workers from two companies, Process Maintenance Solutions and Jurong Technical & Construction, over alleged unpaid salaries, Mothership reports, and The Straits Times says about 90 are receiving daily meals.

stories.headline: DBS to give 500,000 N95 masks to about 275,000 vulnerable seniors and migrant workers
stories.summary: The S$1 million haze relief initiative, announced on 23 Oct, gives each recipient a set of two masks, and DBS will also supply air purifiers to social service agencies that serve vulnerable seniors, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Police warn of Carousell phishing scams that have cost victims at least S$180,000 since July
stories.summary: At least 63 cases have been reported since July, the police said in an advisory on 23 Oct, The Straits Times reports. Scammers pose as interested buyers and direct sellers to a fake Carousell website, where a chatbot walks them through a supposed bank-account 'verification' to receive payment.

stories.headline: Upper Bukit Timah Canal upgrade is complete, adding 30% more stormwater capacity in a flood-prone area
stories.summary: PUB said on 23 Oct that works on the final 900m stretch, begun in 2019, have finished, completing upgrades along the whole 2.3km canal, CNA and The Straits Times report. The extra capacity serves a catchment of about 1,000 hectares and should help limit flash floods during the year-end rainy season, ST reports.

stories.headline: Foodpanda offers full-time rider jobs with a S$1,800 basic salary and CPF contributions
stories.summary: The full-time option, with fixed shifts and employee benefits, is for now open only to bicycle and e-bike riders, who must work 44 hours a week, The Straits Times reports. Riders who sign up now get a S$600 bonus spread over six months.

stories.headline: Singapore needs about 3,000 more regular social-service volunteers by 2030, doubling the pool, MSF says
stories.summary: The Ministry of Social and Family Development said on 23 Oct that volunteer roles in befriending, mentoring, fostering and family support are expanding; it currently has more than 3,000 active volunteers, CNA and The Straits Times report.

stories.headline: SAF tests drones and a 5G battlefield communications node at Exercise Wallaby in Australia
stories.summary: About 6,000 Singapore soldiers and 1,200 platforms are taking part in the SAF's largest unilateral overseas exercise near Rockhampton, Queensland, The Straits Times reports, including counter-drone systems and a 5G-enabled aerial communications node.

stories.headline: Brunei's Prince Abdul Mateen visits the SAF's Special Operations Task Force
stories.summary: During an official visit to Singapore on 23 Oct, the prince was briefed on the SAF's special operations capabilities, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Serial voyeur jailed 28 weeks for upskirt filming and warned he could be caned if he reoffends
stories.summary: Gary Huang Kunjie, 41, who has been in and out of jail since 2018 for similar offences, pleaded guilty to one count of voyeurism committed in June, and the court imposed a longer term than the prosecution sought, CNA reports.

stories.headline: Man jailed 80 days for shoving a seven-year-old who hit his daughter at an indoor playground
stories.summary: Koh Gek Kuan, 44, pleaded guilty to voluntarily causing hurt to a child under 14 after shoving the boy to the ground twice, CNA and Mothership report; a second similar charge was taken into consideration. A gag order bars identifying the boy and the playground.

stories.headline: Police appeal for information on a 24-year-old woman missing since 22 Oct in Woodlands
stories.summary: Siti Nordiana Sapuwan was last seen near Block 577 Woodlands Drive 16 at about 8pm on 22 Oct, the police said; anyone with information can call 1800-255-0000, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Man jailed for emailing an intimate video of his girlfriend to her colleagues and bosses
stories.summary: The 40-year-old pleaded guilty on 22 Oct to intentionally distributing an intimate recording after learning she had been unfaithful, and had used ChatGPT to draft the email, Mothership reports, citing Shin Min Daily News.

stories.headline: Man fined S$7,000 for running an unlicensed massage parlour in Orchard Towers
stories.summary: The 65-year-old ran the outlet, styled as a facial and beauty business, in 2022, and a police raid found sexual services being offered there, according to court documents seen by Mothership.

stories.headline: Some tourists mask up or change plans because of the haze, and tour operators report a dip in bookings
stories.summary: Visitors told The Straits Times they had trimmed outdoor itineraries or carried N95 masks, and some tour operators said bookings had fallen during the haze. Air quality had improved for a few days before Saturday's deterioration, after an earlier 19-day stretch of unhealthy air, ST says.

stories.headline: FairPrice Foundation pledges S$3 million to Hao Ren Hao Shi's grocery runs for low-income residents
stories.summary: The three-year partnership announced on 24 Oct will fund about 1,200 distributions under the charity's Mobile Groceries and Happy Mart schemes, giving more than 126,000 low-income people better access to fresh produce, eggs, milk and household essentials, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Roving climate-adaptation exhibition opens at One Punggol, with Wolbachia mosquitoes and cooling vests on show
stories.summary: The month-long 'Our Climate-Ready Home' exhibition shows how Singapore is preparing for a hotter climate, including a box of Project Wolbachia mosquitoes visitors can put their arm into, since they do not bite humans, The Straits Times reports. One Punggol is its first stop.

stories.headline: Tan Ser Seng's third-generation owners open a new outlet as the herbal soup brand turns 80
stories.summary: Siblings Allan and Vivian Tan, who had not planned to take over their grandfather's business, now run the brand known for traditionally brewed soups, CNA Lifestyle reports.

stories.headline: ITE student with a rare genetic disorder wins swimming bronze medals despite low muscle tone
stories.summary: Jessica Quek, 18, was born with PTPS deficiency, which affects brain chemicals and muscle tone, and won two bronze medals at the ITE Inter-College Swimming Meet in 2025 and 2026, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Team behind Michelin-starred Nae:um opens Osteria Da Su, an Italian restaurant led by a Korean chef
stories.summary: Chef Park Su-ji spent 10 years in Italy, including at three-Michelin-starred Da Vittorio, and pastas start from S$22 at the new restaurant next door to Nae:um, CNA Lifestyle reports.

stories.headline: The first Singapore Book Street at VivoCity on 2-8 Nov will feature more than 1,200 SingLit titles
stories.summary: Organised by the National Arts Council and the Singapore Book Publishers Association, the fair brings together more than 40 local publishers with books in all four official languages, plus poetry performances and a stamp rally, CNA reports.

stories.headline: NHG team that helped more than 130 patients back into work wins a Healthcare Humanity Award
stories.summary: The NHG Health Bounce Back Support Team, made up of occupational therapists and medical social workers from Tan Tock Seng, Khoo Teck Puat and Yishun Community hospitals, was recognised for helping patients find jobs after prolonged illness, The Straits Times reports.

stories.headline: Tree outside Margaret Drive Hawker Centre catches fire, and SCDF is investigating the cause
stories.summary: The Singapore Civil Defence Force told Mothership it was alerted at about 6.50pm on 22 Oct to a fire at Block 38A Margaret Drive in Queenstown; no one was hurt and the cause is under investigation. A TikTok video showed flames on a branch of the courtyard tree.

stories.headline: Taiwanese family doctor who cannot yet practise in Singapore volunteers at a hospital while caring for his children
stories.summary: Hsu Cheng Yuan, 48, moved to Singapore to join his wife, a doctor here, but has not secured a slot for the final stage of his registration assessment, Mothership reports. He now looks after his two young children and volunteers at a community hospital in his spare time.

stories.headline: Woman says a boy 'publicly shamed' her for returning 29 cans at a BCRS machine
stories.summary: Chermaine Kumar said on Instagram that a primary school boy waiting to return two cans grew impatient and commented on how many items she had; she said depositing all 29 took two minutes and 49 seconds, Mothership reports.

stories.headline: Chinese actor Zhang Linghe is refused entry to Taiwan for fan meetings
stories.summary: Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council rejected the 'Pursuit of Jade' star's application, saying he had repeatedly posted content undermining Taiwan's status and that the purpose of his visit was unclear, Mothership reports, citing Taiwan's Central News Agency. China's Taiwan Affairs Office accused Taipei of restricting cultural exchanges for political reasons.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Iran and the US escalated their warnings on Saturday: Tehran says US warships will never enter the Gulf, and Washington is thinning out its embassies over what officials call advanced Iranian attack plans. In Ukraine the Oleshky truce has not spread to the air war, with Russia launching 126 drones overnight and glide bombs killing a civilian in Kramatorsk. Ukraine is hitting infrastructure in return, and monitoring channels say a strike on a southern Russian substation blacked out most of occupied Crimea. In the West Bank, Israel's operation after the Hebron killings has spread to raids on at least 15 northern towns, three days before Israelis vote. Tuesday brings both the Oleshky ceasefire and Israel's election, so watch whether either front calms, or whether Trump's weekend strike threat lands first.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: Russia and Ukraine agreed a local ceasefire for occupied Oleshky from 27 Oct and technical-level talks in Abu Dhabi in November, Kyiv, Moscow and Washington say; strikes went on regardless, with 126 Russian drones overnight into 24 Oct, and monitoring channels report a blackout across occupied Crimea after an attack on a substation in southern Russia.

timeline.event: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opening the largest land war in Europe since 1945.

Ukrainian drones kill five people in a residential area of Russia's Rostov region and three more in the Belgorod, Kursk and Moscow regions, regional governors say; four others are reported killed in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. Moscow's regional governor calls it 'one of the most massive drone attacks in recent memory' and Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted 822 drones overnight.

Russian drones and missiles kill two people and wound 14 at ArcelorMittal's steel plant in Kryvyi Rih, which partially halts production, and burn down stalls at Kyiv's Pochaina second-hand book market. Zelensky says Ukrainian cities were hit by more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided bombs and 62 missiles over the past week, and renews his appeal for air defence.
A Spanish F-18 on NATO air-policing duty shoots down a drone that entered Romanian airspace from Moldova, about 24km north of Galati - the fourth drone downed over Romania this year.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and President Vladimir Putin exchange messages reaffirming bilateral ties to mark Korean Liberation Day.

Six people are killed and four injured, including a 14-year-old, in Ukrainian missile strikes on Russia's Belgorod region overnight, acting governor Alexander Shuvaev says on Telegram. A woman is also killed by a drone strike on a home in the Astrakhan region, its governor says. The claims have not been independently verified.
Russian forces attack port infrastructure in the Izmail district of Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, Ukrainian authorities say.
Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz says Russia attacked its facilities 13 times over the past week.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the bloc plans its most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia in the autumn, without giving timing or detail.
Documents reported by The Straits Times show Binance gave Russian authorities client details later used to charge a Russian over donations to Ukraine.
Russia's defence ministry says air defences intercepted 205 Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea between Sunday night and Monday morning. Kyiv has not commented on the figure.
A separate overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port city of Odesa damages a civilian vessel and injures four people, Ukrainian authorities say.
Moldova's foreign ministry condemns a violation of its airspace by an unidentified aerial object that later exploded on Moldovan territory. It did not name a country responsible.
Italy's government says it sees no sign of a Russian link to the explosion at the Colleferro munitions plant, pushing back on speculation about sabotage.
A Russian court jails a prominent anti-war opposition politician for 11 years over comments about the war, the independent outlet Mediazona reports.
Moscow warns of 'consequences' after reports that British-made drones were used in strikes on Russian territory. London has not confirmed the reports.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says 620 Ukrainian drones headed for the Moscow region between Monday evening and 5am and that 180 were downed over the region, in one of the largest attacks on the capital region of the war. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov says drones hit a Wildberries warehouse and other sites and that three people, including a 10-year-old girl, were injured; Moscow's airports temporarily restricted flights. The figures are Russian officials' account and Kyiv has not commented.

Russia's foreign ministry says the United Kingdom 'will pay' for supplying drones used in strikes on Russian territory, hardening the earlier warning of 'consequences'. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Russia summons Japan's ambassador over the disputed Kuril Islands, which Tokyo calls the Northern Territories. Japan has not detailed its response.
Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing is due in Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin on his first trip there as president, one of a small number of leaders visiting Russia during the war.

A Russian missile attack kills 10 people in a village in Ukraine's north-eastern Kharkiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky says, adding that Kyiv will respond. The figure is Ukraine's and has not been independently verified; Moscow has not commented.

A court in Stuttgart convicts a Ukrainian man over what German prosecutors describe as a Russian intelligence-linked plot to detonate parcels in Europe. Moscow has denied involvement in previous parcel-bomb cases.

The IAEA says a drone exploded at a bus stop used by staff of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killing one person and injuring several others. Russian officials blame Ukraine and call it one of the most serious incidents at the plant; Kyiv has not commented. The IAEA reports no nuclear safety or security damage.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia has the right to treat British involvement in strikes on Russian territory as participation in the war, according to Interfax. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says the United Kingdom 'supports Ukraine 100%' in response to Russia's warning over drones used against Russian territory.

Estonia's prime minister says the country is investigating whether Russia was involved in an arson attack last week on a building housing a defence contractor. No conclusion has been announced and Moscow has not commented.
Ukraine's new defence minister takes office after a parliamentary vote, which the country's anti-corruption agencies had opened a probe ahead of.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, publicly calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since the 2022 invasion. Ukraine has not held elections under martial law.

German federal prosecutors say a second suspect in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage investigation has been arrested in Croatia. Prosecutors have not published the suspect's identity or alleged role.
The Straits Times reports that Russia's 'pivot to Asia' is prioritising ties with isolated states over larger economies, as Moscow's options for trade and diplomacy narrow.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denies President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Pyongyang is deploying additional troops to support Russia. Kyiv has not withdrawn the claim.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine grind to a virtual halt, The Straits Times reports, after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.
A suspected sabotage attack fails to disrupt deliveries by Estonian defence manufacturer Milrem to Ukraine, according to the company. Investigators have not publicly attributed the attempt.

Protests in Kyiv back former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a wartime presidential election, Al Jazeera reports, turning his statement into the first visible street mobilisation on the question since 2022.
Russia and Ukraine each hand over 103 prisoners of war in an exchange, one of the few channels between the two sides still operating.

Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv, with a nine-storey residential block destroyed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital, a school and warehouses damaged. The toll was revised upward through the day from an initial five. Moscow has not commented on the toll.

Ukraine's air force says Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones overnight and that most cruise missiles and nearly 90% of the drones were downed, without specifying how many ballistic missiles were fired or intercepted. Officials say Kyiv is effectively defenceless against ballistic missiles because of an acute shortage of interceptors.
timeline.source: Ukrainian Air Force via BBC, NBC News

timeline.event: German prosecutors say a Ukrainian man has been arrested in Croatia over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage, the second arrest in the investigation. Prosecutors have not detailed his alleged role.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge yet to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Kremlin says the call shows splits in Kyiv.
Poland says it has arrested a man over an alleged plot to assassinate an official in Ukraine's arms industry. Warsaw has not named the suspect or the intended target.
Romania's defence minister says the country destroyed a marine drone near the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea. Bucharest has not attributed the drone to a party.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine remain at a virtual halt after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in the overnight attack on Kyiv, which struck blocks of flats and warehouses and damaged a children's hospital and a school. CNA's earlier count was 16. The figures are Ukrainian and have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Ukraine State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko tells the BBC that critical infrastructure was 'purposefully attacked' for the first time in several months, disrupting hot water supply in parts of the city.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine urgently needs more Patriot interceptors and that the shortage is costing lives.

A senior Russian diplomat says Moscow is ready to consider new ideas on a Ukraine peace settlement but only on its own conditions, repeating that any talks must recognise the 'new realities on the ground'.
Russia holds a rare missile test near the disputed islands north of Japan that Tokyo calls the Northern Territories.

Australia charges a 27-year-old Russian-Australian citizen with foreign interference, alleging he joined Ukraine's armed forces to gather information on their military activities for Russia. The allegations have not been tested in court.

Russia's FSB says nine people have been arrested for planned attacks and espionage on behalf of Ukraine, according to Russian state agencies. Kyiv has not commented and the claims are not independently verified.
A Ukrainian man wanted over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage is detained in Croatia, the second arrest in the German-led investigation.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, plans a trip to the United States to raise funding for his projects, The Straits Times reports - a sign his domestic challenge to Zelensky has shifted abroad after the wartime-election protests ended.

The BBC's Steve Rosenberg reports petrol shortages spreading in Russia as the cumulative effect of Ukrainian strikes on refineries and export infrastructure reaches ordinary consumers, though he finds little erosion of public support for the war.
Japan lodges a formal protest over Russia's missile test near the disputed Kuril Islands, held days ahead of an expected Putin visit.

Russian drones strike a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih, President Zelensky's home city, with a second drone hitting about half an hour after the first. Regional military head Oleksandr Hanzha says 16 people were killed and 130 injured, among them 23 children. Zelensky calls the two-wave attack 'cynical and despicable' and says the second strike targeted emergency workers at the scene; the BBC says it verified footage of the second drone hitting the already burning mall. Russia's military has not commented on the mall.
A separate Russian drone strike in the southern Mykolaiv region kills at least four people, three of them children, and wounds a woman, Ukrainian state media report.
The leaders of France, Britain and Germany announce they will co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday.

Russian state agencies report that nine people have been arrested on suspicion of planning attacks and conducting espionage on Ukraine's behalf. The claim comes from Russian authorities and has not been independently verified.
Russia designates the independent news outlet Mediazona a 'foreign agent'.

German authorities are investigating possible Russian links to a weapons cache discovered in woodland, according to reports cited by the BBC. The investigation is unconfirmed by German officials on the record.

Rescuers work through the night in the wreckage of the Kryvyi Rih shopping centre; Hanzha says the death toll reached 16 after another body was recovered overnight, with nine people reported still missing and 29 in a serious condition. Local officials say at least two more people were killed in further Russian strikes early on Saturday. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted transport infrastructure and warehouses.

Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia kill at least 10 people according to Russian regional officials and halt work at a warehouse of the online retailer Ozon in the Samara region. Russia's figures are not independently verified.

The death toll from Friday's double-tap drone strike on a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih rises to 16, with 130 injured and four people still missing, says Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha. Rescue work may run for two more days.
President Vladimir Putin says Ukraine has opened a 'Pandora's box' by striking economic targets and that Russia will hit back at Ukraine's 'most sensitive economic sectors'.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, visiting Ukraine, condemns what he calls Russia's escalating attacks on civilian areas.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says French President Emmanuel Macron agreed to accelerate deliveries of French air-defence equipment, after Kyiv said a shortage of interceptors was costing lives. Paris has not published a delivery schedule.

Norway's government says it will give Ukraine another 85 billion Norwegian crowns (about US$9.2 billion) in financial support in the 2027 fiscal year, matching its 2026 contribution and split between military and humanitarian spending. Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere announced it while visiting Kyiv with Nordic and Baltic leaders.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine believes Russia plans to draft an additional 300,000 troops after Russian parliamentary elections in mid-September, working towards 500,000 overall by 2027, and that Moscow is raising missile production to about 1,300 a year. These are Ukrainian assessments and have not been independently verified; the Kremlin has not confirmed them.

Zelensky rejects holding a wartime election, saying a vote during this kind of war would 'destroy' the country by splitting Ukrainians. It is his first response to ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a poll. Elections in war are prohibited by Ukrainian law and the country has been under martial law since 2022.

Sacked defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov tells the BBC that Zelensky should be asked what he knew about corruption in his government, following a money-laundering investigation announced last week, while saying he never saw the president act corruptly and never received an improper instruction from him. He repeats his call for a wartime vote.

Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store says Norway will give Ukraine US$9 billion (about S$11.4 billion) in 2027, matching this year's record level, with most of it going to the military. Baltic and Nordic leaders gather in Kyiv for a summit with President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Zelensky says Ukraine's army faces a US$27 billion deficit and urges the European Union to advance payments on part of a 90 billion euro loan, warning that without about US$10 billion by the end of the year his soldiers will not have enough weapons. He did not give a detailed breakdown.

Ozon reports a fire at its logistics hub in Russia's central Orenburg region after a drone attack and suspends warehouse operations, a day after an Ozon centre in the neighbouring Samara region was hit and an unspecified number of workers wounded.
A Russian attack on the outskirts of the north-eastern city of Kharkiv kills three people, the regional governor says on Telegram.

Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev says drone debris hit a private childcare centre overnight, killing two children and injuring nine people including seven children, and that debris fell on apartment buildings. The Russian account is not independently verified.

Ozon says a 'major fire' is burning at one of its logistics centres in the Krasnodar region after a drone attack, the second consecutive day one of its hubs has been hit. The company says staff were evacuated and there are preliminarily no casualties. Ukraine's defence ministry said on 22 Aug it was extending to Ozon a campaign that has already struck the 15 largest Wildberries logistics hubs.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ozon, Ukrainian defence ministry)

timeline.event: A drone attack on an industrial area in Nevinnomysk, a chemical production centre in the Stavropol region, is repelled, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov says on Telegram.
Zelensky says Ukraine was not behind the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline blasts and that Kyiv is cooperating with the German-led investigation, after two arrests in the case.

Kyiv hosts a meeting of the French- and British-led Coalition of the Willing to discuss stepping up support for Ukraine and pressure on Russia ahead of winter, as Ukraine marks 35 years of independence.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is due to urge US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to take a more active role on Ukraine, The Straits Times reports.
President Volodymyr Zelensky marks 35 years of Ukrainian independence, saying Ukraine wants peace but will not give in to Russian terms.
BBC reports that President Vladimir Putin said on Saturday Ukraine had opened 'Pandora's box' by striking economic targets and that Russia would hit back at Kyiv's most sensitive economic sectors.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says measures are being taken to minimise the impact of Ukrainian strikes on Russia's grain exports, telling reporters that 'all grain intended for export' will be shipped on time and in full. Tit-for-tat attacks on ports and vessels have shuttered grain terminals and forced dozens of cargoes to be delayed or cancelled in peak export season.

Zelensky says Russia is 'not ready' for a ceasefire limited to attacks on Black Sea ships carrying agricultural produce, because Moscow wants any deal extended to cover strikes on Russian refineries and pipelines.

Ukrainian drone strikes set fire to logistics centres belonging to Ozon, Russia's second-largest online retailer, in Krasnodar, Dagestan, Stavropol and Adygea. The BBC verified video of the attacks. Ozon said several people were injured; Russia's defence ministry said three children aged 13, 15 and 16 were killed in Krasnodar. Neither account has been independently verified. Ozon shares fell as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange and those of its main shareholder AFK Sistema by almost 13%.

Andy Burnham, on his first overseas trip as UK prime minister, met Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv and chaired his first meeting of the British- and French-led coalition of the willing. Britain agreed to hand over blueprints for UK-made components of the Scalp missile, the French version of the Storm Shadow cruise missile, so Ukraine can build the weapon domestically. Burnham urged the US Congress to 'ratchet up' economic pressure on Russia.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the British missile transfer prevented 'even the slightest progress' towards peace and that the Russian military was already gathering data to locate and destroy any Ukrainian missile production sites. Asked about the charge that Britain was adding fuel to the fire, Burnham replied: 'Who started the fire?'
Ukrainian strikes hit Russia's second-biggest online retailer, extending Kyiv's campaign against Russian commercial and logistics infrastructure.
Britain and Ukraine signed an artificial-intelligence defence partnership covering battlefield technology, extending the industrial cooperation announced during Burnham's visit.

President Vladimir Putin granted the Russian state the right to take control of infrastructure it judges inadequately protected against drone attacks, a response to Ukraine's deepening campaign against Russian economic targets.
Britain and France pledged stronger support as Ukraine marked 35 years of independence, with Burnham saying allies were digging into their own stocks of air defences to help protect Ukrainian skies.

Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev said the Afipsky oil refinery was on fire after a drone attack, and that two people were killed and two injured by falling drone debris at the Afipsky railway station. The account is from Russian regional officials and is not independently verified. The export-focused plant processed about 144,000 barrels a day in 2024, and follows the halt of the Perm refinery after a Ukrainian drone strike on 21 August.

Andrei Fedorov, an adviser to the Kremlin, told BBC Newsnight there might be a 'semi-military' response against UK drone factories by 'unknown sources' over Britain sharing blueprints for Scalp/Storm Shadow missile components. The remark is one adviser's and not a stated Russian government position.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, returning from Kyiv, said he will 'likely' travel to the United States next month with European leaders to lobby President Trump on Ukraine's defence needs, though he said the details were not fully confirmed. It would be his first US trip since taking office in July.

Archbishop Paul Gallagher, the Vatican's foreign minister, met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Moscow — the first in-person Vatican-Russia talks in five years. Gallagher said it was 'urgent and necessary' to end the war, and the two agreed to cooperate on humanitarian matters including children affected by the fighting.

A US Air Force Boeing C-17 Globemaster, tail number 07-7181, flew direct from Riga and landed at Moscow's Vnukovo airport at about 0700 GMT, per Flightradar24 data. It is the first direct flight of a US-registered jet to Russia from Europe since January. The Kremlin said it had no information on the plane; its cargo and passengers could not be verified.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine sees a window for US-led mediation until the end of next summer, and that a one-page set of ideas drafted with US and European officials — a ceasefire as the main point, plus a US-proposed free economic zone in Donbas administered by a third party — will be put to Moscow.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Finnish President Alexander Stubb's approval of Ukrainian long-range strikes inside Russia showed he belonged, alongside Britain's Andy Burnham, to the 'party of war', and accused Western leaders of misleading voters about Russia being strategically defeated.

German investigators found a third drone west of Leipzig/Halle Airport on 14 August, 10 days after the attempted attack, along with about 50g of a substance suspected to be the military explosive hexogen, according to NDR, WDR and the Sueddeutsche Zeitung. Security sources cited in the reports suspect Russian intelligence involvement; Moscow denies it. The prosecutor-general's office did not comment.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (NDR, WDR, Sueddeutsche Zeitung)

timeline.event: Sweden's military said it was seeking to take over a Russian-owned estate close to a Swedish naval base, citing security concerns.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that whoever was behind a drone incident over Germany would 'pay a price'. No party has been formally identified.
Slovak police said they had thwarted a planned arson attack on a drone factory.

German magazine Der Spiegel reported that a man detained over a Berlin gun stash is suspected of being part of a Russian network. The claim comes from the magazine's reporting and has not been confirmed by prosecutors.
Mykhailo Fedorov, recently ousted as defence minister, said Ukraine needs to change how it is fighting to avoid losing the war.

The United States asked Ukraine not to launch air strikes around Moscow, St Petersburg and some northern Russian territories on 24, 25 and 26 August, because a plane carrying a senior US official would be in the area.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe travelled to Moscow for meetings with Russian officials, CBS News and Axios reported citing unnamed sources — the first known Moscow visit by a US intelligence chief since William Burns met Vladimir Putin in November 2021. The CIA declined to comment; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov neither confirmed nor denied the visit and said Putin had no plans to meet Ratcliffe.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, CNA (CBS News, Axios)

timeline.event: Switzerland will hold a referendum next month on adopting a more restrictive form of neutrality that would bar it from imposing economic sanctions or cooperating with NATO in peacetime.

The BBC reports the CIA director's Moscow trip would be the first known visit by a US spy chief since 2021. The CIA declined to comment and the Kremlin said President Vladimir Putin had no plans to meet him.

The Kremlin said CIA director John Ratcliffe held talks with Russian intelligence counterparts during his Moscow visit, while stating that President Vladimir Putin did not meet him. Neither side described what was discussed.
A Wildberries warehouse in Russia's Tambov region was destroyed by fire after being hit by a drone, the regional governor said. Ukraine did not claim the strike.
The BBC reported that as Ukraine keeps striking Russian oil refineries, Russia has shifted to targeting Ukraine's fuel distribution network, including petrol stations.
Ukraine awarded Elon Musk a high state honour as Kyiv seeks to expand its use of Starlink.
The Kremlin said remarks by ousted Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov showed Kyiv was consumed by infighting. The characterisation is Moscow's; Kyiv has not responded.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that those behind a drone incident over German territory would 'pay a price'. Berlin has not publicly attributed the incident.

Ukraine's military named prominent commanders to lead the defence of the eastern region that Russia is demanding be ceded in any settlement, signalling it intends to hold the ground rather than trade it.

President Donald Trump described CIA director John Ratcliffe's unannounced Moscow trip as a 'semi-routine' mission and said 'something may come out of' it. Neither Washington nor Moscow has said what was discussed.
A US senator said he hoped a 'sledgehammer' package of Russian sanctions would pass Congress next month. The bill has not been scheduled for a vote.
A Pentagon official is to brief NATO allies as a US force-posture review raises questions among European members about the scale of the American commitment to the continent.
France's security chief said he sees new threats following the drone attack at Leipzig. No attribution for that incident has been made public by German or French authorities.

The Wall Street Journal and CBS News reported that CIA director John Ratcliffe used his Moscow visit to warn Russia against attacking NATO members, following US intelligence assessments that Moscow could seek to test the alliance. Neither the White House nor the Kremlin has confirmed the content of the talks.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (WSJ, CBS News)

timeline.event: US officials said the Pentagon's global posture review is preparing options on American troop levels in Europe for Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth by 6 November. No decision has been announced.

Russia launched a large overnight missile and drone attack on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities. Ukraine's air force said the barrage included two Oniks anti-ship cruise missiles, 258 drones and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles, and that nearly 90 per cent of the drones were downed along with one Oniks and seven ballistic missiles. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said ports, grain storage, energy and industrial infrastructure were targeted.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ukrainian Air Force, Ukrainian foreign ministry)

timeline.event: President Volodymyr Zelensky said European allies had made 'important decisions' this week to strengthen Ukrainian air defence and that Ukraine had recently received a small batch of Patriot interceptors, renewing his call for further packages. Kyiv has been short of the US-made interceptors capable of downing ballistic missiles.
Russia said it could strike British military targets in response to Ukraine's use of British-supplied missiles against Russian territory.
A senior aide to President Volodymyr Zelensky said talks between Ukraine and Russia may be possible in September.
Russia's foreign intelligence chief confirmed that he held talks with CIA director John Ratcliffe during the American's unannounced visit to Moscow. Neither government has said what was discussed.

US Defense Under Secretary Elbridge Colby, visiting NATO headquarters in Brussels, pressed European allies to set out how they are taking primary responsibility for the continent's conventional defence, as Washington's six-month review of its force posture in Europe continues.
Slovak prosecutors said suspects had planned an arson attack on Skyeton, a Ukrainian drone manufacturer.
Bulgaria will receive seven minehunter ships from Belgium and the Netherlands to help protect the Black Sea.
An EU official said there were no signs Russia is preparing a military attack on NATO countries, pushing back on warnings circulating in allied capitals.

The Netherlands, Poland, Spain and Sweden called for the European Union to reopen discussion next week on using Russia's frozen assets for Ukraine, arguing Moscow shows no sign of wanting to end the war. Belgium, which holds most of the assets, has previously blocked the idea.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Dutch, Polish, Spanish and Swedish governments)

timeline.event: Poland's deputy defence minister said Poland does not want nuclear warheads stationed on its territory.
A car bomb killed a Russian army officer outside Saint Petersburg, Russian media reported. No one has claimed responsibility and investigators have not publicly attributed the attack.

President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin will not attack NATO territory and played down reports that CIA director John Ratcliffe had warned Russian officials against doing so during his unannounced Moscow visit.
Authorities in Ukraine's Kherson told residents to leave the city, the strongest evacuation message from the regional administration in recent weeks.

Ukrainian courier company Nova Poshta said Russian attacks destroyed its sorting centres near Kyiv and in the northern city of Sumy. It said four guided aerial bombs hit the Sumy terminal and damaged three trucks, that all employees were unharmed, and that it continued to operate.
Sweden's military will help survey and protect Finnish territory with Gripen fighter jets and a corvette, at least until the end of 2026, Finland's defence forces said.
Countries bordering the Baltic Sea plan a joint task force for drone defence so they can react quickly to hybrid attacks, German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said in Flensburg.

The Straits Times reported, citing officials, that CIA director John Ratcliffe's 25 August trip to Moscow was an attempt to persuade the Russian leadership against fresh provocations in Europe. The account is single-sourced reporting and has not been confirmed by either government.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said the United States had passed Kyiv information about a number of meetings held in Moscow over the previous few days, following CIA director John Ratcliffe's trip to the Russian capital on 25 August.
Ukraine's top presidential adviser said technical talks on the war would likely take place in the near future, while cautioning that he did not expect a swift agreement.
Mykhailo Fedorov, dismissed as Ukraine's defence chief six weeks earlier, agreed to become adviser on defence innovation to Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto.

Ukrainian officials said Russian attacks across the country killed 16 people and injured 50 over the previous day, with strikes reported on a gas station in Kharkiv, a supermarket in Pavlohrad and warehouses in the Kyiv region. The tallies come from Ukrainian regional authorities and have not been independently verified; Russia's defence ministry says it targets military and military-linked infrastructure.

Zelensky said Ukraine's security service struck a Tu-95MS missile carrier at Engels airbase and that Ukrainian forces hit an oil refinery in Russia's Yaroslavl region. Both are Ukrainian claims; Moscow has not confirmed the damage.
Ukraine's military intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov said Ukraine needs to mobilise at least 30,000 people a month, and separately that ending the war now is unrealistic.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says the United States passed Kyiv information about a number of meetings held in Moscow over recent days, thanking Washington for the information and for "the necessary tone of the conversation with Russia", without saying who took part.

Western officials told the BBC that Russia is sharpening its rhetoric towards NATO but wants to avoid a direct war with the alliance, while remaining likely to continue hybrid activity against member states short of open military action.

Ukraine's Air Force said air defences neutralised 233 of 267 attack drones launched from the evening of 28 August, in a barrage that also included an Oniks anti-ship missile and an Iskander-M ballistic missile fired from occupied Crimea. The figures are Ukrainian military claims and have not been independently verified.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said after a Commander-in-Chief's Headquarters meeting that Ukraine's goal is 1,000 long-range strike drones a day against Russia, against an average of 300 or more now.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service said a Russian strike in the Odesa region killed one person and injured three, setting eight lorries carrying food on fire; an overnight attack on the Izmail district damaged transport infrastructure. Both accounts come from Ukrainian authorities.

Ukraine's General Staff reported 242 combat clashes along the front over the previous day, the largest number of them on the Pokrovsk axis. Russia's defence ministry gives its own, differing accounts of front-line activity.
The leaders of Russia, China and Iran are due to attend a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan, a bloc that presents itself as a counterweight to Western influence.

A Russian drone struck an enterprise in the town of Myla, in Kyiv region's Bucha district, at about 8.10pm on 28 August, causing a large fire and sustained detonations. Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachenko reported 27 dead and more than 40 wounded during the afternoon; Ukrinform reported the toll had risen to 37 by evening and the BBC reported hundreds of residents evacuated. Taras Didych, head of the Dmytrivka community, was among the dead. All figures are Ukrainian officials' and are not independently verified.

Ukraine's prosecutor general opened a criminal negligence investigation into the Myla site, saying it would examine the legality of storing explosive objects and materials on the enterprise's grounds and whether the company held the necessary permits. Officials did not describe the nature of the facility.
A mass drone attack caused a local blackout in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region, leaving about 300,000 customers without power, Ukrinform reported citing Ukrainian authorities.

Ukraine's Defence Forces said they struck launch sites used for Russian attack drones in Donetsk region and occupied Crimea, and separately that drones hit an Ozon logistics centre in Russia's Rostov region. Both are Ukrainian claims; Moscow has not confirmed the damage.
