A Russian strike sets a shopping centre alight in Zaporizhzhia, Al Jazeera reports, as attacks on Ukrainian cities continue through the day.

The Straits Times reports that Russia has adapted a training missile for combat use and is now leading its ballistic barrage of Ukraine with it, a sign of how Moscow is managing stocks of precision weapons.

The UN Human Rights Office reports 1,004 documented cases of sexual violence and torture against civilians and prisoners between February 2022 and the end of July 2026, attributing 89 per cent to Russian authorities - the armed forces, prison service and national security service - and 11 per cent to Ukrainian authorities. It calls on both governments to investigate and prosecute.
Ukraine launches a drone barrage into Russia as the State Duma election opens, Al Jazeera reports.

A decree signed by President Putin transfers the Russian operations of Nestle, Auchan, Lemana Pro (the former Leroy Merlin) and FM Logistic's Russian subsidiaries to LEV Management, a company Novaya Gazeta Europe says was created only at the end of 2025 and is headed by an interior ministry general. The Kremlin calls it a justified measure against firms from 'unfriendly countries'.

Denmark speeds up a Ukraine support package worth an estimated 1.8 billion Danish crowns after saying a Russian frigate fired flares without warning at a Danish military helicopter photographing the ship in international waters. Moscow accuses Denmark of dangerous manoeuvres near the vessel.

President Zelensky launches the 'Carpathian Eight', a new regional grouping with Romania, Serbia, Poland, Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Austria, Hungary and the EU, at a summit in western Ukraine attended by Poland's Donald Tusk, Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic and Romania's Nicusor Dan.
Poland joins an anti-ballistic missile coalition with Ukraine.
The International Committee of the Red Cross says it has had no access to Ukrainian prisoners of war for two years.
A Russian glide bomb hits an apartment building in the northern city of Sumy, killing two people and injuring seven, three of them seriously, President Volodymyr Zelensky and local officials say.
The IAEA says it was informed that a drone hit the cooling tower of a reactor unit at Russia's Kursk nuclear power plant the previous day.
Russia labels Cannes-winning film director Andrey Zvyagintsev a 'foreign agent'.

President Emmanuel Macron says Russian hybrid attacks on Europe are intensifying, warns that attacks on France will not go unanswered, and orders stronger protection for critical infrastructure and defence-industry sites.
President Donald Trump signs the sweeping Russia sanctions bill into law, the White House says, clearing the way for greater economic pressure on Moscow.
Germany takes delivery of its first F-35 fighter from the United States as NATO members raise military spending.
A top NATO commander joins a briefing on the review of US defence engagement in Europe, as allies wait to learn how far Washington will draw down.
Sources tell The Straits Times that an envoy of President Vladimir Putin and Germany's far-right AfD are preparing talks aimed at restoring Russian gas supplies to Germany.
Al Jazeera reports that Russian drones are threatening the routes used by Western officials travelling to Kyiv, as Moscow's broader war effort stalls.
A Russian attack kills two people in Balakliia in eastern Ukraine, local officials say.
Kyiv comes under Russian missile attack, the city's mayor says. The BBC reports that Russia's shift to short-warning missile tactics leaves residents about four minutes to reach shelter.
President Putin says Ukraine is interfering in Russia's parliamentary election, which is in its second day of voting.
The United States clears the way for a possible US$2.7 billion sale of air-defence development upgrades to Ukraine, hours after President Trump signed the Russia sanctions bill into law.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia attacked overnight with 174 drones launched from Russia and occupied Crimea plus two Zircon antiship missiles fired from the Kursk region, and that air defences intercepted or jammed 141 incoming targets, with downings in 15 locations and debris falling in nine. It says the Zircon missiles did not reach their targets.

Russian attacks across 14 settlements in the Kharkiv region kill five people and injure 15, with heavy destruction in Balakliya and Lypkuvativka, Governor Oleh Syniehubov says; shelling across 25 communities in the Kherson region kills three and injures five, damaging apartment blocks, a cell tower and a gas pipeline, Governor Oleksandr Prokudin says.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Kharkiv and Kherson regional governors)

timeline.event: Russia's defence ministry claims its forces used Geran-4 loitering drones to strike two commercial vessels in the Black Sea - a Ukrainian dry cargo ship bound for Odesa and a tanker docked at the port - asserting both carried military supplies. The claim has not been independently verified.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Russian defence ministry claim, not independently verified)

timeline.event: Russia reports online attacks on its electoral system on the second day of parliamentary voting, and the election triggers a row with Moldova over polling arranged for the separatist Transnistria region.

Ukraine's General Staff reports 188 combat clashes along the front line on Sept 19, with Russian forces most active in the Kostiantynivka sector; it says the day brought one missile strike, 64 air strikes using 199 guided aerial bombs and 6,084 attack drones. The figures are Ukrainian military claims and are not independently verified.
A Russian FPV drone strikes a car in the Sumy region, killing four civilians, Ukrainian officials say.
Denmark announces its 31st military aid package for Ukraine, worth about US$275 million and focused on air defence ahead of winter, Ukraine's defence ministry says.
A Russian strike on a shopping mall in Dnipro injures five people, the head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional military administration says, with the count rising through the evening from an initial two.

A mother and her two young children are killed in a Russian drone attack in the Fastiv district of the Kyiv region, the head of the Kyiv regional military administration, Timur Tkachenko, says on Telegram; homes and a car were damaged and a fire broke out. Separately, a woman and a child were injured in the region's Vyshhorod district. The casualty reports come from Ukrainian officials and are not independently verified.

Kyiv regional authorities raise the death toll from the overnight Russian drone attack to four, three of them children: a mother and her two three-year-olds killed in a private home, and a girl who died in hospital after a separate strike. Governor Tymur Tkachenko says 31 sites were damaged in five districts over more than a day of attacks, 24 of them in Fastiv district. The figures come from Ukrainian officials and are not independently verified.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 138 Shahed-type, Gerbera and decoy drones from 6pm on Sept 19 and that 101 had been shot down or suppressed by 8am, with hits recorded at 17 locations - a Ukrainian military claim, not independently verified.

Ukraine's General Staff reports 234 combat clashes over the past day, heaviest in the Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk sectors, and claims Russian forces carried out 98 airstrikes with 313 guided aerial bombs and used 10,856 kamikaze drones - Ukrainian military figures that are not independently verified.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine)

timeline.event: The head of the Kherson regional military administration says a Russian FPV drone struck a monastery in Chervonyi Maiak at about 3pm on Sept 19, killing a 71-year-old priest and injuring four others. The report comes from Ukrainian officials and is not independently verified.

Russian officials report one of the largest Ukrainian drone attacks of the war on the Moscow region. Governor Andrei Vorobyev says two people were killed and six injured and that 249 drones were shot down over the region; Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin says more than 1,600 drones were downed since Sept 19, 450 of them headed for the capital, that drones reached an oil refinery and one hit an apartment, and that the attack was meant to disrupt the election. Flight restrictions were imposed at Moscow airports. The tallies are Russian official claims and are not independently verified; Ukraine has not commented. Both sides have continued hitting energy infrastructure despite President Trump's Sept 14 announcement that they had agreed to stop.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Russian regional and city officials)

timeline.event: Russia's three-day State Duma election, the first since the 2022 invasion and cast by President Putin as a test of support for the war, enters its final day with United Russia expected to retain its dominance; most anti-war candidates were barred from the ballot.

President Zelensky confirms Ukraine's overnight long-range strikes on the Moscow region, saying 'one of Russia's key oil industry facilities' and a logistics site were hit and listing the domestically made drones and missiles used. He says de-escalation steps in energy remain on the table. The damage claims are Ukrainian statements and are not independently verified.

Zelensky says Russia launched more than 2,000 attack drones, 1,700 guided aerial bombs and 19 missiles at Ukraine over the past week, hitting infrastructure in the Kharkiv, Sumy and Odesa regions and homes in the Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions - Ukrainian figures, not independently verified.

Sumy regional police say a Russian FPV drone hit a civilian vehicle in the Sviesa community, killing two men and two women, among 47 strikes on 18 settlements in the region over the past day. The report comes from Ukrainian officials and is not independently verified.

Ukraine's Third Army Corps claims it has retaken the villages of Shandryholove and Derylove in the Donetsk region, and says its 'Vivaldi' operation has returned 125 square kilometres to Ukrainian control. The claim, including the Russian losses the corps cites, is not independently verified and Russia has not commented.

The head of the Proliska humanitarian mission says a Russian aerial bomb scored a direct hit on an evacuation point in Kramatorsk while evacuees and workers were on site. The account is from a Ukrainian aid organisation and is not independently verified.

Kramatorsk city council says three Russian artillery shells hit the Lazurnyi neighbourhood at 10:10, killing a woman and injuring a man and damaging a school and apartment blocks; Ukraine's emergency service later says two aerial bombs dropped on a residential area injured two more people and set fire to an educational building. Both accounts are from Ukrainian officials and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Kramatorsk city council, State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: Russia's defence ministry vows to 'continue and intensify' strikes on what it calls military targets in Kyiv in response to the drone attack on the Moscow region, accusing Ukraine of trying to disrupt Russia's parliamentary election. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says some 1,600 drones were involved, 450 aimed at the capital - a Russian claim that is not independently verified. A state-run exit poll puts the ruling United Russia party on 49.4 per cent.

Zelensky says he has spoken with Trump and that the two agreed to meet in New York during the UN General Assembly, a meeting he says 'could change a lot'; he speaks of 'diplomatic momentum' and ideas for de-escalation steps and security guarantees.

Evening Russian drone attacks: the Sumy regional administration says two drones struck near an apartment building in Sumy, killing a woman and wounding her 41-year-old husband; the Kyiv regional administration reports warehouse and industrial fires in the Boryspil, Fastiv, Bucha and Obukhiv districts with one man lightly injured; Dnipropetrovsk officials report five injured in more than 50 drone and artillery attacks on the Nikopol area. All are Ukrainian official accounts, not independently verified.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Sumy, Kyiv and Dnipropetrovsk regional administrations)

timeline.event: Early returns from Russia's first parliamentary election since the full-scale invasion put United Russia on nearly 58 per cent of the party-list vote with about 58 per cent of precincts counted, according to the Central Election Commission; the vote, described by Al Jazeera as tightly controlled, was also held in occupied parts of Ukraine. Russian officials say Ukrainian drones killed at least three people in the Moscow region and two in Russian-held Kherson region on Sept 20 (Russian claims).

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 172 strike drones and decoys from 18:00 on Sept 20, 64 of them jet-powered Shahed types, and that 147 drones and one Banderol/Dan-T were shot down or suppressed by 08:00, with hits at 14 locations. The Zaporizhzhia regional administration says five people were injured when high-rise buildings and a shopping centre were struck; fires were reported in two districts of Kyiv region, and the National Police put the Sumy region's toll for the past day at two killed and three injured. Ukrainian claims, not independently verified.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian Air Force; Zaporizhzhia regional administration; National Police)

timeline.event: Ukraine's General Staff reports 238 combat clashes over the past day, the heaviest on the Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk axes, along with 91 Russian airstrikes using 295 guided bombs. These are Ukrainian military figures and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine)

timeline.event: Russia's Central Election Commission chief Ella Pamfilova says preliminary results give United Russia 355 of the Duma's 450 seats, above its previous record of 343; near-complete returns put the party on 57.83 per cent of the party-list vote with turnout given as 59.3 per cent. No party critical of the war was on the national ballot. The Kremlin is expected to present the result as public backing for the war.

The UN Special Rapporteur on human rights in Russia tells the Human Rights Council that Moscow has intensified surveillance, intimidation and reprisals against critics abroad since the 2022 invasion, including attempted assassinations and poisonings.

Ukraine's General Staff reports 197 combat clashes by 22:00 on Sept 21, with 50 Russian airstrikes dropping 168 guided bombs and 6,137 kamikaze drones used; 23 attacks were repelled in the Pokrovsk sector (Ukrainian claim, not independently verified).
timeline.source: Ukrinform (General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine)

timeline.event: Regional officials say Russian strikes killed at least five civilians across Ukraine on Sept 21: one in Lozova in Kharkiv region, a driver in Nikopol, one in Kramatorsk and one in a nearby village, and a three-year-old child in Mykolaiv region. Both sides deny targeting civilians and the reports are not independently verified.

The Moscow Oil Refinery has halted operations after both primary processing units caught fire in the Sept 20 drone attack, with repairs expected to take weeks, according to industry sources cited by Ukrinform; Moscow's mayor had confirmed damage to an industrial facility. Refinery output has not been offered on the St Petersburg exchange since Sept 21.

The Kremlin acknowledges 'critical problems' with food and medicine in Russian-held Oleshky in Kherson region and says its military is working to resolve them; Ukraine's foreign minister says 6,000 residents including 200 children are 'dying from hunger and cold' and that Kyiv will raise the town at the UN General Assembly.

UN investigators warn that escalating long-range strikes on infrastructure by both Russia and Ukraine leave civilians increasingly vulnerable as winter approaches, citing last winter's power outages and cold-related deaths; neither side has agreed to an energy truce.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UN Commission of Inquiry)

timeline.event: Turkey has submitted proposals to both Ukraine and Russia aimed at halting attacks in the Black Sea, Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan says.
Zelensky met CIA director John Ratcliffe at Shannon Airport in Ireland on his way to the UN General Assembly, two people familiar with the matter said, without disclosing what was discussed.

After meeting Trump in New York, Macron says they discussed initiatives for a moratorium on energy-sector attacks between Ukraine and Russia and agreed on the need to get Kyiv more interceptors quickly; no agreement was announced.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia attacked overnight from 6pm with 212 Shahed and decoy drones, four Kalibr cruise missiles, eight Banderol missiles and Oniks and ballistic missiles, mainly at the Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad and Poltava regions; it reports 186 targets shot down or suppressed (one Kalibr, eight Banderols, 177 drones) and hits at 22 locations (Ukrainian claim).

The overnight strikes hit industrial enterprises in Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad, killing three people and injuring six in Dnipro, governor Oleksandr Hanzha says, with a worker still missing; a distributor says an attack on an energy facility left nearly 100,000 consumers in the Chernihiv region without power (Ukrainian officials, not independently verified).
timeline.source: The Straits Times, Ukrinform (Ukrainian regional officials)

timeline.event: Ukraine's General Staff counts 248 clashes in the 24 hours to 8am, the most, 33, in the Pokrovsk sector, and says Russia carried out 87 airstrikes with 305 guided bombs and launched 9,647 kamikaze drones (Ukrainian claim).
Poland scrambles military aircraft and puts ground-based air defences and radar on readiness during the overnight Russian strikes, its Operational Command says, calling the measures preventive.

Zelensky meets Macron in New York on the evening of Sept 21, after which Macron says France will 'join forces to secure a moratorium on attacks on Ukraine's energy and civilian infrastructure'; Zelensky is due to meet Trump on Sept 22 to press for an energy truce, saying Ukraine's energy, infrastructure and food exports must stop being targets. Russia has not signalled it wants a pause.

Ukraine's General Staff confirms strikes on Sept 21 and overnight on the Bashneft-UNPZ refinery in Ufa (about 7.5 million tonnes a year, fire reported) and the Kuibyshev refinery in Samara; Samara's governor says Ukrainian drones killed one person and wounded four in civilian areas and the city's mayor says a 'massive' attack was repelled (each side's claims, not independently verified).
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian General Staff), The Straits Times (Russian regional officials)

timeline.event: Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi says 13 regions and Kyiv came under drone and missile attack overnight and in the morning, with businesses, farms, warehouses, railways, energy sites and homes targeted, and puts the Dnipro toll at four killed and six injured; Naftogaz says at least five ballistic missiles hit a long-idle facility in the Poltava region, causing damage it calls irreparable (Ukrainian accounts).

Pipe maker Interpipe says four of its employees were killed and seven injured in the overnight ballistic-missile strike on its Dnipro plant, that main production equipment was damaged and that production is suspended.

After meeting Zelensky in New York, Macron says France is strengthening Ukraine's air defence by signing a contract for radars and providing interceptor missiles, without giving numbers or a timeline, and warns Russian strikes on energy infrastructure threaten to leave millions without heat this winter.

Ukraine's General Staff reports 134 combat engagements by 22:00, one missile strike, 53 airstrikes with 191 guided bombs and 5,378 kamikaze drones used, with most fighting on the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka axes; a Joint Forces spokesman confirms gains near Zapadne as Ukraine reduces the Russian bridgehead on the right bank of the Oskil (Ukrainian claims).
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian General Staff, Joint Forces Grouping)

timeline.event: Russian jet-powered drones hit warehouses in the Odesa region, killing one person and injuring two, the regional governor says; a strike on Zaporizhzhia sets a shopping centre on fire (Ukrainian officials' accounts).

EU states agree to delist Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman while extending sanctions on nearly 3,000 others for three years; Foreign Minister Sybiha says 'Moscow is celebrating because it got what it wanted' and Zelensky says sanctions relief cannot be discussed while Russia, which he says intelligence shows is preparing a 'new massive attack', keeps striking.

After meeting Trump in New York, Zelensky says Washington made no request for Ukraine to halt refinery strikes unilaterally and that Kyiv will agree to an energy ceasefire if Russia stops attacking all energy infrastructure; Trump says the refinery strikes are 'causing significant damage to Russia' and raising diesel prices, and predicts a peace agreement soon. At the UN, Macron says Ukraine needs more interceptor missiles before winter.

Ukraine's General Staff reports 247 combat engagements in the past day as of 08:00, one missile strike, 87 airstrikes with 309 guided bombs, 9,377 kamikaze drones and 2,693 shelling attacks, with the fiercest fighting on the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka axes (Ukrainian claims).

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 161 Shahed-type drones, 82 of them jet-powered, plus decoys and Banderol drones overnight and that 119 drones and three Banderols were shot down or suppressed, with hits at 18 locations; the Kyiv regional administration reports three people injured and 18 facilities damaged in Bucha district, and a strike on an enterprise in Poltava district caused a fire with no casualties (Ukrainian officials' accounts).
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian Air Force, Kyiv Regional State Administration, State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: A Russian strike on an Antigua and Barbuda-flagged cargo ship in the Black Sea overnight kills its Ukrainian captain and sets the vessel on fire; the crew is evacuated by the Ukrainian Navy, the Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority says, days after a Tanzanian-flagged ship bound for a Ukrainian port was attacked with its captain killed (Ukrainian account).

Unmanned Systems Forces commander Robert Brovdi says his units hit 38 more Russian energy facilities, including gas distribution stations in Crimea and substations in occupied Donetsk, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia, bringing the total disabled since July 6 to 412 (Ukrainian claim, not independently verified).

The State Department says Rubio will meet Lavrov in New York on the morning of Sept 23; Lavrov said last week Russia will not stop fighting while talks take place. Zelensky, after meeting UK Prime Minister Burnham, says lifting sanctions is 'out of the question' while Ukrainians live under daily strikes and thanks the UK for a new energy-sector contribution.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters), Ukrinform (Office of the President)

timeline.event: Russian drones hit railway infrastructure, warehouses and petrol stations across Kyiv on the morning of Sept 23, hours after the Zelensky-Trump meeting; city authorities say two people were killed and 22 injured, 16 of them in hospital, in one of the heaviest strikes on the capital since the summer. Ukrenergo reports new outages in the Kharkiv, Sumy, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Kyiv regions, and a shopping centre in Odesa district burns after a separate strike with no injuries (Ukrainian officials' accounts).
timeline.source: CNA (Reuters), Ukrinform (Kyiv Mayor Klitschko, Ukrenergo, Odesa emergency service)

timeline.event: Ukraine's General Staff says it struck Russian UAV command posts near Novoselivka Persha and Dachne and a 'Rubicon' unit drone depot near Volnovakha in Donetsk region overnight; Russian media and an OSINT analyst report drones over Ufa in Bashkortostan with smoke near the Ufa oil refinery, not confirmed by either side (Ukrainian claim; Ufa report unverified). Air Force spokesman Ihnat says Russia's use of jet-powered drones has risen eightfold in three months, to about 7,700 launched in total.

A Russian Mi-8 military helicopter enters Polish airspace from Kaliningrad for 42 seconds to a depth of about 300 metres, the Polish Army Operational Command says; fighters are scrambled and the command calls it a test of NATO air-defence readiness.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters), Polish Army Operational Command

timeline.event: Hours before the Rubio-Lavrov meeting in New York, Kremlin spokesman Peskov says there are 'still no prerequisites for moving to a peace track' though Russia remains open to a diplomatic settlement, and accuses European states of funding more weapons for Kyiv.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters), Ukrinform (The Moscow Times)

timeline.event: Kyiv's final count for the Sept 23 daytime attack rises to two killed and 45 injured, Klitschko says; the digital ministry says internet to about 100,000 households was cut, and Russia's defence ministry says it struck data centres and logistics sites it claims served the military. ST (AFP) counts at least seven killed across Ukraine that day as Lavrov tells the Security Council there will be no 'pause'.

A Russian attack drone hits a civilian vessel in the Black Sea after it leaves a Ukrainian port, killing the captain of a 16-strong crew; border guards evacuate 15. Russian glide bombs injure seven in Sumy and an Uragan MLRS strike injures nine in Kramatorsk, regional officials say.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (State Border Guard Service, Sumy administration)

timeline.event: Zelensky tells the Crimea Platform Ukraine is ready for a Black Sea maritime truce on options from Egypt, India and Turkey and that Russia must now respond; at the General Assembly he calls it 'Putin's crazy war' and urges sustained pressure on Russian revenues. Sybiha tells the Security Council Ukraine is ready for a full ceasefire 'now'. Kyiv signs a drone deal with Finland.
timeline.source: CNA (Reuters), Al Jazeera, Ukrinform, The Straits Times (Reuters)

timeline.event: After meeting Lavrov in New York, Rubio says Trump has invited Putin to the December G20 summit in Miami because 'you have to meet with the people that you disagree with'.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, Al Jazeera (AFP, Reuters)

timeline.event: UN political chief Rosemary DiCarlo tells the Security Council more civilians were killed or injured in Ukraine in the first eight months of 2026 than in all of 2025, with OHCHR confirming at least 17,257 civilians killed since February 2022. The ICRC confirms it has had no access to PoWs held in Russia since 2024.

Zelensky tells reporters in New York that the December G20 in Miami could host a trilateral Ukraine-US-Russia meeting and that Kyiv has discussed the format with Washington, calling Trump's participation the key factor.

Russian ballistic missiles strike Kyiv after 1am; Klitschko says two people are killed, one in the car park of a maternity hospital whose facade is damaged, and three medical staff injured as debris falls on three districts.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched Zircon and Iskander/KN-23 ballistic missiles and 282 drones from 18:00 on Sept 23, mainly at Odesa and Kyiv regions, and that 227 targets were downed or suppressed by 08:00, with hits at 13 locations. Kyiv's final toll: two killed and eight injured, including a police officer.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian Air Force, Kyiv city authorities)

timeline.event: Odesa governor Oleh Kiper says a Russian attack damages a hospital roof, a gymnasium, a shopping centre, food warehouses and homes in the region, injuring two.

Erdogan tells Zelensky that Russian and Ukrainian attacks on commercial ships in the Black Sea are 'inexplicable' and must stop, and says Turkey will keep trying to revive direct talks, according to his office's readout.

Kharkiv governor Oleh Syniehubov says a Russian attack on a farm in Stara Hnylytsia kills at least six and injures 12; Ukrinform's later headline gives seven dead. Al Jazeera counts at least eight killed across Ukraine on the day, including two in Kyiv.
Ukraine's General Staff reports 277 combat engagements over the past day and says Russia used 287 guided bombs and 7,467 kamikaze drones; these are Ukrainian military figures.
Russia's Krasnodar governor declares a regional state of emergency because Ukrainian drone attacks are slowing grain exports.

Polish Deputy PM Krzysztof Gawkowski says a fire at a Starlink ground station was sabotage meant to disrupt internet access, including for the Ukrainian army, and fits a 'new Russian doctrine of attack'; the Kremlin does not comment. Denmark's intelligence service says Russia will likely escalate hybrid warfare in the coming months.
Moldovan police say a drone that crashed and exploded on Moldovan territory has been identified as a Russian Gerbera, the first of the type found in the country.

Zelensky says in New York that Ukraine has agreed a new package of Patriot missiles with an unnamed partner and signed a security agreement with Australia; the EU Council approves nearly EUR3 billion in Ukraine Facility aid.
Polish PM Donald Tusk warns that inviting Putin to the Miami G20 may encourage Russian aggression; the Kremlin says no decision has been taken on a December Putin-Trump summit.

Russia's Defence Ministry says overnight strikes hit drone-production facilities in Kyiv, two military telecoms centres, logistics hubs at Odesa port and an oil tanker bound for Chornomorsk, followed by daytime strikes on a drone warehouse in Novi Biliari and a cargo vessel bound for Odesa. Russian claims, not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Russian Defence Ministry via Reuters)

timeline.event: NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe Alexus Grynkewich says the alliance is stepping up intelligence-sharing after a wave of sabotage incidents apparently linked to Russia, as Denmark's defence intelligence service warns of a 'low but growing risk' that Moscow could launch a limited military attack on one or more NATO border states.

The European Defence Agency's first Defence Readiness Report, seen by Reuters, says EU members' plans 'do not seem to meet' the goal of being ready to defend against Russia by 2030, citing gaps in air and missile defence, munitions and drones.

Finnish President Alexander Stubb says he pleaded with Elon Musk to extend Starlink coverage over occupied Ukraine and Russian territory so Kyiv can strike the ballistic-missile launchers it cannot intercept for lack of air defences.

Zelensky meets more than two dozen US companies in New York, in a session facilitated by Citigroup and the US Chamber of Commerce, on winter energy support, a sovereign wealth fund and reconstruction; Kyiv says the war now costs about US$190 million a day.

A Russian drone hits a 16-storey residential building in Kyiv's Pechersk district, killing a 14-year-old boy and injuring at least seven, police say; one person is killed in Odesa region. Russia denies targeting civilians.
Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 295 strike drones overnight, 52 of them jet-powered, and that 267 were shot down or suppressed, with hits at 16 locations (Ukrainian claim).

Ukrainian drones hit southern Russia overnight: Rostov's governor says the Novoshakhtinsk refinery was damaged and suspended operations; Ulyanovsk reports eight injured, Belgorod one killed, and Voronezh says 88 drones were downed (Russian regional claims).
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters), Ukrinform (Russian regional governors)

timeline.event: Russian drones strike Zaporizhzhia in the morning, setting a medical centre on fire and injuring one person, the regional defence council says.

Ukraine's General Staff reports 236 clashes over the past day, with Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka the hottest sectors, and says Russia used one missile, 80 air strikes and 296 guided bombs (Ukrainian claim).

Macron tells TF1 and France 2 that intelligence points to Russia possibly raising 300,000 additional troops after its Duma elections, and that Russian drones could target sites in France because Moscow treats Europe as Ukraine's 'strategic rear'.

Kyiv's mayor says the number injured in the morning drone attacks rose to 20, with a 14-year-old killed; the High Council of Justice building in Shevchenkivskyi district was also damaged (Ukrainian officials).
Odesa prosecutors say the Russian attack on the region killed a 40-year-old woman and a 51-year-old man and injured two others, one in serious condition.

Zelensky says Ukraine's overnight 'long-range sanctions' hit refineries in Perm and Novoshakhtinsk, the Iskra defence plant in Ulyanovsk and two radar stations in Rostov region; the General Staff lists three missile-related enterprises struck (Ukrainian claim; Rostov's governor confirms the refinery suspended operations).
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Zelensky, Ukrainian General Staff), The Straits Times (Reuters)

timeline.event: Zelensky says Trump told him he has made a 'final decision' to grant Ukraine licences to produce Patriot missiles, after repeated reversals; Kyiv is short of the interceptors.
The US proposes technical-level three-way talks with Ukraine and Russia, suggesting the UAE as venue; Zelensky says a date is awaited and Al Jazeera reports Moscow has also confirmed the plan.

Russia's election commission confirms 46 veterans of the Ukraine war won Duma seats, more than 10 per cent of the chamber; the Kremlin calls it 'excellent'. Finland and Sweden fly their first joint intercept of Russian aircraft over the Gulf of Finland.
Ukraine's foreign minister Andrii Sybiha tells Ukrinform there are 'no obstacles on Ukraine's side' to trilateral talks with the US and Russia, including at leaders' level.
EU member states agree terms to release €6.6 billion in European Peace Facility funds for Ukraine, including €900 million for the EUMAM training mission, Kaja Kallas says.

Russia's defence ministry says its overnight drone strikes hit a drone assembly and storage site in Kyiv region, logistics hubs in Odesa region and port infrastructure at Reni; Moscow's claim is not independently verified.
Israel's foreign ministry condemns the Kyiv attack, in which a 14-year-old Israeli citizen was killed and his mother injured.

Putin says all settlement proposals remain on the table but Moscow must weigh its interests, and claims Russia was ready to resume talks after the Duma elections until Ukraine attacked Moscow and polling stations.
Kyiv's toll from the Sept 25 drone attacks rises to seven killed and 57 injured, including two children, after a strike on an office building in the Solomianskyi district, mayor Klitschko says.
Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 162 attack drones in daylight on Sept 25, 76 of them jet-powered, and that 127 were shot down or suppressed with hits recorded at 27 locations.
Trump again urges Zelensky to travel to Moscow to meet Putin, ST reports; Zelensky declines, as he has before.
Zelensky says Russia has widened its attacks to data centres and internet providers to disrupt ordinary life; a Friday drone strike on a Kyiv business centre damaged a data centre.
Ukraine's Air Force says Russia attacked overnight from 18:00 on Sept 25 with 173 Shahed-type drones, more than 50 of them jet-powered, plus decoys, and that 134 were neutralised.

A drone strikes between a five-storey residential block and a shop in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district, starting a fire from which 20 people are rescued, and an office building in the same district catches fire, the city military administration says; injuries are reported.
In Kyiv region a warehouse fire in Boryspil district injures two people, one hospitalised, and a home in Obukhiv district is damaged, the State Emergency Service says.
Sumy regional administration reports one civilian killed and 13 injured over the past day, nine of them, including a baby and two children, by a guided bomb on the Sumy community.
Ukraine's General Staff logs 205 combat engagements over the past day as of 08:00, with 79 Russian airstrikes and 277 guided bombs; the figures are Kyiv's and not independently verified.

The Trump administration has legally committed to spend nearly all of the US$400 million Congress approved for Ukraine aid, pledging the remaining US$93 million by the fiscal year end, Ukrinform reports citing Reuters sources.

Sumy regional administration says Russian guided bombs (KABs) on the city's Kovpakivsky district kill two people and injure at least three, including a child, after the morning's tally of one dead and 13 injured over the previous day

Kyiv region's injury toll from the overnight drone attack rises to five, including two children in Obukhiv district, the regional administration says; the Darnytsia pharmaceutical plant in Kyiv is struck again with no injuries, three days after a previous hit

Lukoil's Perm refinery, which processed about 252,000 barrels a day in 2024, halts operations after a drone attack, Reuters reports citing two industry sources; OSINT outlet Astra says the Ilsky refinery in Krasnodar Krai caught fire after an overnight strike - both are unconfirmed by Russia
Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck a P-18 'Terek' radar station near Semenivka in Donetsk region and a Russian ammunition depot on Sept 25-26 (Ukrainian claim, not independently verified)

Zelensky says 14 people were injured and two killed in Zaporizhzhia in Russian attacks overnight, with strikes on homes in Kyiv and four regions, and calls on partners to choose 'stronger responses' and tighter sanctions

Russian guided-bomb strikes on Sumy kill two people and injure 23, including four children, damaging dozens of apartment blocks, two preschools and a cultural building, the regional military administration says.
A Russian airstrike on Synelnykove district kills a 17-year-old girl and a 59-year-old woman and injures two others including a six-year-old boy, the Dnipropetrovsk regional head says.
Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko says seven people were injured in the capital over the day's attacks, four of them in a Solomyanskyi apartment fire after a drone crash.

Lavrov and Germany's Wadephul hold the first Russian-German foreign-minister talks since 2022 on the UN sidelines; Berlin presses for a Black Sea grain-export deal while Lavrov tells the Assembly the war will continue 'through to the end'.

Ukraine's military intelligence says the 'Freedom of Russia' Legion's underground network sabotaged rail tank-car oil shipments inside Russia in 'Operation Barrel', claiming over US$10 million in damage; not independently verified.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 170 Shahed-type drones (76 of them jet-powered) plus Gerbera and decoy drones from 18:00 on Sept 26; air defences shot down or suppressed 147 by 07:30, with hits at 18 locations and debris at eight.
A man is found dead after a Russian drone strike sets a non-residential building alight in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district; a second strike burns a service station, the State Emergency Service says.

A Russian strike on a car driving through a village in Zaporizhzhia region kills two people, the acting regional administration head says; a separate strike on Komyshuvakha kills one and injures four.
Russian air attack on Kiliia in Odesa region hits port and civilian infrastructure overnight; the fire is extinguished, the Izmail district administration says.

Zelensky says Russia struck a data centre in Kyiv twice on Sunday morning, injuring three people including two children in the first strike, and that overnight shelling killed three in Zaporizhzhia region and a drone strike one in Kyiv; he puts the week's Russian launches at more than 2,200 attack drones, about 1,650 aerial bombs and 38 missiles. Ukrainian figures are not independently verified.

Kharkiv's governor Oleh Syniehubov says the city and 21 settlements came under attack in 24 hours, killing two people and injuring eight; a Russian strike in Odesa region set off a large fire at a production facility, killing one and injuring two, the regional emergency service says.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Kharkiv regional administration, State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces hit a facility used to store and launch attack drones in Donetsk city and two ammunition depots, a logistics depot and a fuel depot in Luhansk region; the claim is not independently verified.

Russian strikes kill eight people across Ukraine on Sunday, Ukrainian officials say: three at a children's centre in Sumy including a 16-year-old girl, three in Zaporizhzhia region overnight, one in a drone strike on Kyiv and, separately, two in Sofiivska Borshchahivka in Kyiv region; Kyivstar says its head office was hit with no casualties. Russia's defence ministry says it struck logistics hubs, communications centres and vessels linked to the military. Ukrainian figures are not independently verified.
timeline.source: CNA (AFP), The Straits Times (Reuters), Ukrinform (Kyiv regional administration)

timeline.event: Zelensky says Russia launched 277 attack drones since Saturday, 155 of them jet-powered, and that in Kyiv alone they hit two kindergartens, two schools, a residential building and communications facilities; Ukraine's digital ministry says strikes on data centres over the past week cut service to about 100,000 households around Kyiv. Not independently verified.

Ukraine's 40th Marine Brigade says it cleared five square kilometres of Russian forces in the Pokrovsk sector and took two prisoners; presidential office head Kyrylo Budanov says Ukraine critically needs Patriot missiles and expanded Starlink/Starshield access to strike Russian missile systems. Claims are Ukrainian and unverified.

South Korea demands an official explanation and apology from Ukraine, accusing Kyiv of disclosing the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul and then falsely denying that a confidentiality agreement existed; Seoul says it is reviewing further measures.

A Russian guided aerial bomb 'double strike' hits Kharkiv's Saltivskyi district overnight, injuring 24 people including eight children by regional governor Oleh Syniehubov's count (earlier reports said 20 to 22); the Kyiv regional administration counts three dead and eight injured across the region over the past 24 hours with 21 civilian sites damaged in five districts. Ukrainian figures, not independently verified.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (AFP, AP, Reuters), Ukrinform (Kharkiv and Kyiv regional administrations)

timeline.event: Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 165 Shahed-type attack drones, 79 of them jet-powered, plus Gerbera and decoy drones from 18:00 on Sunday and that 112 were neutralised; the General Staff's 08:00 update counts 229 combat clashes, 90 airstrikes with 277 guided bombs and 8,845 kamikaze drones in a day, and Zelensky says nearly 4,000 drones, bombs and missiles hit Ukraine in the past week. Ukrainian claims, not independently verified.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian Air Force, General Staff), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: Brigadier-General Andrii Biletskyi says Ukraine's Third Army Corps recaptured 51 sq km in northern Donetsk, taking the 'Vivaldi' operation's total to 176 sq km; the ISW says it disrupted a Russian encirclement of the 'fortress belt' cities. Ukrainian claim, not independently verified.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says Ukraine is 'paying the price' for its attacks on Russia in recent months and Russian forces will keep striking targets; he separately says Russia-US arms-control talks should have resumed 'yesterday'.

Pope Leo, in Metz, says negotiators must be willing to sacrifice some positions to reach peace, lamenting a 'senseless slaughter' in Europe; EU defence ministers meet in Brussels to debate a NATO-style emergency mechanism against Russian 'hybrid attacks'.

Russian drones strike across Ukraine in a daytime assault; one hits the National Academy of Sciences in central Kyiv, where emergency services say two died. Zelensky says at least nine were killed and more than 80 injured nationwide; Klitschko reports 24 injured in Kyiv.

Russia's defence ministry claims strikes on fuel, telecoms and data-centre infrastructure in Kyiv, three cargo vessels bound for Odesa, a ship in Chornomorsk and a ship-repair yard in Izmail; the claims are not independently verified.

Zelensky says more than 8,000 North Korean troops are in Russia and another 10,000 are being prepared (unverified); Seoul summons Ukraine's acting ambassador over his disclosure of the transfer of two captured North Korean soldiers.
On his flight back to Rome, Pope Leo urges Russia and Ukraine to sit down and discuss ending the war, and criticises leaders who talk about nuclear weapons.
Ukraine tells the EU it sees no prospect of a Black Sea ceasefire covering grain exports in the coming months, saying Russia rejects all proposals while strikes on shipping cut its export capacity.

Russia strikes Kyiv again before dawn; Mayor Klitschko says missile debris fell in a courtyard and a building caught fire. Emergency officials say Monday's drone strike on the National Academy of Sciences killed two.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched three missiles and 152 attack drones, 82 of them jet-powered, overnight and that it downed all the missiles and 106 drones; an educational institution in Kyiv was hit and one person injured. Claims not independently verified.
Zelensky says the depot at Kyiv-Pasazhyrskyi station, data centres and business centres in Kyiv were damaged overnight, along with a dormitory and two foreign-flagged vessels in Odesa region.
Kyiv's city military administration says 12 people were killed and about 200 injured in Russian attacks on the capital over the past week.

Estonia says Russian security services ordered the Aug 15 arson attack on Milrem Robotics, which supplies ground drones to Ukraine; NATO chief Rutte and EU leaders back Tallinn and the Kremlin rejects the accusation.
timeline.source: CNA (AFP), The Straits Times (Reuters), Kyiv Independent

timeline.event: Russian glide bombs hit homes and a school in Sumy, killing two people and injuring six, including three children; about 100 people were in the school's shelter, officials say.
Zelensky says Belgium will transfer three F-16s by the end of the year and that a package of NASAMS air-defence missiles has arrived.
Chancellor Merz says Russia's reaction to the Lavrov-Wadephul meeting at the UN shows it is 'obviously not interested in serious talks'.
Air Force spokesman Yurii Ihnat says Russia has launched 3,177 jet-powered drones so far in September, against 2,850 in all of August (Ukrainian figures, not independently verified).
Budget documents obtained by Reuters show Russia plans record defence spending of 17.1 trillion roubles in 2027 while cutting welfare, education and health funding.
Ballistic missile explosions rock Kyiv shortly before 3am and cut electricity in parts of the city, Kyiv Independent reporters say, as the multi-day assault on the capital continues.
Russian missile and drone strikes kill three people, including a child, and injure seven in Kyiv and the surrounding region, local officials say.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched Zircon/Oniks and Iskander-M/S-400 missiles and 188 drones from the evening of Sept 29, mainly at Kyiv region, and that 160 targets, five missiles and 155 drones, were shot down or suppressed (Ukrainian figures, not independently verified).
Poland and Romania scramble jets during the strikes; Lublin and Rzeszow airports close temporarily and later resume flights, Poland's air traffic agency says.

A drone crashes and explodes in an open area near Hirbovat in Moldova's Anenii Noi district, about 20km from the Ukrainian border, with no casualties reported, Moldovan police say; Ukrinform describes the drone as Russian.
Ukraine's General Staff reports 221 combat clashes over the past day, with the heaviest fighting on the Kostiantynivka axis (Ukrainian figures).
South Korea made no military-aid pledge to Ukraine in return for the transfer of two captured North Korean soldiers, a lawmaker says after an intelligence briefing.

Russia's defence ministry says its overnight strike hit the De Novo data centre in Kyiv, the Kyivska substation, the Kyiv hydroelectric plant in Vyshhorod, the Trypilska thermal power plant and port infrastructure in Izmail (Russian claims).

Zelensky says five people, including a child, were killed and 14 injured across Ukraine and that the strikes mainly targeted energy infrastructure in and around Kyiv; Kyiv police later count three dead and seven injured in the city.

The BBC reports the barrage as Russia's largest attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure since spring; DTEK restores power to about 8,000 homes and Centrenergo says equipment at the Trypilska plant was damaged.

Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck a Russian command-and-observation post in Lysychansk, a repair facility in Starobilsk and depots in occupied Donetsk region and Crimea on Sept 29-30 (Ukrainian claims).
In a document sent to NATO and seen by Reuters, Russia says it would be ready to use nuclear weapons if the alliance tried to isolate Kaliningrad.
Prime Minister Koretskyi puts Ukraine's 2026 war costs at US$155 billion and says a US$27 billion funding gap remains, US$20 billion of it still to be found from partners.
Four US House members from both parties urge Trump not to ease Russia sanctions in exchange for prisoner releases; the Kremlin denies Russia holds political prisoners.
Zelensky visits troops in the Lyman sector and says Operation Vivaldi has returned more than 125 square kilometres to Ukrainian control (Ukrainian claim).
Zelensky says seven people, including a child, were killed and 24 injured in Russian attacks since the start of the day (Ukrainian figures).
Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 285 strike drones, 174 of them jet-powered, between 6.30am and 6.30pm, and that 254 were shot down or suppressed (Ukrainian claims).

Zelensky adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov says Russia used a jet drone with a shaped-charge warhead designed to cut high-voltage pylons for the first time; emergency power cuts are imposed in Kyiv and three regions.
Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova says European factories producing weapons for Ukraine are potential military targets for Russia.
Ukraine's charge d'affaires in Washington says Kyiv will ask the US to sanction component suppliers for Russia's Rassvet satellite network, AP reported.

Ukraine's nuclear regulator says a Russian drone struck the premises of Kyiv's Institute for Nuclear Research, which houses a research reactor, at 18:18 on Sept 30; the reactor was not damaged and radiation levels did not change.
Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 107 strike drones overnight, 63 of them jet-powered Shaheds, and that 87 were shot down or suppressed by 8am (Ukrainian claims).
Overnight drone strikes start fires in Kyiv's Solomianskyi and Obolonskyi districts, including at a cafe in a residential building; one person is injured, Ukraine's emergency service says.
A 50-year-old man is killed in a morning drone attack in the Mykolaiv region, and a Russian strike damages a business centre in Odesa, injuring one person, regional officials say.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte tells Russia to 'stop the nuclear threat' after reports of a Russian letter to the alliance, while saying NATO faces no immediate threat despite rising hybrid attacks.

Two Russian drones strike near the supports of Kyiv's Southern Bridge, the first attack on one of the capital's bridges, Mayor Klitschko says; metro trains are limited to underground sections, and a drone hits a school while pupils shelter, with no injuries.
timeline.source: Kyiv Independent, The Straits Times (Reuters), Ukrinform

timeline.event: Local authorities say Russian attacks killed at least six people and injured 38 across Ukraine over the past day, including two killed in Sumy Oblast.

Zelensky says Ukrainian long-range strikes hit a target in the Black Sea, a drone launch and storage site in Russia's Oryol region, an oil facility in Samara and a supply depot in Bryansk; the claims could not be independently verified.
Ukraine's General Staff claims a 2026-high 46,230 Russian personnel losses in September, up from 31,710 in January; Russia does not publish its losses and the figure cannot be verified.
Britain adds 31 Russia sanctions but extends licences that let Japan and South Korea keep importing Russian LNG.
Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 97 strike drones between 06:30 and 18:00, including 66 jet-powered, and 78 were shot down or suppressed.
A Ukrainian MiG-29 is shot down by a Russian missile; the pilot, Capt Marat Mambetov, 25, ejected but did not survive, the Air Force says.
Zelensky announces the first combat use of Ukraine's FP-7 tactical ballistic missile but his office will not say what it hit.
A Russian drone hits Kyiv's Southern Bridge for the second time, damaging a support, the road surface and the metro's protective structure, Mayor Klitschko says.
Putin rules out a ceasefire on energy and shipping strikes, calling the idea 'ridiculous', and warns Russia would use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad.
Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 108 strike drones overnight and 88 were shot down or suppressed.
An overnight attack kills one person and injures two in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district; the Southern Bridge is hit again and the Southern and Paton bridges are closed to traffic, city authorities say.
Russia announces an autumn call-up of 120,000 conscripts and again says they will not be sent to fight in Ukraine or the occupied regions.
Ukrainian monitoring channels report strikes on the Volgograd refinery and a Samara oil station; the Kyiv Independent could not verify the damage.
South Korea's President Lee threatens unspecified measures unless Kyiv apologises for disclosing the transfer of two North Korean POWs; Kyiv calls it a 'diplomatic misunderstanding'.

Zelensky says nearly 50 of the more than 100 drones launched overnight were jet-powered and urges allies to choke off foreign components; Kyiv's Southern and Paton bridges stay closed, causing traffic chaos.
Regional authorities say Russian attacks killed two and injured 27 across Ukraine over the past day; an FPV drone hit a passenger bus in Kramatorsk, injuring two.
The dline.ua data centre in Kyiv is destroyed in a Russian strike, the third data centre to halt operations in recent days, the company says.
Zelensky says Ukrainian forces hit oil facilities in Russia's Samara and Volgograd regions over the past 24 hours; the claim could not be independently verified.
A combined missile and drone attack on Mykolaiv damages port and civilian infrastructure and injures three men, the regional administration says.
Ukraine receives EUR 2.9 billion under the EU's Ukraine Facility after passing reforms; Hungary welcomes Kyiv's minority-education bill, due for a vote on Oct 12.

Three Russian glide bombs hit Kharkiv, killing two women aged 66 and 80 and injuring more than 30, including three children, regional officials and emergency services say; one residential building is destroyed.
A fourth Russian drone strike in two days hits Kyiv's Southern Bridge at evening rush hour; mayor Vitali Klitschko says the strikes are 'tearing Kyiv apart' and the city should be on a war footing.
Ukraine's foreign ministry says foreign embassies are not planning to evacuate Kyiv, after a Guardian report quoting an unnamed diplomat raised concerns.
Zelensky tells El Pais that Putin will intensify attacks as the US midterms approach; he also signs a law making Ukraine part of the European Defence Fund.
The UK sanctions seven Russians, including the head of the state youth group Movement of the First, over the deportation and indoctrination of Ukrainian children.
Kyrylo Budanov says more than 26,000 bodies have been returned to Ukraine but many remain unidentified, and announces an interagency group to speed up identification.
The joint US-Ukraine reconstruction fund seals its first critical minerals deal, about US$30 million in early-stage mining projects.
A Russian drone attack on Hostomel in Kyiv Oblast hits warehouses and injures four people, including an eight-year-old girl, the regional administration says.

UN human rights chief Volker Turk tells the Human Rights Council that his office documented 15,280 civilians killed or injured in Ukraine in the first eight months of 2026, an average of more than 400 a week and 55% more than in the same period of 2025.

A Russian strike hits Kyiv's Northern Bridge, damaging the road surface and trolleybus wires, Mayor Vitali Klitschko says; traffic is suspended and he later says two people were injured. It is the second Dnipro bridge struck this week after repeated drone hits on the Southern Bridge.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Reuters), Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform

timeline.event: A Russian attack sets fire to the roof of a business centre in central Dnipro that a drone had already hit earlier in the week, regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha says.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 157 Shahed, Gerbera and decoy drones overnight, 45 of them jet-powered, and that 131 were shot down or suppressed, with hits at 12 locations; regional authorities report at least eight civilians killed and 83 injured over the past day.

Moldova's President Maia Sandu says five Russian weapons exploded on Moldovan territory during the overnight attack on Ukraine; Defence Minister Anatolie Nosatyi counts three missiles and two drones. No casualties or damage are reported.

The New York Times reports that US-Russia talks on ending the war now include a multibillion-dollar deal for Lukoil's overseas oil fields, refineries and petrol stations, contingent on US and Kremlin approval; the White House, the US Treasury and Lukoil did not respond to requests for comment.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters, citing the New York Times)

timeline.event: The IAEA says strikes on 19, 20 and 27 Sep damaged transformers at the Zaporizhzhia Thermal Power Plant that supply off-site power to the nuclear plant; Director General Rafael Grossi is negotiating an eighth local ceasefire so repairs can be made.

Russia's foreign ministry again urges diplomats and foreigners to leave Kyiv, saying its forces 'will continue to deliver massive retaliatory strikes' and that those who ignore the warning bear responsibility for the consequences.
A Russian attack on a civilian vessel in a port in Odesa region kills a motorman and injures three crew members, the Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority says; 13 crew are evacuated.

ISW says Vladimir Putin's claim at the Valdai Club on 1 Oct that Russian forces seized 1,301 sq km of Ukrainian territory in September is contradicted by the evidence, which it says shows Russia suffered a net loss of about 81 sq km that month.

Infrastructure Minister Mykola Kalashnyk says pontoon crossings and a dam crossing are being built quickly in Kyiv after strikes on the Southern and Northern bridges between 1 and 3 Oct; the pontoons could take up to three months.

Zelensky tells Reuters that Ukrainian intelligence has documents showing Putin approved a 'new doctrine' of strikes on a broader range of civilian targets this winter, including roads, schools and hospitals, to push people out of Kyiv and other cities; he says Ukraine will step up strikes on Russian oil refineries but not civilians.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters), Ukrinform, Kyiv Independent

timeline.event: Zelensky says Operation Vivaldi has retaken about 125-140 sq km so far and that Russian losses have risen over the past two to three months; the figures are Ukrainian claims and have not been independently verified.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrives in Kyiv with defence-industry chiefs; German officials say he will release €1 billion in military aid and €350 million for energy repairs, and a deal on jointly producing drones is expected to be finalised.

Kyiv authorities report drone debris falling in the Obolonskyi, Desnianskyi and Dniprovskyi districts during the day, setting fire to a high-rise roof and a non-residential building; no casualties were mentioned in the reports.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Kyiv City Military Administration, Mayor Vitali Klitschko)

timeline.event: President Zelensky says Russia launched more than 1,900 attack drones, 1,700 aerial bombs and 25 missiles at Ukraine this week, over 800 of the drones jet-powered, and 135 drones overnight; Ukrainian figures, not independently verified.

A Russian drone hits Kyiv's Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge for a second day, injuring two people, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko, as Chancellor Merz visits; regional authorities say Russian attacks killed at least five people and injured 30 across Ukraine over the past day, with Sumy hit by drones and glide bombs.

Russia's defence ministry says it will intensify strikes on military and defence-industry sites in Kyiv and elsewhere, responding to Zelensky's pledge in a Reuters interview to step up attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Germany and Ukraine sign a US$1.5 billion weapons and energy deal and drone-cooperation agreements during Chancellor Merz's visit to Kyiv; Merz announces a further €1 billion in military aid and says Germany will not be intimidated.

Russia's defence ministry says it hit Kyiv's Northern bridge over the Dnipro, calling it a route for troops and military cargo, and two dry cargo vessels it says were carrying military equipment to Odesa; Russian claims, not independently verified.
Ukraine's SBU says drones hit a Su-35 and a Su-34 fighter jet and an ammunition depot at the Khanskaya military airfield in Russia's Adygea region; Ukrainian claim.
Ukraine's defence ministry says its long-range strikes have disabled more than 51% of Russia's oil refining capacity; Ukrainian figure, not independently verified.

Zelensky says the US is proposing trilateral technical talks with Russia by the end of October, possibly in the UAE, and that Ukraine believes Russia has shared jet-powered drone technology with North Korea; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says Moscow does not rule out talks in October.
timeline.source: Kyiv Independent, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

timeline.event: A Russian drone strike on an energy facility in Poltava region leaves 22,000 customers without power, according to Ukrainian officials.
A Russian double-tap strike with Banderol missiles on Kharkiv's industrial district kills one person and injures six, and damages at least 10 residential buildings, Mayor Ihor Terekhov says.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 205 Shahed-type drones, 49 of them jet-powered, plus other attack and decoy drones from 18:00 on Sunday; air defences shot down or suppressed 172 by 08:00, with hits at 13 locations. Ukrainian figures.

Odesa Governor Oleh Kiper says massive Russian strikes targeted industrial and port infrastructure in the region; Russia's defence ministry says it hit Vylkove port, fuel depots in Chornomorsk and cargo vessels. Russian claims, not independently verified.

Russian attacks killed five people and injured 61 across Ukraine over the past day, according to regional authorities compiled by the Kyiv Independent; Ukrenergo says shelling caused new power outages in the Donetsk, Kharkiv, Sumy, Poltava, Odesa and Kherson regions. Ukrainian figures.
A projectile lands at the Palanca crossing on the Moldova-Ukraine border, ricochets into a passenger bus and a control booth, and lightly injures a Moldovan border guard, Moldova's Border Police say.

The Turkish-flagged grain carrier Royad Mammadov catches fire and sinks in the Black Sea outside Romanian waters; Romania's interior ministry says two crew died and 11 were rescued. Romanian authorities gave no cause; Romanian media cited by Ukrinform say a Russian drone hit the ship, which is not officially confirmed.

Three Russian airstrikes on the Sloviansk community kill a woman and injure three people including a 13-year-old boy, and damage at least four apartment buildings and 50 homes, the local military administration says. Ukrainian figures.
Russian guided bombs hit Kharkiv's Slobidskyi district, killing six people and injuring 59, regional governor Oleh Syniehubov says after rescuers recover a sixth victim. Ukrainian figures.

Zelensky says two Russian drones struck the Turkish-owned, corn-carrying Royad Mammadov in neutral waters, killing its captain, with another sailor missing; Russia's defence ministry had said it struck two cargo vessels but did not comment on this ship.

Rosatom's chief Alexei Likhachev says Ukrainian drones attacked a laboratory building and a radioactive-waste processing plant at the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant overnight, killing a driver, with no threat to nuclear safety. Ukraine has not commented.
Russia targets Kyiv with drones late in the evening; debris from an intercepted drone falls on a residential area of the Pechersk district and sets cars on fire.

The Financial Times, cited by Ukrinform, reports that Hungary's PM Péter Magyar has told diplomats not to block letters on opening two more EU accession clusters for Ukraine and Moldova this week, with final support tied to a law the Rada is due to pass.

A Russian drone hits one of the Dnipro bridges in Zaporizhzhia overnight; the bridge is closed and regional head Mykhailo Semikin says five people were injured, two of them Red Cross workers on their way to work. Ukrainian figures.
Russian forces strike infrastructure in Odesa again overnight with no casualties, regional head Serhii Lysak says, a day after a large attack on the region's industrial and port facilities.

The Guardian, cited by the Kyiv Independent, reports that more than 176,000 tonnes of fuel, mostly diesel, were shipped from South Korean ports to Russia in July and August on vessels under Western sanctions. Seoul has not commented in the report.
Dutch PM Rob Jetten says the Netherlands will help Ukraine with F-16 maintenance, spare parts and ammunition after speaking with Zelensky about the weekend strikes on Kyiv.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 137 Shahed-type drones overnight and 114 were downed; regional authorities say Russian attacks killed at least 13 people and injured 104 over the past day, seven of the dead in Kharkiv region, and a missile strike damaged a hospital in Kryvyi Rih. Ukrainian figures.

Ukraine sends drones at the Moscow region in one of its largest attacks on the capital area: Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says more than 650 headed for Moscow and the regional governor says two people were killed; Russian war bloggers say the Volodarskaya fuel depot was hit, without official confirmation.

Drones sink the Togo-flagged cargo ship Alfa Watan inside Bulgaria's Black Sea economic zone, with its crew missing, and hit the grain carrier Able, whose 18 crew are rescued; Bulgaria's PM does not say who was responsible. Ukraine says a Russian drone separately killed a crew member on a Marshall Islands-flagged ship, and the EU's von der Leyen calls the attacks unacceptable.
timeline.source: BBC, Kyiv Independent, The Straits Times (Reuters)

timeline.event: Lithuania's parliament approves, in the first of two readings, lifting the constitutional ban on hosting nuclear weapons; the Kremlin warns the move risks further escalation.
Zelensky says Ukraine has received updated intelligence on Russian preparations for a massive strike and that air-defence assets are being deployed to protect key sites.

Russia's Transport Ministry says all 23 crew of the Liberian-flagged tanker Aframax Rio were rescued after an unmanned vessel attack set it ablaze off the Black Sea coast near Sochi; Ukrainian outlets describe it as a sanctioned 'shadow fleet' tanker.
Zelensky says Ukraine's forces conducted no operations in Bulgarian waters, where two civilian ships were hit by drones earlier in the day.
Poland says it will deploy Patriot batteries in Lublin province on the Ukrainian border and announces a US$26 billion civil defence plan.

Russia launches a mass missile and drone attack on Kyiv from about 3.15am, on Putin's 74th birthday; strikes are reported around Podil and on a non-residential area in Obolon, and the damage is not yet clear.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 48 cruise missiles, ballistic and anti-ship missiles and 130 attack drones from 6pm on 6 October, mainly at the Kyiv, Kharkiv, Poltava and Dnipropetrovsk regions; it says 161 targets were downed or suppressed, including five ballistic missiles, 39 cruise missiles and 117 drones, with hits at 18 locations.

Ukrainian officials say two people were killed in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district, two killed and seven injured when a missile hit an apartment block in Pryluky, and one killed in Oleksandriia; Russia's defence ministry says it carried out a 'massive strike' that hit port facilities in the Odesa region.

The BBC reports at least 15 deaths across central and eastern Ukraine from the overnight strikes, and Zelensky says 70 missiles were fired in total; Ukraine's State Emergency Service later puts the toll from the strike on a Pryluky apartment block alone at 14, with 50 injured including seven children.

Ukraine's General Staff says damage has been confirmed to 14 oil storage tanks at the Samara oil pumping and blending station it struck on 2 October; Zelensky says Ukraine hit targets in Russia's Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions in the past 24 hours.
Bulgaria ends the search for the crew of the cargo ship sunk by a drone strike in its Black Sea economic zone, saying there is no trace of the sailors.

EU ambassadors approve nearly 1,600 new sanctions listings on Russia's military-industrial complex, the largest single list yet, for adoption by foreign ministers on 12 October, the Kyiv Independent reports; Norway's 2027 budget earmarks 85 billion kroner for Ukraine.

Ukraine says a Russian Kh-101 missile strike on an apartment block in Pryluky killed 20 people including five children, and police chief Ivan Vyhivsky says strikes on Pryluky, Kremenchuk, Oleksandriia and Kyiv killed 28 people that day (Ukrainian official figures).
A Danish intelligence official says Russia has begun sabotage operations against Danish companies supplying Ukraine.
Yandex says drones hit one of its major data centres in Russia's Ryazan region, causing a fire and forcing it to suspend the site; OSINT groups identify it as the Sasovo facility, its largest.
Ukraine's State Emergency Service says a Russian drone struck a 12-storey residential building in Kyiv's Desnianskyi district, injuring four people including two children.
Five sources tell Reuters that US envoy Jared Kushner and Putin adviser Kirill Dmitriev have discussed bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream gas pipelines; neither government has confirmed it.
Ukraine's General Staff confirms an overnight strike on the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat refinery in Bashkortostan, which set the plant ablaze.

Kyiv authorities say Russian attacks killed four people and injured 19 in the capital over the day (final count from Mayor Klitschko, revised from earlier reports), with a key energy facility hit and widespread outages, metro and water disruption.
South Korea recalls its ambassador from Ukraine over the disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean POWs to Seoul.
Rubio tells Kathimerini a negotiated settlement is 'currently unattainable' because Russia demands all of Donetsk without fighting.
The UK publishes 38 new sanctions listings targeting shadow-fleet ships, military suppliers, three crypto exchanges and two payment platforms.
Russian glide bombs strike two passenger buses in Kramatorsk; officials say at least 30 killed and 18 wounded, with the State Emergency Service later putting the toll at 33.
Ukraine's General Staff confirms a drone strike on the Omsk oil refinery in Siberia, about 2,500 km from the border.
Russian regional officials say two people were killed in Ukrainian drone strikes in Belgorod region.
Yandex says it cannot yet tell whether its Sasovo data centre can be restored; Zelensky says Ukraine 'always responds in kind'.
The Kremlin says it agrees with Rubio that the war is in a stalemate; Ukrainian negotiators will meet Witkoff and Kushner in Miami on 9 Oct, a US source says.
Britain announces £54 million (US$71 million) in humanitarian and energy aid for Ukraine's fifth winter of war, as Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband visits Pryluky with Zelensky.
The State Emergency Service's toll for the Kramatorsk bus strike stands at 33 killed and 22 injured; the BBC describes a surge in deadly Russian attacks on civilians.

Russian Telegram channels report Ukrainian drones hit the Redkino Experimental Plant in Tver region, which makes components for Kh-55 and Kh-101 cruise-missile fuel, and oil infrastructure overnight; the reports are not independently confirmed.
Ivano-Frankivsk's regional governor says a Russian drone attack killed one man in the city.
Russian guided bombs strike Zaporizhzhia between 5am and 6am, killing a 50-year-old man; the acting regional head says the day's injury toll rose to 23.

Ukraine's General Staff says it hit three Russian missile-production facilities overnight, including a Tver region plant making missile components and a centre for dismantling intercontinental ballistic missiles in Nizhny Novgorod region.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters, Ukrainian General Staff)

timeline.event: Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 136 drones overnight, including 93 jet-powered Shahed-type drones, and that 114 were shot down or suppressed.
Yandex says a drone attack disabled several modules at its data centre in Kaluga region, the second of its data centres hit in two days.
Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets says Russian forces forcibly removed 25 civilians, including children, from occupied Kharkiv Oblast to an unknown destination.
Zelensky says Ukrainian An-196 drones hit the Ukhta oil refinery, about 1,900 km from Ukraine's border, a day after the Omsk strike.
Moscow's Domodedovo, Sheremetyevo, Vnukovo and Zhukovsky airports temporarily halt flights as suspected Ukrainian drones and balloons enter airspace around the capital.

Mediazona, working with the BBC Russian Service, identifies 20 Russian officers killed in Ukraine's 26 Aug missile strikes on command posts in Donetsk, the most in any single attack of the war, the monitors say.
Trump says Putin agreed to supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately and more later to the US and world markets; Zelensky calls it 'a gift to Putin' and 'an investment in a war that must be ended'.
The Kremlin says Putin told Trump that Kyiv undermined an immediate resumption of trilateral talks by striking Moscow with drones during last month's election.
Zelensky says Ukraine's negotiating team, in Florida for two days of talks with US officials on at least an energy ceasefire, is being used as a 'smokescreen' while Trump speaks to the Kremlin.

Yandex says it is struggling to maintain services after two of its five data centres were hit by Ukrainian drones in two days; Zelensky says the strikes answer weeks of Russian attacks on Ukrainian data centres.

US, Ukrainian and European officials meet in Miami for talks on ending the war, which the US side describes as 'productive'; no outcome is announced and the meeting is overshadowed by Trump's diesel deal with Putin.

Five Russian glide bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, killing 20 people including three children, Ukraine's emergency service says; regional official Ivan Fedorov says 32 were injured. Zelensky calls it Russia's 'thank you' for the lifting of US diesel sanctions, and the city declares 11 Oct a day of mourning.
timeline.source: CNA (AP), Ukrinform (State Emergency Service, Fedorov), BBC

timeline.event: A fire breaks out at an oil terminal linked to Russia's Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Rostov region after a suspected Ukrainian drone strike, Russian regional media report - hours after the Trump-Putin diesel announcement.

Russia launches a daytime ballistic missile attack on Kyiv after morning drone strikes on energy facilities; power outages briefly halt the metro and missile debris falls in the Obolon district, the city says.
Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck the Samara oil pumping and blending station in Russia again, and confirms a fire and four destroyed storage tanks there from a 7 Oct strike.

Axios, citing a US official, reports that Trump pressed Zelensky to halt strikes on Russian refineries unilaterally because they were pushing up US fuel prices; Zelensky had offered a mutual halt on energy strikes.
Germany says it will keep its Russia sanctions and work with EU partners on further measures after the US temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel.

Russian strikes kill at least 24 people and injure 47 across Ukraine in a day, the Kyiv Independent tallies from regional officials, including an 11-year-old boy killed by a drone-dropped munition in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast's Nikopol district; an administrative building and a residential block are hit in Odesa.

Ukraine's negotiating team heads home from the US after talks in Florida; a Zelensky adviser says the second day was not cancelled but the first 'turned out to be longer and had a somewhat different flavour'.

Trump says 'it's time for Ukraine to get a new president' and tells Zelensky to 'damn well stop' striking Russian refineries; Russia says it has partially lifted its own diesel export ban, and the deal draws bipartisan criticism in Washington.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, Kyiv Independent (TASS)

timeline.event: Overnight Russian strikes on Dnipro injure four people, including two children, regional head Oleksandr Hanzha says; an apartment block is damaged and food warehouses, trucks and cars catch fire.

Yandex's data centre in Russia's Vladimir Oblast is completely shut down after a reported drone attack, TASS says, citing the company; it follows strikes on Yandex data centres in Ryazan and Kaluga oblasts on 8 and 9 Oct.

Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha rejects Trump's call for a new Ukrainian president, saying Zelensky 'has the support of the Ukrainian people, and they have the right to decide'. Finland's PM Petteri Orpo calls the US-Russia diesel deal a 'terrible disappointment', and Republican senators John Kennedy and Lisa Murkowski also criticise it.
Japan's Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi says Tokyo has signed a contract to buy interceptor drones from Ukrainian company SkyFall.
Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 116 attack and decoy drones overnight, of which 94 were shot down or suppressed; hits by 10 drones were recorded at seven locations.
Russian aircraft drop three FAB-250 bombs on a residential area of Sloviansk, injuring at least seven people, Mayor Vadym Lyakh says; Zelensky says a five-storey block of flats was hit.

Zelensky says Ukraine will stop attacking Russian oil refineries if Russia stops striking Ukraine's energy infrastructure, rejecting Trump's demand for a unilateral halt; German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul says Berlin fully supports Zelensky after Trump's call for him to be replaced.
