Iran has not responded to the allegation, but said earlier that two tankers caught fire after striking mines on an unauthorised route.
timeline.source: BBC (Saudi government, Bahri, maritime security firms)

timeline.event: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warns that operations against American forces in the region will continue until the US 'regrets' its actions.
Israel says it is prepared to 'respond with great force' if Iran attacks, with forces readied for a possible attack over the Jewish high holiday season beginning in mid-September.
President Donald Trump floats renaming the Strait of Hormuz the 'Trump Strait', after claiming US sovereignty over the waterway Tehran has effectively shut for six months.

Iran attacks US military bases in Kuwait. Kuwait's army says it is intercepting a missile and drone attack; Iranian state TV says the strikes target US bases in the Gulf state 'in response to America's crimes against the Iranian people'. Tehran says it also hit US targets in Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Iraq's Kurdistan region. Trump says the US is prepared to attack Iran 'any time we want'; security chief Mohsen Rezaei says Iran has adopted a 'new strategy' that 'will shatter your foundations'. All strike and interception claims are from parties to the war.
timeline.source: CNA (Kuwait's army, Iranian state TV, Donald Trump, Mohsen Rezaei)

timeline.event: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres says he is 'deeply alarmed by reports of civilian casualties, including a strike that reportedly hit a wedding ceremony in Iran'.

On his first Middle East visit in four years, Chinese President Xi Jinping tells Egypt's Abdel Fattah al-Sisi that regional countries should be 'masters of their own destiny' and explore a new regional 'security architecture', according to Chinese state agency Xinhua. The two agree to deepen security and counter-terrorism cooperation. Egypt receives about US$1.3 billion a year in US military aid.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says Washington will expand sanctions on Iran's trade partners to choke its economy, as the US presses a counter-blockade of Iranian ports while Tehran keeps its hold on the Strait of Hormuz.
The number of Iranian military personnel reported killed by US strikes this week rises to 13, according to Iranian accounts. The figure is Tehran's and is not independently verified.
US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick apologises for saying no Americans have died in the Iran war.

Vice-President J.D. Vance says the United States is investigating whether an American munition struck a wedding party in Iran. The Straits Times reports that open-source analysis points to a likely direct hit by a US munition; the Pentagon has not confirmed a cause, and Iran's casualty account has not been independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (J.D. Vance, Iranian officials)

timeline.event: Vance says the Iran conflict 'is not a war' and declines to offer a timeline for its end.

South Korea's presidential office says it is reviewing options, including military measures, to support freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, while denying reports by JTBC and MBC that a deployment had already been decided. Options reported under consideration include a maritime patrol aircraft, a logistics support vessel or a mine-clearance unit. 'Nothing has been decided,' a presidential official said, citing domestic legal procedures, readiness on the Korean Peninsula and the need for parliamentary approval.
timeline.source: CNA (South Korean presidential office, JTBC, MBC)

timeline.event: Three senior Iranian sources tell CNA and The Straits Times that the US effort to blockade Iran's oil exports and cut its access to international financing networks is becoming increasingly difficult to withstand, leaving Tehran with few channels for foreign currency or imports. The assessment comes from Iranian officials and is not independently verified; Iran has warned it could answer the pressure with military escalation.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (senior Iranian sources)

timeline.event: Fighting between Yemen's Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces kills 81 people, military and medical sources tell AFP, as the rebels push towards high ground overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb strait and the government-held port of Mokha. A coastal military official reported 24 of his men killed and a Taiz official 15; medical sources in Houthi-held areas counted at least 42 rebel dead. All tallies come from parties to the fighting. Bab el-Mandeb has become a critical oil transit route since Iran's blockade of Hormuz.
timeline.source: CNA (AFP, Yemeni military and medical sources)

timeline.event: The US military has switched off advertising trackers on service members' devices after reports that location data broadcast by mobile apps was being used to target American forces in the Middle East.

The United States, Britain, France and Germany seek a resolution at the IAEA's 35-nation board next week referring Iran to the UN Security Council for the first time in about 20 years, according to diplomats and a draft text described by news agencies. Iran has not let inspectors return to the enrichment sites destroyed or damaged in the US and Israeli strikes, or verify stocks enriched to up to 60 per cent purity. The draft has not been formally submitted and wording is still being negotiated.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (diplomats, draft IAEA resolution)

timeline.event: The United States sanctions a Turkish bank and two of its subsidiaries in the latest round of Iran-related financial pressure.
US diesel prices reach an all-time high, a knock-on from the disruption to crude and refined-product flows caused by the conflict.

President Donald Trump describes the Iran conflict as 'small potatoes' and plays down the scale of the war, days after Vice-President J.D. Vance declined to call the six-month confrontation a war or set an end date.

Iran's semi-official Tasnim agency reports that a tanker at the Kharg Island anchorage was hit by four US missiles, with no casualties and the crew evacuated. Iranian authorities issue no official statement and US Central Command does not respond to requests for comment, so the account rests on a single state-linked source.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Tasnim news agency)

timeline.event: US Central Command says it struck three Iranian oil tankers, including one off Kharg Island, after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired ballistic missiles at two US Navy ships - an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer. Centcom says it evaded the attacks, that no American troops were harmed, and that the tankers were 'part of a multi-billion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies'. It says two tankers were 'permanently disabled' and a third 'completely destroyed' in the Gulf of Oman. Centcom chief Admiral Brad Cooper said: 'If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost - taking out three of yours.'
timeline.source: CNA, BBC, The Straits Times (US Central Command)

timeline.event: The IRGC threatens intensified strikes on US military vessels in the region and says it later targeted three tankers travelling on 'unauthorised' routes through the Strait of Hormuz as well as three US-linked vessels elsewhere. Iranian state outlet Irib reports no casualties in the US strike on the tanker near Kharg Island. The BBC says it has approached Centcom for comment on Iran's claims, which are not independently verified.

Hours before Iran's response, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth writes on social media: 'It's simple: if Iran shoots at US ships, we will destroy (and sink) their oil tankers.' President Donald Trump, who a day earlier called the conflict 'small potatoes', has not commented on Saturday's exchange.

Ten people are killed and six injured when a fuel tanker explodes after a crash on the Hamedan-Sanandaj highway in western Iran, Iranian state media report, citing the governor of Sanandaj who blamed a braking-system fault. The incident is described as a traffic accident, not part of the conflict.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Iranian state media, governor of Sanandaj)

timeline.event: Iran vows tougher reprisals after the US strikes on its tankers, while US Central Command repeats that Iran's Revolutionary Guards fired first at American warships. It is the first direct ship-on-ship exchange since the confrontation began in February.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, CNA (US Central Command, IRGC)

timeline.event: Iran's top negotiator threatens a 'faster, more intense' response to the US strikes; The Straits Times reports Tehran targeted one US naval drone and six ships after American forces disabled three Iranian tankers. The tallies are Iranian claims and are not independently confirmed.
Iran says it will step up efforts to deal with the damage US sanctions are doing to its economy, while a senior official warns of a 'painful response' if the country comes under further attack.

Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei tells state TV that Iran will announce a 'prohibited zone' outside the Strait of Hormuz in the coming days, running from the US Navy's blockade line and covering areas of the Persian Gulf, and that any ship entering it will be placed on Iran's sanctions list.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Mohsen Rezaei, Iranian state media)

timeline.event: Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's chief negotiator, says 'the era of proportionate responses has come to an end' and warns that any aggression against Iran's interests will draw 'a faster, more intense and more painful response'. Iranian state media also report the navy struck a US remote-controlled vessel trying to enter the Strait of Hormuz; Central Command spokesman Captain Tim Hawkins calls that 'a total lie'.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iranian state media, US Central Command)

timeline.event: Iran raises petrol prices for heavier consumers as Washington tightens sanctions. Its quota system charges 1,500 tomans a litre for a consumer's first 60 litres a month, 3,000 for the next 50 and 5,000 thereafter.

Relatives in Kuhestak, Hormozgan province, describe pulling family photographs and appliances from the wreckage of a home that Iranian authorities say was destroyed by a US strike on the night of 1 September, killing five people gathered for a wedding. The United States has said it is investigating whether an American munition struck a wedding party in Iran.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, AFP (Iranian authorities, relatives)

timeline.event: Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz falls to a 10-day average of 10 vessels a day, the lowest since May, according to analytics firm Kpler - down from more than 15 on 4 September. Only two vessels passed on 5 September and six on 6 September, mostly using the Iranian route; there have been 27 projectile strike incidents in the region since July.

Parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, Iran's top negotiator, writes that the region's oil and gas production chain is 'sprawling, accessible, and exposed' and that American energy companies share that exposure - 'Strike our assets and you get struck' - responding to US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's warning that Iran's tanker fleet is 'defenceless'. Oil touched six-week highs during Monday trading.

UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash tells the Hili Forum in Abu Dhabi that the country is building alternative pipelines, ports and trade corridors so its energy exports are not 'held hostage', and warns rebuilding trust with Tehran could take decades. Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari says at the same forum that a strategic alliance with the US 'is very important but is not enough'.

IAEA chief Rafael Grossi says the planned US-Saudi civil nuclear agreement will not include the Additional Protocol but will give the agency verification and monitoring authorisations 'very, very similar' to it over enrichment, conversion and reprocessing, to be put to the IAEA Board of Governors once finalised.

The secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council says Tehran will announce a new restricted zone in the Gulf within days and will soon approve maps setting out passage routes through the Strait of Hormuz.
Qatar says the Gulf cannot rely on the United States alone for its security, echoing a wider regional rethink after the strikes on Iranian tankers.

A wave of Houthi attacks on southern Saudi Arabia wounds 73 civilians, including women and children, and ignites fires at oil and utility sites in Jazan, Najran, Abha and Khamis Mushait, the Saudi-led coalition says. Aramco's Jazan facilities were hit and operations at some energy sites were halted while damage is assessed. The casualty figure is the coalition's.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times, AP (Saudi-led coalition)

timeline.event: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, says 'economic warfare will be met by a maritime exclusion zone across the Persian Gulf to the blockade perimeter', and says Washington has had a warning from Iran's new missiles. Iranian media reported a Qassem Basir missile fired at US warships near the Strait of Hormuz; the US military said its warships were not hit. Both accounts are the parties' own.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Iran's Supreme National Security Council; US military)

timeline.event: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi says a secret Assad-era Syrian nuclear reactor destroyed by Israel in 2007 was almost complete and could have been useful for weapons, according to a UN assessment made public this week.

Britain publishes legislation for tougher sanctions on Iran, expanding trade restrictions and creating powers to target ships, which London says is aimed at curbing Tehran's nuclear programme and other hostile activity.

Saudi authorities say Houthi attacks on southern Saudi cities injured 73 people and disrupted energy facilities, with fires at oil and utility sites; the Houthis report Saudi reprisal strikes. Figures are those given by Saudi authorities and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: CNA, BBC, The Straits Times (Saudi authorities; Houthi statements)

timeline.event: Saudi Arabia vows to respond after the Houthi attacks on its cities and energy facilities.
South Korea sends a fact-finding team to assess conditions in the Strait of Hormuz, while stressing that no decision has been made on any troop deployment to the waterway.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they seized an unmanned US submarine drone in the Strait of Hormuz. The claim is Tehran's; Washington has not confirmed it.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Iran's Revolutionary Guards)

timeline.event: The United States announces sanctions on Iranian airlines and service providers.

US Central Command says it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on 8 September, calling it a response to the Revolutionary Guards targeting a US Navy warship twice with ballistic missiles; Washington says no Americans were harmed. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Iran will 'lose tankers' each time it tries to hit US ships.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC (US Central Command)

timeline.event: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it fired ballistic missiles at a base used by US forces near Al Azraq in Jordan and attacked 10 ships, including two US vessels and eight oil tankers. Tehran says the missiles caused heavy damage; Jordan says its air defences intercepted 18 of 20 missiles, with two falling in unpopulated areas and no casualties.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC (IRGC statement; Jordanian government)

timeline.event: CNA reports the heaviest single day of attacks on merchant shipping since the war began, with US and Iranian forces both striking tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz. All strike claims are those of the parties involved.
A merchant oil tanker is hit in Iraqi waters as commercial vessels are caught in the exchange of US and Iranian attacks, The Straits Times reports.
Brent crude rises above US$100 a barrel for the first time since July, which the BBC attributes to the US and Houthi strikes and the widening conflict.
Saudi Arabia lifts the alert in a southern city a day after Houthi strikes that Saudi authorities say injured 73 people and disrupted energy facilities.
A Sunni Kurdish cleric is killed in north-west Iran; the Revolutionary Guards blame 'separatists'. The attribution is the Guards' own and no independent account has been published.
Protesters in South Korea urge Seoul to stay out of the Iran war, days after the government sent a team to assess conditions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, visiting Syria, says 'the main task is to bring down the terror regime in Iran' and that Israel is 'very close' to that. The assessment is his own; Iran's government remains in place.
The Straits Times reports Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi faces a credibility test as Iran-backed Shi'ite militias resist his call to hand their weapons to the state.
Protesters in South Korea urge their government to stay out of the Iran war, CNA reports.

The IAEA's 35-nation Board of Governors passes a resolution reporting Iran to the UN Security Council for breaching its Non-Proliferation Treaty obligations - the first such referral in 20 years. Tehran condemns the resolution and blames US and Israeli strikes on its nuclear facilities for disrupting inspections.
Iran strikes further ships and announces an expanded no-go zone outside the Strait of Hormuz, saying exact coordinates will be published later. The claims are Tehran's.
Brent crude passes US$100 a barrel, the first time since July, on the Middle East flare-up; CNA reports the move is stoking inflation fears.

The Straits Times reports Iran is likely to try to reverse-engineer the unmanned US underwater vehicle its Revolutionary Guards say they seized in the strait. Washington has not publicly confirmed the loss.
Advisers to President Donald Trump warn the conflict with Iran may last through the end of his term, the Wall Street Journal reports - a contrast with the president's own public remarks.

Iran says it attacked more than a dozen vessels attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz in a single day, and the Revolutionary Guards expand the declared no-go zone into the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, warning vessels to seek permission. Brent crude is quoted at US$101.28 a barrel in early Asian trade. The attack claims are Tehran's and are not independently verified.

President Donald Trump says he does not expect the Iran war to end until after November's US midterm elections and that oil prices will not come down until then: "I think the war's going to end immediately after the election because they can't hold out any longer." The assessment is the president's own.
President Donald Trump says activity has been seen at Iran's Pickaxe Mountain site, threatens to attack it and urges Tehran "not to get cute". Iran has not publicly responded to the specific claim.

The Straits Times reports Yemen's Houthis are closing in on a stranglehold over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the southern chokepoint of the Red Sea shipping route, after clashes near Khamis Mushait in Saudi Arabia. Riyadh says there is no danger following the alert.

Four Yemeni government military sources say Iran-aligned Houthi forces have seized the port city of Mocha, a shift that could let them threaten the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The group has also attacked the Hanish islands and pushed government forces south towards Dhubab. The account comes from one party to the conflict.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Yemeni government military sources)

timeline.event: Saudi Arabia says there is no danger after an alert at Khamis Mushait, amid intensifying clashes with the Houthis.

Brent crude closes above US$100 a barrel for the first time since late July, rising more than 3 per cent to US$101.21, dragging equity markets down and pushing European gas above 80 euros per megawatt hour, its highest since early 2023.
India prepares to host the BRICS leaders' summit in New Delhi on 12-13 September with the bloc split by the war: Iran, a member since 2024, and the UAE sit on opposing sides of the conflict.

US President Donald Trump says the war with Iran will not end until after the November US midterm elections, and threatens to strike the underground site known as Pickaxe Mountain. Iran has not responded publicly to the specific threat.

A US official says an Iranian attack on a base in Jordan damaged American military aircraft. The Pentagon has not released a damage assessment and Iran has not confirmed the strike, so the account rests on a single unnamed US official.

Houthi forces advance along Yemen's Red Sea coast after taking Mokha, in a push Saudi and Western officials say threatens Saudi oil exports routed through the Red Sea. Accounts of the advance come from Yemeni government military sources and regional officials and are not independently verified.

Four sources tell The Straits Times that Iranian-supplied weapons and military advice were central to the Houthi capture of Mokha. The sourcing is anonymous and Iran has not commented, so this is a claim rather than an established fact.
The US Treasury sanctions networks it accuses of financing and supplying Iran-aligned armed groups across the Middle East. Tehran rejects the designations as economic pressure without legal basis.

Axios reports that President Donald Trump declined a request from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for US strikes on Houthi forces in Yemen. The report rests on unnamed sources and neither Washington nor Riyadh has confirmed it.

South Korea says its foreign minister discussed the Strait of Hormuz with his Iranian counterpart, one of the few open channels between Tehran and a US ally since the war began. Much of North-east Asia's crude oil transits the strait.

Four Yemeni government sources say Houthi forces have reached the strategic island of Perim (Mayyun) in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, days after taking the port of Mokha. The Houthis have not publicly commented and the account is not independently verified.
Iran's and Saudi Arabia's foreign ministers discuss what both sides describe as regional 'insecurity' as fighting in Yemen flares. Neither released details of what was agreed.
The International Energy Agency warns the 2026 oil supply gap will widen because normal Gulf flows have not resumed. Brent remains above US$100 a barrel.

Six people familiar with the matter say the UAE is revising plans for a 5-gigawatt AI data centre project after Iranian attacks prompted a rethink of where critical infrastructure should be built. The UAE has not confirmed the changes.

Yemeni government officials say Houthi forces completed their takeover of the Bab al-Mandab area and Mayyun (Perim) island, then seized Greater and Lesser Hanish and the remainder of Yemen's Red Sea coastline. 'Everything that was under our control on the western coast has fallen,' a government military official told AFP. The Houthis have made no detailed public statement on the seizures and the accounts have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA, BBC (Yemeni government officials, AFP)

timeline.event: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree says navigation through the Bab al-Mandab strait is 'safe' for all shipping except Saudi Arabia's. The Houthis have been targeting Saudi tankers since July.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Houthi military spokesman, AFP)

timeline.event: AFP reports the week-long Houthi offensive has killed more than 500 people, according to sources on both sides, and displaced about 46,000 people. The tolls come from parties to the fighting and are not independently verified.

Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry says drones launched from Iraq struck the East-West oil pipeline in the Riyadh and Medina regions on the morning of 10 September, causing injuries and damage, and that the line was halted as a precaution. Riyadh says it has chosen not to respond 'at this stage' at the request of the Iraqi prime minister, while reserving the right to protect its sovereignty and facilities. The pipeline runs from Abqaiq near the Gulf to Yanbu on the Red Sea and has carried more Saudi crude since Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Saudi foreign and energy ministries, SPA, AFP)

timeline.event: Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, congratulates the Houthis on their 'resounding victory'.

Oil trades above US$100 a barrel and average US diesel prices top US$6 a gallon for the first time, according to figures cited by The Straits Times. The IEA separately warns the 2026 supply gap will widen because normal Gulf flows have not resumed.
Iran says it will discuss the Strait of Hormuz with Gulf states in Oman on Monday, one of the few open channels with its neighbours since the war began.
President Donald Trump links the 25th anniversary of the 11 September attacks to the current conflict with Iran in public remarks, saying 'that's why we fight'.

The office of Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi confirms the drones that struck Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline were launched from Iraqi territory, dismisses the commander responsible for Maysan province on the Iranian border and opens an investigation. Saudi Arabia keeps the line shut as a precaution and says it will not retaliate at this stage; the BBC cites analysts putting the pipeline's recent throughput at 4–5 per cent of global oil supply.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Iraqi prime minister's office, Saudi foreign ministry)

timeline.event: Xi Jinping arrives in New Delhi for the BRICS summit, which Iran's leadership is also attending; the Middle East war and energy security are expected to dominate the two-day meeting.

Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces say they destroyed Houthi vehicles and weapons and killed fighters near Mocha's port and on the Mocha–Dhubab road, a day after the Houthis completed their hold on the Red Sea coast; the UN migration agency puts the displaced at about 46,000. Claims from parties to the fighting, not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Saba), Al Jazeera (IOM)

timeline.event: In Dublin, Trump says Iran was 'probably' responsible for the drone attack on Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline and that the Houthis have told his administration they do not want the US directly involved and are 'letting most ships go through'. He offered no evidence; Baghdad's finding is that the drones were launched from its Maysan province.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters copy; Donald Trump), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: BRICS leaders unanimously adopt a New Delhi declaration that, per Al Jazeera, stresses keeping trade, supply chains and energy flowing; CNA cites sources saying it condemns unilateral aggression without naming any country. Xi Jinping says the Middle East war 'does not serve the common interests of the international community'.

A senior Iranian official says Monday's Oman-initiated meeting with Gulf states will discuss Hormuz but is not expected to yield a signed agreement, and that Iran still wants to charge ships fees, which Oman rejects. Bahrain's foreign ministry says it will not attend any collective meeting with Iran before diplomatic ties are restored.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Iranian official), Al Jazeera (AFP; Bahraini foreign ministry)

timeline.event: The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed US officials, reports that Chinese entities gave Iran satellite images of the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan before and after the July 17 strike that killed three US soldiers; Chinese officials asked for proof and did not acknowledge involvement.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (The Wall Street Journal)

timeline.event: Iraq temporarily closes the Shalamcheh, al-Shib and Mandali crossings into Iran after drone launch sites are found, an Iraqi security source says, and Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi approves an Iranian request for a joint investigation into the launch platforms. No group has claimed the pipeline attack.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Iraqi security source, Iraqi armed forces spokesman)

timeline.event: Saudi Civil Defence says a Houthi projectile wounded two people and damaged a mosque, buildings and vehicles in Jazan's al-Tuwal governorate; the Houthis say they targeted a Saudi base in Sharurah and accuse Saudi Arabia of 129 strikes on them in 48 hours. Claims from both sides are not independently verified.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Saudi Civil Defence, Houthi statements)

timeline.event: UKMTO says it received a report of a projectile hitting a vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz, with damage and crew status unknown; Al Jazeera reports an Iranian commercial vessel was attacked near Qeshm Island, killing one and wounding three, and quotes an Iranian official blaming the 'US terrorist enemy'. Not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UKMTO), Al Jazeera (Iranian official)

timeline.event: Al Jazeera reports the Houthis have seized Mayun (Perim) Island in the Bab al-Mandeb strait along with US-made military hardware left there; Djibouti's finance minister says about 1,400 Yemenis arrived in Obock within 24 hours. Houthi claims not independently verified.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (AFP; Djibouti finance ministry, Houthi statements)

timeline.event: Iraq says security forces located and seized a drone-launching platform in Maysan province near the Iranian border, which Saudi authorities had traced as the launch site of the East–West pipeline attack.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says Tehran is 'not at war with Saudi Arabia' and that the Houthis have 'their own issues', calling on regional countries to work together on peace and security.

Al Jazeera reports Yemeni government forces and Saudi Arabia carrying out air attacks to stop the Houthi advance around Mocha and the Bab al-Mandeb, with the humanitarian situation deteriorating; claims from both sides are not independently verified.

The BRICS summit in New Delhi closes with a declaration that avoids condemning the US-Israel war on Iran; analysts say Iran leaves without strong backing, though its delegation met the UAE's crown prince.

CNA reports the continued shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline threatens the loss of about 4 per cent of global oil supply as the Houthis tighten their grip on Red Sea shipping. CNA's estimate, not independently confirmed; Saudi Arabia has given no restart date.

Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree says Saudi Arabia carried out 58 air strikes on Houthi positions in 24 hours, after the group claimed a rare drone and missile attack on a military base in the kingdom; Almasirah reports strikes on Saada and a market in Al-Jawf. The Houthis have claimed more than 100 Saudi strikes since Sept 8; Riyadh has confirmed none.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Houthi military spokesman, Almasirah TV)

timeline.event: The IOM says displacement in Yemen has reached 85,818 people, up 10,000 in a day, with more than 82,000 displaced since the Houthi offensive began in early September; Taiz is worst hit with nearly 56,000 displaced, and more than 2,000 people have reached Djibouti.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; International Organization for Migration)

timeline.event: Trump says the US could stay in Iran and 'keep the oil', comparing it with the US push for a fifth of Venezuela's reserves, while repeating that he expects the war to end this year, possibly after the November midterms, and that Iran is 'calling constantly' for talks — a claim Tehran has previously dismissed.

Oman postpones the Sept 14 Salalah meeting at which Iran was to present an Omani-brokered plan for the Strait of Hormuz, citing 'the interests of consensus'; Fars says the delay was requested by some regional states and agreed jointly by Tehran and Muscat. It came hours after an attack on an Iranian cargo vessel in the strait that Iranian media said killed one person. No new date has been set.
timeline.source: CNA (AFP), The Straits Times, Al Jazeera (AP; Omani foreign ministry, Fars)

timeline.event: Oil prices jump as markets reopen with Saudi Arabia's 1,200km East–West pipeline still shut after the Sept 11 drone strikes; traders warn Riyadh will run out of export stocks within days without a restart, a loss of up to 4 per cent of global supply.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA (wire copy; Saudi traders)

timeline.event: Al Jazeera reports from Sanaa that Houthi fighters are advancing toward government-held Marib, the oil and gas province, and the city of Taiz, as fighting intensifies (Al Jazeera reporting; no independent confirmation of front-line positions).

Trump dismisses a Wall Street Journal report, citing unnamed US officials, that Iran obtained satellite images of a Jordan base from Chinese entities before July's attack that killed three US troops, saying 'we spy on them too'.
The Houthis say they fired dozens of missiles and drones at Saudi military targets; Saudi Civil Defence issues alerts in Khamis Mushait and Abha, and Iran denies involvement in Yemen's war.

The US blocks Iranian nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami from attending the IAEA General Conference by opposing a snapback-sanctions exemption; Iran says Austria revoked his visa and protests the 'politicisation' of the agency.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Iranian state TV)

timeline.event: The US Defense Department inspector general tells Congress the Iran campaign cost an estimated US$33.4 billion from 28 Feb to 30 Jun, including US$22.3 billion in munitions, and caused strategic inventory shortfalls.

US Central Command disputes the IRGC's claim that the tanker El Gaia struck a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, saying it was hit by an Iranian missile last month and a drone this weekend off Oman; Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei says there will be no talks with the US until Iran's demands are met.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (CENTCOM and IRGC claims attributed)

timeline.event: Yemeni officials say the Houthis launched a new wave of attacks on Saudi Arabia and are digging into positions on the Red Sea coast as Riyadh deliberates its response; the Gulf–Iran talks remain postponed.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (wire copy; Yemeni officials)

timeline.event: Saudi Arabia warns it will react “firmly” to the Houthis after ballistic-missile and drone attacks wound 13 civilians in the kingdom’s south.

China's foreign ministry says Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi will hold talks with Wang Yi in Beijing on Wednesday, as China seeks to mediate and a week before Xi Jinping is expected to meet Trump in Washington.

The Congressional Budget Office reports the six-month US war against Iran has cost US$38 billion through Aug 1 and projects it to rise about US$3 billion a month, adding roughly 0.5 per cent to inflation in the first quarter of 2027, with munitions stockpiles possibly taking five years to replenish. The CBO says the Defence Department did not cooperate with its auditors.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; CBO), CNA (AFP), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: Oman's Maritime Security Centre says two sailors are missing and 23 were rescued after the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia was attacked about 1.3 nautical miles north of the Musandam peninsula and caught fire in its engine room. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say the vessel struck naval mines; US Central Command says it was hit by an Iranian missile last month and by a drone at the weekend. The competing accounts are not independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC (Oman Maritime Security Centre; IRGC and CENTCOM claims attributed)

timeline.event: The UN refugee agency says more than 100,000 people have been internally displaced by the renewed fighting in Yemen, with thousands more crossing by sea to Djibouti, after Houthi forces routed Saudi-backed government troops along the Red Sea coast and tightened their hold on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; UNHCR, IOM)

timeline.event: BBC Verify satellite imagery shows the most significant damage from last week's strike on Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline is at a pumping station, with experts saying repairs could take more than a month; Saudi Arabia blames Iran-backed militias in Iraq. The US energy secretary says separately the pipeline should be back online within days.
timeline.source: BBC Verify, The Straits Times (wire copy)

timeline.event: A US official, speaking anonymously, says US Central Command has a task force in place to enhance intelligence sharing and planning support for Saudi forces facing Houthi attacks.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; unnamed US official)

timeline.event: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi backs Saudi calls for secure navigation in the Red Sea at a meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Cairo, according to the Egyptian presidency; Suez Canal revenues have fallen by about US$7 billion over two years.

Republican Representative Thomas Massie reads articles of impeachment against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on the floor of the US House, seeking to force a long-shot vote over the conduct of the Iran war.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Reuters copy), The Straits Times

timeline.event: Saudi-led coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki says air defences destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday before it entered prohibited airspace, calling the security of the holy sites a 'red line'. A Houthi military source, quoted by the group's SABA agency, denies threatening Mecca or other holy sites.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Saudi-led coalition and Houthi claims attributed)

timeline.event: Oman's Maritime Security Centre says two sailors are missing and 23 were rescued from the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia, which was being towed to an Omani port after a fire in its engine room; the IMO says at least 22 seafarers have been killed in 79 confirmed incidents in the Strait and the wider Middle East since the war began in late February.
timeline.source: BBC (Oman Maritime Security Centre, International Maritime Organization)

timeline.event: The Congressional Budget Office reports the Iran war cost the US Defence Department about US$38 billion as of 1 Aug, with monthly costs of US$2-3 billion or more; munitions replacement accounts for US$21.7 billion and the CBO estimates the US has used between half and two-thirds of its missile-defence interceptor inventory since June 2025. The Pentagon disputes the shortfall finding.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy), CNA (Congressional Budget Office)

timeline.event: BBC Verify publishes satellite imagery showing major damage to a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline; Kpler estimates repairs could take four to six weeks and that the closure could remove up to 3.6 million barrels a day from supply. Brent traded as high as US$108 a barrel.

Trading sources say Saudi Arabia has cancelled some September-loading crude cargoes to European customers and suspended loadings at the Red Sea port of Yanbu, sending Poland's Orlen to seek North Sea alternatives; Riyadh separately offers Asian refiners additional crude routed via Oman.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy), CNA (trading sources)

timeline.event: The Pentagon's inspector general confirms to Congress that the Iran war has left the US with munitions shortfalls.
timeline.source: BBC (US Department of Defense inspector general)

timeline.event: US officials tout American energy power at a G-20 energy meeting while avoiding discussion of the Iran war.

The US House passes a war powers resolution to end the Iran war for a third time; AP puts the vote at 220-204 with seven Republicans in favour. None of the resolutions has reached Trump, who is expected to veto.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (AP), The Guardian, The Hill

timeline.event: Five sources tell Reuters that US embassy staff met Houthi representatives in Muscat over the weekend, with the Houthis reportedly saying they will not attack US vessels and will spare all commercial shipping except Saudi ships; Vice-President Vance said on Monday the US is in direct contact with the group. Not independently confirmed.

Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree says Saudi warplanes carried out as many as 450 strikes on Yemen this week and claims a Saudi F-15 was shot down, offering no evidence; Saudi officials did not respond. The US bans its government employees from travelling within 20 miles of the Yemen border.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters; Houthi military media, US State Department)

timeline.event: China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi, hosting Iran's Abbas Araghchi in Beijing, urges Iran and the US to return to their June interim deal and take 'effective measures' to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The Guardian reports the weekend Muscat meeting between US officials and Houthi leaders as confirmed, and says it led Washington to decide against militarily backing Saudi Arabia against the Houthi advance; the Houthis told the US only Saudi-linked shipping is a target.

CBS publishes leaked, undated photos from service members showing a destroyed E-3 surveillance aircraft at Prince Sultan Air Base and heavy damage at Camps Buehring and Arifjan in Kuwait from Iranian strikes; the BBC has not independently verified them.

CENTCOM spokesman Capt. Tim Hawkins tells Al Jazeera the strait is open, that US forces have helped move more than 900 million barrels of crude since May and redirected over 100 blockade-running ships, and denies targeting civilians; Trump says the war is 'hopefully toward the end' and claims direct contact with Tehran, which Iran has not confirmed.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (US Central Command, Trump remarks)

timeline.event: Two officials tell AP that Saudi Arabia, short of interceptors, has asked France, Pakistan, Egypt and the UK for air-defence support as the coalition strikes Houthi positions around Mocha; the Houthis claim to have downed a Saudi F-15 over Marib and hit Khamis Mushait air base, claims not independently confirmed. The US bars government staff from within 30km of the Yemen border.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (AP; Houthi and Yemeni government statements), The Straits Times (Reuters)

timeline.event: Axios reports Trump will meet leaders or foreign ministers of the six Gulf Cooperation Council states on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Sept 22 to discuss the war's next steps; the White House did not comment.

A UN fact-finding mission says it has found grounds to believe the US committed war crimes in Iran and that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity; US officials say operations are conducted in line with the law of armed conflict.

The US State Department approves a US$24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth jets to Saudi Arabia and notifies Congress, saying it will not alter the regional military balance. Israel, the only current Middle East operator of the aircraft, has objected to the sale; congressional approval is still required and no delivery timeframe was given.
timeline.source: CNA (AFP; US State Department), The Straits Times

timeline.event: Five people are killed as Yemen's Houthis, the Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia trade strikes; Saudi Arabia says one person died as it intercepted a Houthi drone. The BBC verifies video showing the wreckage of a Saudi fighter jet shot down over Yemen.
Sources tell CNA that satellite imagery shows three pumping stations along Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline were hit in the recent attack — one more than previously thought.
timeline.source: CNA (Reuters; sources familiar with the assessment)

timeline.event: Russia and China vote down a resolution extending the mandate of the UN Security Council's independent panel of experts monitoring Iran sanctions; 11 members vote in favour and Pakistan and Somalia abstain. Moscow and Beijing argue all UN measures lapsed under the 2015 nuclear deal.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters; UN Security Council)

timeline.event: Italy prepares to deploy its navy to protect Italian-linked shipping amid tensions in the Bab el-Mandeb strait, and US Democrats move to block Trump's Saudi nuclear cooperation deal.
A US official says Washington will allow an Iranian delegation, including President Masoud Pezeshkian, to attend the UN General Assembly in New York next week, as the war passes the half-year mark.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it struck a Togo-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming the vessel attempted 'illegal passage'. The claim has not been independently verified and no casualty details were given.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (IRGC claim, not independently verified)

timeline.event: Trump tells Axios he is weighing a major decision on Iran, saying he is considering whether to 'annihilate' Iranian adversaries and that 'anything could happen'.

South Korean President Lee Jae-myung rules out any South Korean military involvement in the Middle East conflict, explicitly excluding a deployment to the Strait of Hormuz, and says US-North Korea talks remain possible.
Iran expels a Swedish diplomat in what it describes as a retaliatory move, and Al Jazeera reports Iran's nuclear chief was blocked from attending an IAEA conference in Vienna over US objections.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards say via IRNA that the Togo-flagged tanker Trend was targeted and detained after a fire broke out on board late on Thursday, calling it an attempted 'illegal passage'. UKMTO separately reports a vessel hit by an unknown projectile early on Friday. The IRGC account is not independently verified.

Aid agencies say about 115,000 people are on the move after a rapid Houthi advance, and the UN migration agency puts internal displacement at 112,000 with thousands crossing to Djibouti, as a civil war largely paused since the 2022 truce reignites.
Italy's minister calls for more warships to protect navigation in the Red Sea as attacks on shipping widen.

Sources tell CNA that three pumping stations along Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline were hit in the recent attack that shut the line, a fuller picture of damage that satellite imagery had already suggested.
Saudi Aramco tells European refiners it will not supply them with crude in October, sources say, after a drone attack shut the East-West pipeline last week.
The Washington Post reports at least 22 US military fatalities in the Iran war, exceeding the Pentagon's published count by at least four.
The US warns allies that deliveries of key missile and air-defence capabilities could be delayed by as much as five years because of munitions shortages.
Houthi authorities accuse Saudi Arabia of launching 26 strikes in 24 hours. The claim has not been independently verified and Riyadh has not confirmed it.
President Trump extends US sanctions on Iran, Al Jazeera reports.
The Straits Times reports Yemenis fleeing on foot from the advancing Houthi front, as displacement from the offensive continues.
JP Morgan tells the BBC it cannot reliably forecast oil prices because of the war, saying 'we simply don't know' how the conflict will move the market.
The UN Security Council condemns 'in the strongest terms' continued Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia.
South Korea and the United States discuss Seoul's role in the Middle East alongside an investment pact, days after President Lee Jae-myung ruled out any South Korean military deployment.
Saudi Arabia issues air-raid alerts for Riyadh, the first for the capital since the Houthis escalated their attacks, the BBC reports. Saudi authorities have not said what was intercepted.

A large plume of black smoke is seen near Riyadh's main airport after booms are heard in the city, hours after Saudi civil defence sent overnight alerts warning of potential aerial attack over Riyadh and Al-Kharj and then issued an all-clear. The Saudi government media office does not immediately comment. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree had said on Friday that the group foiled unspecified 'criminal attempts' in Sanaa, blaming Saudi Arabia and vowing a response.
A Saudi-led naval coalition prepares to secure Red Sea waterways, Al Jazeera reports, as attacks on shipping widen.
Turkiye revokes the operating licence of Iran's Bank Mellat in Istanbul.
Iran stages a show of force in Tehran during a mobilisation campaign, Al Jazeera reports.

Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command, says oil and liquefied natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz over the past two weeks reached their highest level in six months, that the strait's main transit lanes are clear of mines, and that US naval protection and mine clearance are 'paying off'.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan tells broadcaster NTV that Saudi Arabia may have unmet military needs because of the Houthi attacks and that Turkiye would consider how to help under the trilateral Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, adding that it is unacceptable for Riyadh to be dragged into the US-Iran war and that proposals to end the fighting have been passed to all sides.

The Houthis say they fired ballistic missiles and drones at Riyadh and at energy sites on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast. The Saudi-led coalition says air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired at the capital at dawn and thwarted attempts on Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu; Riyadh has not confirmed any further strikes or casualties. A column of black smoke was seen rising from fuel tanks near King Khalid International Airport and flights were briefly disrupted. The US State Department urged Americans in the region to expect possible flight cancellations.
timeline.source: BBC, Al Jazeera, CNA, The Straits Times (Saudi-led coalition, Houthi claims)

timeline.event: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, tells Al Jazeera that Tehran has conveyed conditions to Washington through Qatari mediators for ending the war - an end to the fighting on all fronts, release of Iran's frozen funds and an end to the naval blockade - and is awaiting President Trump's response. Washington has not publicly responded.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Iran's Supreme National Security Council)

timeline.event: The US State Department warns that the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis 'has the potential to escalate rapidly' and tells Americans to seriously reconsider travel to and through the region, after the first missile attack aimed at Riyadh since Yemen's war resumed. President Trump returns early from Camp David on Sept 19; the White House gives no explanation. The Houthis say they carried out two operations with ballistic and cruise missiles and drones against sites in Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu; the Saudi-led coalition says the missile was intercepted and the other attempts thwarted. The UN says the Houthis' recent offensive in Yemen has displaced more than 110,000 people.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; US State Department, Saudi-led coalition, Houthi claims)

timeline.event: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed and there will be no return to negotiations until Tehran's conditions are met and US commitments fulfilled. Al Jazeera lists the conditions security chief Mohsen Rezaei sent through Qatar: an end to the war on all fronts including Lebanon, release of frozen funds, an end to the US naval blockade, and an end to US attacks and interference. Washington has not publicly responded.

Iran's military central command says on state media that it has information a new attack by the US and its allies is being prepared, and warns any such strike would bring sustained retaliation against US bases and interests, with Washington's regional allies treated as parties to the conflict. It gives no details; the statement is an Iranian claim.

Fox News reports President Trump saying the Houthis 'have agreed not to fight the United States', that he is in 'deciding mode' on Iran and that 'big things will be happening in the not-so-distant future'. The remarks are relayed second-hand by a Fox reporter; the Houthis, who continue to attack Saudi Arabia, have not confirmed any understanding.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP, citing Fox News)

timeline.event: Qatar's prime minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, speaking in New York, calls the fallout of the war an 'earthquake', urges a regional security framework based on respect for sovereignty and says Doha is working to revive Iran-US talks.

The Statistical Center of Iran reports that the economy contracted 10.1 per cent year-on-year between late March and late June, the first full quarter of the war. The figure is the Iranian government's own.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Statistical Center of Iran)

timeline.event: Al Jazeera reports that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has left Tehran for the UN General Assembly with a stopover in Qatar, and that Trump told Fox News his options on Iran include further military action, economic pressure or a deal and that he would be open to meeting President Pezeshkian in New York. Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf says the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until Washington meets what Iran calls its commitments under an earlier agreement; Qatar's foreign ministry says it is carrying proposals between the two sides.

A spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards says any new US attack would be met with 'new weapons with new capabilities' and that Iran's targets 'will not necessarily be the same as before'. This is a statement by a party to the conflict; no new military action by either side was reported.

Houthi fighters push to seize strategic heights in Yemen that would cut the Red Sea coast off from areas held by Saudi-backed forces, following a media report that Trump called off US strikes on the group at the last minute. The Houthis said on Sept 19 they had fired on Riyadh; Saudi Arabia has not commented and the claims are not independently verified.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says that from Sept 23 'all the Iranian airlines will be shut down around the world' under US sanctions, warning that anyone refuelling, servicing or selling tickets for them will be cut off from the dollar system.

Britain agrees to a Saudi request for limited 'defensive' air-to-air refuelling of Saudi jets after the Houthis intensified attacks on the kingdom, Prime Minister Andy Burnham says; the EU's Kaja Kallas says the bloc's Red Sea mission needs more than 10 warships, up from about six.

Trump made no direct pledge of military support in a Sept 20 call with Yemen's President Rashad al-Alimi, who asked for US help against the Houthis, two sources familiar with the call said; the White House did not comment.

The World Food Programme says it is scaling up in Yemen, where the UN counts nearly 700 killed and more than 120,000 displaced by the Houthi advance along the Red Sea coast, with thousands more fleeing by boat to Djibouti.

Al Jazeera reports that the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency says a second vessel has been hit by 'debris from an unknown projectile' in the Strait of Hormuz, and that Iran's Revolutionary Guards say the US and Israel 'must accept withdrawal' from the region. Details of the vessel incident are not yet independently confirmed.

G7 foreign ministers, meeting informally on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, say Iran must 'end its arming of and support' for the Houthis, condemn 'in the strongest terms' the continued Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, and call on the group to stop attacks on shipping and return to the political process.

The Houthi-run Saba agency says Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on the Red Sea port of Mokha killed six civilians, including two children and a woman, and wounded eight; not independently verified and no coalition account reported.

Al Jazeera reports fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces for strategic mountains near the Red Sea coast, with Yemeni officials putting the toll of the renewed hostilities at least 674 killed and more than 158,000 displaced (higher than the UN's earlier count of nearly 700 killed and 120,000 displaced; tallies differ by source and date).

Oil rises for the first time in five sessions (Brent up 1.7 per cent to US$102.06 by mid-afternoon Singapore time) as traders await possible US-Iran contact at the UN, after more supplies moved through the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend; Trump has said he is open to meeting President Pezeshkian in New York this week.

A senior Iranian official tells Kyodo News that Tehran has offered, through mediators, to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps to ease military pressure, with talks to follow on a permanent end to hostilities; another senior official later tells Reuters the strait could reopen within days if the US lifts its port blockade and calls the UN gathering a 'golden opportunity', though no Trump-Pezeshkian meeting is scheduled and Washington has not responded publicly.

UNHCR says the upsurge in fighting in Yemen, where Houthi forces have advanced along the Red Sea coast, has displaced more than 130,000 people in September, with projections of 100,000 more within three months, some fleeing by boat to Djibouti and Somalia; its Yemen plan is under 20 per cent funded.

Trump tells the UN General Assembly he faces a 'big decision' on striking Iran again or pursuing peace, warns he could 'annihilate the Islamic Republic' without a deal, predicts an agreement after the Nov 3 midterms and urges countries to isolate Iran economically; a Revolutionary Guards spokesman says Iran has toughened its conditions for ending the war since the June memorandum collapsed.

Trump says envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held a 'very good, very productive' three-hour meeting with Iran's delegation in New York and that another meeting is scheduled 'in the very near future'; neither side gives details. Qatar's emir tells the UN the Gulf is in 'one of the most dangerous phases' and can only be resolved diplomatically.

Saudi King Salman calls the Houthis a 'terrorist militia' and accuses them of repeatedly targeting Mecca, calling it a 'heinous crime' (Saudi Press Agency; targeting not independently verified); Putin and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman call for safe passage through Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb and a swift halt to fighting in Yemen, the Kremlin says.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Saudi Press Agency), The Straits Times (Reuters, Kremlin)

timeline.event: US and Iranian officials hold their first talks since the June ceasefire collapsed, mediated by Qatar on the UN sidelines and involving Foreign Minister Araghchi and envoy Witkoff; no breakthrough is reported, Witkoff says a round was completed 'that we hope will prove constructive and promising', and Iran repeats its demand that the US end its 'acts of aggression'. Al Jazeera reports the sides differ on whether they met directly, with Witkoff describing mediators shuttling between delegations, and that Tehran ties progress to lifting shipping blockades and unfreezing assets; President Pezeshkian arrives in New York for the assembly.

ST (Reuters) reports the first US-Iran shuttle talks in months raised hopes of progress although neither side spelled out any change in position; Araghchi and envoys Witkoff and Kushner communicated through mediators on the UN sidelines. Iranian airlines cancel flights to Baghdad, Muscat, Qatar, Georgia and Azerbaijan after US Treasury sanctions on Iran's aviation industry announced on Sept 21 take effect, a Tehran travel agent tells AFP; routes to China remain. Al Jazeera notes Trump's 'annihilate' warning was met by Tehran's promise of a 'crushing' response even as both sides talked.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters, AFP), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: Pezeshkian tells the General Assembly Iran will never 'bend the knee', accuses the US of 'terrorism' for killing Khamenei and says any deal must end the US blockade of Iranian shipping through Hormuz; the US delegation walks out. Iranian authorities put civilian deaths from the strikes at more than 175, two thirds children (Tehran's figure). Al Jazeera reports US aviation sanctions on 27 airlines are pushing Iranians to overland routes.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (AFP), CNA (Reuters), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: A letter from acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao to Senator Kirsten Gillibrand says eight sailors in the USS Abraham Lincoln strike group attempted suicide during its more than 300-day deployment for the Iran war; the Navy denies a mental health crisis aboard the carrier, which is returning home.

Yahya Rahim Safavi, adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, says the war could expand 'to the Indian Ocean and perhaps beyond' if the US attacks again, the first explicit mention of the Indian Ocean by a Khamenei adviser.
The India-bound bulk carrier Cape Dao is attacked off Oman; Al Jazeera reports it was struck twice by projectiles and set on fire, killing a crew member. The attacker was not identified.

The Saudi-led coalition says it shot down six missiles fired by the Houthis at Taif and Yanbu after brief civil-defence alerts including Mecca; Greek sources say a Greek-operated Patriot battery downed a ballistic missile and a drone near Yanbu.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera, CNA (AFP), The Straits Times (Reuters)

timeline.event: Iran threatens neighbours with retaliation for enforcing new US sanctions on its airlines; Georgia and Azerbaijan suspend Iranian flights and Iranian media say the UAE has barred them too.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera, The Straits Times (Iranian media)

timeline.event: Senate Democrats tee up a vote, possibly on Sept 24 US time, on a war powers resolution requiring Trump to end the Iran war or get Congress' authorisation, as some Republicans break ranks before the midterms.

US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased path out of the war in which Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifts its economic blockade and possibly unfreezes assets, according to two Iranian sources, two regional officials and two Western diplomats speaking to Reuters; neither side wants to give up leverage first.

Some 80 countries, in a joint statement read by Bahrain's foreign minister at the UN, demand the urgent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and condemn Iranian and Houthi attacks, warning that Houthi advances near Bab el-Mandeb raise the risk to global trade.

Saudi Arabia intercepts Houthi ballistic missiles after warnings for several regions including Mecca; President Macron says France will send 'military means' to help shield the Yanbu oil terminal. Fighting between the Houthis and Riyadh-backed forces in Yemen kills dozens on both sides, according to an AFP tally from seven sources.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian tells Fox News that Tehran does 'not wish to continue' and that 'it's America that must choose whether it wants to end this or not', a day after telling the UN Iran would never surrender to US pressure.

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband tells Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in New York that the UK 'will not tolerate intimidation, threats or hostile activity on UK soil' from Iranian-linked groups, Sky News reports, citing the Foreign Office.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan announce an urgent meeting of their chiefs of staff under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement after Houthi missile fire on the kingdom; the Saudi Grand Mufti tells troops to be ready to die fighting the Houthis. Brent closes above US$106.50 after the Houthis claim strikes on Aramco facilities.

Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi says Tehran has proposed a seven-day roadmap: a region-wide cessation of hostilities including Lebanon, after which the Strait of Hormuz reopens within seven days and talks begin; passed via mediators with Qatar carrying messages. Washington has not said whether it accepts.

Turkish and Pakistani military chiefs travel to Riyadh for the urgent Mecca-pact meeting on the Houthi attacks; Turkey's parliament speaker says the pact could broaden to the wider Muslim world including Iran and goes to ratification from next month.
US ambassador to China David Perdue says Trump told Xi at the White House that Chinese help for Iran is unacceptable.

Iraq's Baghdad, Najaf, Erbil and Sulaimaniyah airports suspend Iranian flights after new US aviation sanctions; Iran warns that blocking its flights could bring similar restrictions on other countries in the region.

Pakistan's prime minister Shehbaz Sharif tells the UN General Assembly that a Houthi attack on Mecca or Medina would cross a 'red line', as Pakistani, Saudi and Turkish military chiefs meet on the Mecca pact.
An Iranian official tells Reuters that Tehran will make no nuclear concessions even if the US accepts its plan to reopen Hormuz.

Araghchi says 'the choice now rests with the United States' on the seven-day plan, delivered via Qatar; a US official tells the BBC that positive discussions are under way through mediators, including on nuclear issues.

Trump and Xi discuss the Middle East war at their summit; Xi urges the US and Iran to return to the June framework that produced the short-lived ceasefire, according to Xinhua, and Trump again warns Xi against helping Iran.

Iran awaits an official US response to its seven-day plan after the Wall Street Journal reports that Trump has rejected it; Araghchi says acceptance would start a seven-day countdown to reopening Hormuz, and Tehran has also engaged Saudi Arabia on the strait.
The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted two Houthi drones launched towards Riyadh early on Saturday; civil defence had issued overnight alerts for Khamis Mushait and Abha.

Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council chair Rashad al-Alimi calls a general mobilisation and offers amnesty to Houthi defectors, his first speech since government forces were routed from the western Red Sea coast.

President Pezeshkian tells Al Jazeera Iran 'no longer trusts' negotiations with the US after past talks were followed by attacks and sanctions, and says Qatar and Pakistan are relaying its messages while it awaits a reply to the seven-day plan

The Guardian, citing the WSJ's unnamed US officials, reports Trump is privately sceptical Iran would dismantle its nuclear programme and has told aides he expects to resume bombing after the November midterms; he posts a map renaming the strait the 'Trump Strait' (unconfirmed by the White House)

Trump tells reporters he has rejected Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end fighting, saying Tehran wants a deal 'because they're losing so badly'; Araghchi says Iran will await an official response via mediators.
China's Vice-President Han Zheng tells the UN General Assembly the sovereignty of Gulf countries should be respected, without naming the US.
Saudi Arabia's foreign minister uses his UNGA address to accuse Iran of 'flagrant attacks' on civilian and economic targets and calls for condemnation of Houthi threats to Red Sea shipping.
Iraq opens direct talks with Washington to exempt some of its airports from the new US measures on Iranian airline flights, after four Iraqi airports suspended Iran flights.
US Treasury Secretary Bessent says envoys were sent worldwide to press governments to isolate Iran economically, citing Turkey and Oman halting Mahan Air flights.
Foreign Minister Araqchi says any reopening of the strait is contingent on Iran's conditions being met and that 'only a negotiated solution' can break the deadlock.

Foreign Minister Araghchi says Iran is waiting for a 'definitive' US response through the mediators after Trump's rejection, that only a 'negotiated solution' can end the conflict, and that the reopening terms are those of the June US-Iran memorandum; Trump says the US already has 'total control' of the strait.
Schools across Riyadh are told to switch to remote learning for a week at short notice, with no official reason given, amid near-daily Houthi drone and missile launches towards Saudi Arabia.

With its southern ports under US naval blockade, Iran is pushing oil exports and imports north through Caspian Sea ports such as Anzali, Al Jazeera reports from Tehran; the route's capacity is a fraction of the Gulf's.

Trump tells Axios he expects talks with Iran to resume in the coming week even though he has rejected Tehran's seven-day truce-and-reopening plan for the Strait of Hormuz: 'They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make.' Foreign Minister Araghchi says Iran is fully prepared for war if strikes resume.
timeline.source: CNA (Reuters), The Straits Times (Reuters), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: British counter-terror police arrest five men on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act and explosives offences after three vehicles head towards RAF Fairford, the base used by US aircraft for strikes on Iran; homes in Whelford are evacuated and Trump says the men wanted to do 'big damage'. Police have not linked the case to Iran.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Iran is open to 'real diplomacy' but ready for an 'apocalyptic war' if the US attacks, in a social-media warning posted after Washington rejected Tehran's seven-day roadmap to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz; Trump has said he expects talks to resume this week.

Iran's IRNA, citing an unnamed source, says the UN delegation in New York has no plans to negotiate with the US, that its positions went to Washington through a Qatari mediator, and that it returns to Tehran on Tuesday; Brent nears US$108 in Asian trading after Trump's rejection of Tehran's seven-day Hormuz reopening plan.

British counter-terror police question the five men held near RAF Fairford, the base used for US strikes on Iran, on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences; a local councillor says there was a specific Iranian threat against the base about six weeks ago. No charges yet.
US and Iranian officials speak separately to mediators about an amended version of Iran's seven-day truce proposal; Araghchi says Iran expects Washington's final response through Qatar.
Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei says on state TV that the US will be forced out of the Middle East after 'painful blows'; he has not been seen in public since the war began.

A source says the US Treasury will grant a one-month sanctions waiver letting Iraqi Airways fly pilgrims between Iran and Najaf, after Iraq halted Iran flights on Friday; Al Jazeera reports the flights resumed as Tehran protested US curbs.

Araghchi meets Qatari mediators in New York on Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran conditions on a seven-day region-wide ceasefire; a US official tells Al Jazeera there will be no deal to end the war unless Iran's nuclear programme is addressed.

Rubio and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan hold talks in Washington on Yemen and Hormuz, as the Iran-backed Houthis press an offensive on the Red Sea coast after striking Saudi airports and oil sites.
Trump calls a report that he offered Iran sanctions relief and access to frozen funds a 'hoax'; Bloomberg-sourced reporting says Iranian officials privately doubt a deal before the Nov 3 US midterms.
US forces are set to leave their last bases in Iraq by Sept 30 under a 2024 agreement; Iran and its allies hail it as a victory, and Iraqi analysts say it could give Tehran a freer hand.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards publish a 25-page open letter urging US midterm voters to reject Trump's policies and accept coexistence, as Tehran awaits a US reply on its Hormuz plan.

Rubio tells Fox News the suspected plot near RAF Fairford, a British base hosting US bombers flying missions against Iran, involved 'the hands of a foreign actor'; UK police have released the five suspects on bail.
Italy completes the withdrawal of its last troops from Iraq, ending a 12-year presence; Italian and NATO forces had agreed with local authorities to leave by Sept 30.
Iran's chief negotiator warns that if Iran cannot sell oil 'no one else will' and 'no infrastructure will remain safe', as Tehran awaits a formal US reply on its Hormuz plan.
The US Treasury sanctions 10 individuals and entities, some in China, Hong Kong and Pakistan, for allegedly helping Iran procure weapons.
UK counter-terrorism police say no explosive devices were found in vans seized near RAF Fairford, only a quantity of petrol.
UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour visits Saudi Arabia for the first time since last year's rift, as Houthi missiles and drones target the kingdom; Saudi Arabia resumes oil loadings at Yanbu.
Trump says he does not know if Iran will 'give up yet' but that the war will end 'very soon', without giving details.
US forces withdraw from their remaining bases in Iraq, including Baghdad, under the 2024 agreement.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards urge Americans to vote out Trump's allies in Congress as US forces leave Iraq; Qatar continues its shuttle diplomacy and Trump again predicts a swift Iranian surrender.

The latest US sanctions over Iranian weapons procurement cover 13 individuals and entities in Russia, Hong Kong, China and Pakistan, including Russia's MG-Flot and the Yakovlev design bureau, the Kyiv Independent reports, citing Reuters.
Somali pirates kill five crew on the hijacked tanker MT Honour 25, officials say; analysts link the revival of Somali piracy partly to the effects of the war on Iran.
Oil falls below US$90 a barrel on hopes of an eventual US-Iran deal, Saudi Arabia's restoration of about half of its East-West pipeline capacity and a US order to release more emergency reserves.

Iran says the official US response to its proposal to end the war was presented to President Pezeshkian by Foreign Minister Araghchi at a cabinet meeting; the contents are not disclosed (IRNA, via AFP).
The Times reports that one of the five men arrested near RAF Fairford, the UK base used by US bombers, had called police shortly beforehand; police have not confirmed this.
The last US and British troops leave Iraq, including about 100 UK personnel from Irbil, ending Operation Inherent Resolve.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham says there are 'strong indications' Iran played a part in the RAF Fairford incident; Iran denies it.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman says the kingdom will not compromise on its security in the face of Houthi attacks and will respond firmly to any threat, while pursuing de-escalation.

Trump tells reporters the US faces a choice to either make a deal with Iran or 'blow them up'; Hegseth tells commanders at Quantico that US forces have 'destroyed' Iran's navy, air force and defence systems (US claims).
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Britain is 'barking up the wrong tree' after Prime Minister Burnham linked Iran to the RAF Fairford incident; Burnham gave no details of the evidence.
Netanyahu tells Fox News that Israel warned Britain that Iran was planning an attack on an airbase
Trump says Iran was likely involved in the flydubai cockpit attack and will be 'hit very hard' if so; no link has been established.
UK counter-terrorism police arrest a dual UK-Iranian national on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts in the RAF Fairford investigation.
The US Treasury sanctions Iran's rail and auto sectors and their foreign suppliers under 'Operation Economic Outcast'.
The Saudi-led coalition says a Houthi drone attack on Tuesday knocked out a transformer at a Medina power station serving the Prophet's Mosque.

A US official tells Al Jazeera three carriers and two landing groups are deploying around Iran, including 2,000 Marines; UKMTO says a supertanker was hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire.
Yemen's government says its warplanes carried out 20 strikes on Houthi forces in Taiz in three hours; the Houthis have denied the Madinah power-station attack.
Iran's foreign ministry urges Iraq to lift restrictions on flights to Iran imposed under US sanctions; Najaf-Iran flights had restarted on Monday, Iraqi state media said.
EU states hold an emergency meeting on diesel prices after Washington urged Europe to release reserves and Trump threatened a US export ban.
A US official tells Al Jazeera the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and a Marine unit are heading to the region; the WSJ reports 9,000 to 10,000 more troops in total.
G7 leaders hold a video call on fuel prices convened by Macron, after the EU pushed back against US threats of a diesel export ban.
The wounded flydubai captain says he forced the cockpit door open during the co-pilot's attack to stop the plane going down.
WFP says a record number of people in Yemen's government-held areas cannot meet their food needs as Saudi-Houthi fighting escalates.
The G7 agrees to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel and to avoid energy export curbs on one another; Trump says a US diesel export ban is off the table.
A tanker leaving the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz is hit by an 'unknown projectile', causing a small fire and blackout but no casualties, UKMTO says.
Netanyahu says the flydubai co-pilot was radicalised and warns of a 'very heavy price' if any power sent him, without offering evidence; Israeli officials are expected to question him in the UAE.

Officials tell Reuters Saudi Arabia is planning an offensive against the Houthis to secure the Red Sea route; Pakistan says the Mecca pact will hold emergency talks in Riyadh on Iran's suggestion of political engagement with the Houthis.
WFP says 74% of households in government-held parts of Yemen it can reach lack enough food after weeks of fighting.
Iraq clears Iranian airlines for 40 daily flights to Najaf after the US granted an exemption from its sanctions on Iran's aviation sector.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (AFP, Reuters), The Straits Times

timeline.event: Yemen's government forces say 474 attacks in 24 hours killed or wounded 1,540 Houthi fighters and the Saudi-led coalition intercepted three ballistic missiles fired at southern Saudi Arabia; the Houthi figures are unverified.

The UAE's prosecutor general says the flydubai co-pilot used a crash axe on the captain and tried to take the flight controls in an attempted 'terrorist act'; media report Oman had earlier barred him from flying over extremist views.

Loud explosions are reported in Houthi-held Sanaa as Yemen's military spokesman says government forces struck Houthi positions across the country and closed a key crossing between al-Houban and Taiz city; the claims are not independently verified.

Iran says it has executed Siavash Jamshidi, convicted of firing a military-grade weapon at police during the anti-government protests that peaked in January; authorities have stepped up executions linked to the unrest and the war.

Two Iranian nationals appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court charged with preparing a bomb attack on Manchester's Jewish community, allegedly at the behest of a figure believed to be based in Iran; separately, a UK-Iranian man arrested over the RAF Fairford incident is released on bail.

Portugal's Prosecutor General's Office opens an investigation into whether the government lawfully authorised US use of the Lajes Air Base in the Azores during the Iran war, after a complaint from the Left Bloc.
