The Houthis' Al-Masirah TV says Saudi aircraft struck Sanaa 26 times, and an AFP journalist in Riyadh reports flames and smoke at an oil facility on the city's outskirts; Saudi Arabia has not commented on either.

Yemen's government-aligned armed forces say they are striking 'vital targets' in Sanaa and the Houthi stronghold of Saada; Al Jazeera reports that the fighting is displacing more civilians and that Donald Trump said of Iran, 'it'll either be the easy way or the hard way'.

The Houthis say they hit an Aramco facility in Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones on 3 Oct, which the Saudi-led coalition calls 'misleading'. The coalition says it then carried out 97 strikes on Houthi reinforcements on the Tor al-Baha front and around Taiz, and Yemen's government forces claim 700 Houthis were killed in 24 hours; none of the claims has been independently verified.
The US State Department says it has expelled two members of Iran's UN General Assembly delegation who stayed in New York after being ordered to leave on 28 Sep.

Iran's parliament speaker and top negotiator Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf says the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until seven conditions based on the 'Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding' are met; the US replied to Iran's seven-day reopening proposal last week via Qatari intermediaries.

Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi announces the start of a major military operation to retake territory held by the Houthis, after officials told Reuters that Saudi Arabia would lead the air campaign with Yemeni ground forces.
Iran's oil minister Mohsen Paknejad resigns and National Iranian Oil Company chief Hamid Bovard is appointed acting minister, the president's office says, amid the US blockade of Iranian oil exports.

The US withdraws all 12 B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in England after commanders receive new threats about an Iran-backed plot against the base, two US officials say; US European Command confirms the redeployment but does not comment on any warnings.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, Al Jazeera, CNA

timeline.event: More than 70 people die in fighting around Taiz as the Houthis cut the city off from Aden, sources on both sides say, as the Yemeni government's offensive begins; the Houthis say they struck Saudi Aramco sites again.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says there is 'no military solution' to the conflict with the US but that Tehran is ready to return to war.

Ship-tracking firm Kpler's provisional data show Middle East crude exports above pre-war levels on four days in the last week of September; IRGC commander Ali Fadavi says only 3-4 million barrels a day move through the US-supervised route and claims no US vessels remain in the Gulf. Iranian claims not independently verified.

Yemen's government says its forces have secured effective control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait after seizing positions around Dhubab with Saudi air support, and announces an offensive towards Sanaa; the Houthis call the claims 'completely untrue', and government military sources say the Houthis have cut a road near Taiz, leaving government forces there besieged. Claims from both sides not independently verified.

US and Israeli reports say the flydubai co-pilot who attacked his captain planned to crash the plane into Tel Aviv's Ben Gurion airport or a tower block; Downing Street says RAF Fairford is safe after the US bomber withdrawal.
Yemen's military says government forces captured the Red Sea city of Mokha with Saudi air support; unnamed government and military sources tell Reuters and AFP they have only reached its outskirts.

The Houthis say they struck Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, an Aramco refinery in Rabigh, Abha airport and the Khamis Mushait base; the claims are unverified and Saudi Arabia does not comment, though explosions are heard in Riyadh.
Turkey and Pakistan agree with Saudi Arabia on a 'rapid deployment' of troops to the kingdom under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, citing attacks on Mecca and Medina.
Trump says 'threats' he believes are linked to Iran led the US to pull its B-1 bombers out of RAF Fairford.

The Saudi-led coalition says it has destroyed Houthi targets on Yemen's Red Sea coast as the Houthis repeat claims of strikes on Riyadh's airport; the UN says the Yemen fighting has displaced more than 184,000 people.

The Houthis deny losing territory on the Red Sea coast and claim an attack on Riyadh's main airport; Saudi Arabia's aviation authority says three people were hurt in attacks on the Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border. Neither side's battlefield claims can be independently verified.
British counter-terrorism police arrest a 22-year-old British man in London in their investigation into a suspected plot near RAF Fairford, the base the US used for Iran strikes.
India says 12 crew, 11 of them Indian, were injured when the Panama-flagged tanker MT On Peace was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz; the injured are being treated in Oman.
Two US officials tell Reuters a suspected Iran-linked plot for a complex drone attack on RAF Fairford led the US to move its B-1 bombers out of the base; Iran denies involvement.

Saudi-backed Yemeni forces say they have taken the highest peak in Taiz's Jabal Habashi district; the Houthis say they thwarted an advance towards the Bab al-Mandab. Neither claim is independently verified.
Oman's air force evacuates 10 injured crew members of the tanker On Peace to hospital in Khasab; Oman's defence ministry says the vessel was struck 9 nautical miles off the port of Limah.

Yemen's government says the Houthis fired at least two ballistic missiles and several drones at Aden airport, forcing a flight from Cairo to divert to Jeddah; the Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile north of Riyadh.

Turkey is sending mainly defensive and technical support to Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, two officials say, after Turkey and Pakistan pledged to act on the collective-defence commitment of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement.

The International Organization for Migration says more than 200,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces began in early September, up from 76,000 in mid-September.
Maritime security sources tell Reuters that attacks and harassment of tankers in the Strait of Hormuz were at their highest last week of any week since the war began.

Saudi Arabia says three people were killed and 36 wounded at Abha and King Khalid airports after the Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes; the Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed the launch platform.
UKMTO says a tanker was hit by multiple projectiles 94km north of Qatar's Madinat ash Shamal, with casualties reported; it did not give numbers.
Yemen's internationally recognised government says its counter-offensive has 'neutralised' 1,860 Houthi fighters in 2,103 strikes; the claim has not been independently verified.
Blasts over Riyadh send diplomats into shelters and schools into basements as the Houthis claim a ballistic-missile attack on King Khalid airport.
A US official and a Syrian defence official tell Reuters Syria may deploy troops to help Saudi Arabia fight the Houthis; neither government has confirmed it.
The US Treasury sanctions 17 vessels and associated networks moving Iranian oil under 'Operation Economic Outcast'.
Trump says the US will not attack Iran before the 3 Nov midterm elections and calls talks with Tehran productive.
Lufthansa Group suspends Riyadh flights to 16 Oct and Air India to 10 Oct as the Houthis renew threats against airlines after claiming a strike on the capital's airport.
Putin tells Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan that Russia will 'do everything' to help end the war, Russian news agencies report.
Iranian media report 'massive explosions' in the southern Strait of Hormuz, with Fars citing unnamed military sources; no independent confirmation.

Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority says three Saudi nationals, including a Saudia pilot, were killed in two Houthi attacks on Riyadh's airport, which has since reopened; several airlines suspend Riyadh flights and Singapore's foreign ministry condemns the strikes.
timeline.source: BBC, Al Jazeera, The Straits Times

timeline.event: EASA widens the area of Saudi airspace it tells airlines to avoid, saying recent attacks show the Houthis' ability and intent to strike deeper inside Saudi territory.
Iran's President Pezeshkian says peace talks can only succeed without 'pressure and threats'; diplomacy to end the seven-month war has been at an impasse since the summer.

UN envoy Hans Grundberg tells the Security Council that Yemen has slid back into 'full-scale war'; Yemen's government claims more than 2,750 strikes on the Houthis in 24 hours, not independently verified.

The Kremlin says Trump welcomed Russia's involvement in efforts to reach an Iran settlement; Iran's IRGC claims a strike on an LPG carrier south of the Strait of Hormuz, without independent confirmation.
Organisers of two major Saudi conferences say they will go ahead after missile attacks on Riyadh's airport killed four people this week; the UK, France and Germany have told citizens to avoid Riyadh.

An attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport kills 12 people and injures 309, the Saudi civil aviation authority says; the Saudi-led coalition blames the Houthis, calls it a 'war crime' and vows to respond, and a projectile also falls near Dammam's airport. The Houthis had not claimed it by Saturday evening.

Yemen's government military claims its forces killed at least 1,150 Houthi fighters in almost 2,000 operations over 24 hours and are advancing; the claim is not independently verified. Al Jazeera reports Houthi threats against Pakistan if it joins the fighting on Saudi Arabia's side.

US Central Command says a US fighter jet struck the Panama-flagged cargo ship M/V Ocean Molica (also known as Arika Sun) in the Gulf of Oman, disabling its propulsion without harming the crew, after it ignored warnings and tried to run the naval blockade of Iran on leaving an Iranian port.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (AFP), The Straits Times (Reuters) - CENTCOM statement

timeline.event: UN Secretary-General Guterres and governments including Egypt and Qatar condemn the Riyadh airport attack that Saudi Arabia blames on the Houthis; Trump calls it 'terrible' and says he will speak to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

Yemen's government health ministry warns of an 'imminent health and humanitarian catastrophe' in besieged Taiz, saying medicines, IV fluids and fuel at hospitals are nearly depleted; it blames the Houthi siege.

The Houthis warn airlines, travellers and airport workers to stay away from Saudi airports and airspace, except in Mecca and Medina, without claiming the Riyadh attack; the Saudi-led coalition calls that attack a 'full-fledged war crime' and Saudi Arabia vows to 'firmly' retaliate.

A projectile hits Terminal 4 of Riyadh's King Khalid airport, killing a Pakistani resident and injuring 11, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority says; the toll from Saturday's strike rises to 13 dead and 308 injured. The FAA tells US airlines to exercise caution over Saudi Arabia until 10 Dec.

Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei says the US reply, sent via Qatari intermediaries, to Iran's seven-condition proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz is 'insufficient', Iranian state media report.

In a call with Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi offers to mediate between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, saying the region's conflicts have no military solution, according to his office.
Australia and New Zealand warn their citizens against travel to Saudi Arabia after the Houthi attacks on Riyadh's airport, joining the US, Canada, the UK, South Korea and Japan.

Saudi Arabia extends the closure of Riyadh's King Khalid airport after the two Houthi strikes, and its energy minister vows a 'serious' response; Malaysia advises citizens to postpone Umrah trips and China condemns the attacks.
Iran says it is still reviewing the US reply to its Strait of Hormuz proposal and will answer through intermediaries once the review is complete.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham tells Parliament the suspected plot against RAF Fairford, which US bombers used for strikes on Iran, was 'highly likely' coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by the IRGC; Al Jazeera reports Britain sanctioned two Iranian nationals, and Iran's ambassador denies any involvement.

The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted another Houthi ballistic missile fired at Riyadh on Monday night and two aimed at Khamis Mushait; the Houthis say they targeted King Khalid airport, which a notice to airmen shows will stay closed until 17 Oct.

Trump writes on Truth Social that he does not believe China and Russia are helping Iran 'at all', saying they have 'too much to lose'; he had earlier warned it 'would be very bad for them' if they did.

The IMF forecasts the Middle East and Central Asia economy will contract 0.3% in 2026, citing prolonged disruption to Strait of Hormuz shipping, with Kuwait, Iraq and Qatar facing contractions of about 16%.
MI5 Director General Ken McCallum says Iran is pursuing 'harder targets, like military sites' in Britain this year, without discussing the RAF Fairford case; Iran denies hostile acts in the UK.
Singapore's foreign ministry advises against all travel to Saudi Arabia, citing missile and drone attacks on airports in Riyadh, Abha, Dammam, Khamis Mushait, Najran and Jizan in recent weeks.

The Saudi-led coalition strikes the Houthi-run Yemen Petroleum Company's al-Sabaha fuel depot near Sanaa; coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki says missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh and other cities were intercepted.
Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry says an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran was attacked late on 13 Oct, causing a limited fire with no injuries.
Trump says the Houthis, 'probably at the behest of Iran', are attacking Saudi Arabia to push up energy prices before the US midterms, and warns he 'will never forget' the attacks.

Two senior Iranian officials tell Reuters Tehran is using new tactics against Strait of Hormuz shipping to keep oil prices high ahead of the US midterms; Singapore's MUIS advises citizens to postpone umrah trips to Saudi Arabia.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters), The Straits Times (MUIS)

timeline.event: Singapore's MPA says the Singapore-flagged GFS Pride sank after a projectile strike on 13 Oct and the GFS Giselle was damaged on 14 Oct; all crew are safe. Security data show at least ten vessels attacked in or near Hormuz since 11 Oct, the most since the war began.
Netanyahu says he does not favour a pre-emptive strike on Iran before Israel's 27 Oct election, while warning Tehran and its proxies against attacking Israel.

CNN reports that the US military is planning for possible use of the GBU-43/B 'Mother of All Bombs' against Iranian energy and nuclear sites if Trump renews combat; officials have questioned its effectiveness.
The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a cruise missile in the Medina region; the Houthis deny targeting it.

Houthi missiles hit Aden's presidential palace, killing five and injuring 16, Yemen's government says; the Houthis say they struck a Saudi military headquarters. The UN Security Council condemns 'escalatory' Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on Riyadh's airport.
The UN Security Council condemns 'escalatory' Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on Riyadh's airport, which has been targeted 20 times since the start of October.
Top Pentagon officials plan to delay the report on the US strike on a school in Minab, which killed more than 150 people on the war's first day, until after the 3 Nov midterms.

BBC Verify counts 12 vessels reporting attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz in the week to 11 Oct, the most in any week of the war, based on UKMTO reports; four more have been reported this week.
Iran has exported some LPG and jet fuel since July despite the US naval blockade by hiding cargoes among ship-to-ship transfers off Oman, maritime security sources tell Reuters.
Trump tells Newsmax the US 'may have to' strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site, and rules out using a nuclear weapon or ground troops.
A UK court sentences Norwegian teenager Johannes Natland to 20 years for a murder plot; prosecutors say he was recruited by the Iran-linked Foxtrot Network.

Houthi missiles hit Aden airport, Yemeni officials say; the Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a ballistic missile over the oil port of Yanbu plus cruise missiles and drones. The UN Security Council condemns the attacks on Saudi Arabia, and Iran denies a Saudi accusation of involvement.

UKMTO says at least 12 vessels were attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz in the week to 16 Oct, one of which sank, and that most attacked ships do not report; a tanker reports an RPG strike from a small boat north-east of Saudi Arabia's Jubail.

Egypt's President Sisi asks parliament for an emergency session to authorise helping defend Saudi Arabia from the Houthis if asked; the Saudi-led coalition says it downed four drones over Riyadh, the Eastern Province and the south, and Houthi media say Saudi strikes killed at least 12 in Taiz and Dhamar, a claim not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters, AFP), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: Iran's IRGC says a supertanker struck a naval mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran's navy says another tanker caught fire in the Sea of Oman; both are Iranian claims, not independently verified.

Iran's IRNA says the two tankers the IRGC reported mined and on fire in the Strait of Hormuz each carried about 2 million barrels and had switched off their positioning systems; their names have not been released.
The Saudi-led coalition says a reconnaissance helicopter crashed in Najran from a technical fault, killing two crew; the Houthis say they shot down a Saudi Apache.
Foreign Minister Araqchi says Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, conditional on the US lifting its port blockade and oil sanctions, is still on the table.
Iran's parliament approves Mehrdad Akhlaghi as defence minister with 237 votes, replacing Aziz Nasirzadeh, who was killed in the 28 Feb US-Israeli strike.

Egypt's National Defence Council says it is ready to give Saudi Arabia 'all necessary and possible support' against Houthi attacks; Riyadh's Kingdom Centre orders mandatory remote work for office tenants.

The GCC condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia; Riyadh's Kingdom Centre orders remote working after drone interceptions, Egypt's parliament postpones its vote on military support for Riyadh to 19 Oct, and Iran's new defence minister threatens 'enormous damage' if the US resumes strikes.
Four government and medical sources tell Reuters a Houthi attack with three ballistic missiles on a government security forces training camp in Shabwa province killed at least 18 people.

Egypt's parliament is expected to vote this week on authorising the armed forces to help defend Saudi Arabia if Riyadh asks; Qatar's deputy prime minister warns the energy shock from the Iran war has yet to peak.

Local authorities and the Saudi-backed Yemeni armed forces say more than 50 security recruits were killed and 200 injured when the Houthis fired three ballistic missiles at al-Alam camp near Ataq, Shabwa, up from the at least 18 reported earlier
Saudi Arabia postpones the Future Investment Initiative, due on 26-29 Oct, to 2027; government agencies in Riyadh tell staff to work from home, AFP reports
Egypt's parliament adjourns its vote on authorising military support for Saudi Arabia to 26 Oct
Iran summons Germany's ambassador after a Hamburg court convicts two men of plotting at Tehran's behest to kill two Jewish community leaders, calling the case 'baseless political allegations'
Netanyahu airs a phone call in which Trump predicts his win in Israel's 27 Oct election; Netanyahu thanks Trump for joining the February attack on Iran and says 'we have a job to finish'

Trump says the US continues to hit Iran hard 'economically and militarily' and praises Putin for 'laying off Iran'; IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi threatens to target undersea communication cables in the Strait of Hormuz if US attacks disrupt Iran's regional security
Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi says Iran and Russia have 'never' worked so closely, after hosting Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov in Tehran on 19 Oct on his first visit since the war began

Yemeni provincial officials raise the toll from the 19 Oct Houthi missile strike on a Shabwa training camp to 73; the UK says it will deploy RAF Typhoons to help defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
Iranian officials tell Reuters Tehran is prolonging talks with the US to weaken Trump before the midterms; Iran rejects CENTCOM claims it can no longer fund its allies
Saudi Arabia says it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile fired at Riyadh after blasts were heard in the capital
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say naval mines hit three tankers using routes Tehran calls illegal in the southern Strait of Hormuz, setting two ablaze; unverified
Pezeshkian tells Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir there will be no talks with Washington until Iran's demands are met; security chief Rezaei rules out moving enriched uranium abroad
Araghchi says Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have not answered Iran's offer to mediate between them
UK police re-arrest two London men on suspicion of assisting Iranian intelligence over September's RAF Fairford security scare
Turkey submits the Saudi-Pakistan defence pact to parliament for ratification, sources tell Reuters
Rubio tells US media a peace deal with Iran is 'extremely difficult'; Araghchi says Hormuz stays closed until Washington accepts Tehran's conditions and indirect talks continue via Pakistan and Qatar
Iraq closes the Sheeb border crossing with Iran to review security and install equipment to stop smuggling, an Iraqi border official says.

The Houthis say they hit a military camp in Aden with a ballistic missile, with a blast heard near the airport (Al Jazeera), and deny the Saudi-led coalition's claim that they launched drones towards Medina (The Straits Times, Reuters).
Iranian officials tell the US to prove it wants peace by lifting its blockade; Netanyahu says at a rally that 'toppling' Iran's government is the only way to end the threat.

The US orders non-emergency staff and families out of its Saudi mission, citing Houthi attacks on airports and infrastructure; Egypt's Sisi says Egypt would defend Saudi territory but not attack Yemen.

Qatar's emir and France's Macron call in a joint statement for freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz 'without constraints or fees' and for the Gaza ceasefire to be implemented; Iran's foreign minister says Tehran is 'prepared to give diplomacy another chance'.
Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority says one person was killed and eight injured in an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam; it did not name the attacker.

The New York Times reports the US and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the US elections; neither government has confirmed it. Iran's IRGC says its doctrine is now 'offensive' and threatens to invade any attacker (Al Jazeera).
timeline.source: The Straits Times (The New York Times), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: Saudi authorities say debris from a drone intercepted during an attempted attack on an oil field killed two people, bringing deaths from attacks across the kingdom to three including the Dammam airport strike, the BBC reports.

Trump denies the US is negotiating with Tehran and says the situation will resolve 'fairly soon'; Iran's IRGC claims its navy struck four ships involved in oil transfers in the Gulf and that three other vessels caught fire after hitting mines near Hormuz. Al Jazeera reports the claims; they have not been independently verified.

Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority now says two people were killed and eight injured at Dammam's King Fahd International Airport; a drone strike on Aramco's Shaybah oil field killed two early on 21 Oct without affecting output, the energy ministry says.
IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebi announces an 'offensive' doctrine, saying renewed US attacks could prompt Iran to invade neighbouring countries and hit bases used for US operations.
Fighting intensifies between Yemeni government forces and the Houthis in Taiz; the UN warns nearly 260,000 people are displaced.

Egypt's foreign minister calls for a political solution in Yemen ahead of a parliamentary vote, postponed to 26 Oct, on authorising the army to support Saudi Arabia against the Houthis; President Sisi says any support would be limited to defending Saudi territory.

Trump signals possible further military action, saying the US knocked 'the hell out' of Iran; Iran says seven oil tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in a single day, which would be the highest daily toll of the war. The tanker claim is Iran's and is not independently verified.
European and Middle Eastern foreign ministers meet in Istanbul for security talks on the Strait of Hormuz and other regional crises, Al Jazeera's live page reports.
Trump tells a Florida rally 'We may do another little Epic Fury'; US ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack says a strike could come this weekend.
After meeting counterparts from Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Germany, France, Britain and Italy in Istanbul, Turkey's Hakan Fidan says they agree a new attack on Iran would widen the war.

A Washington Institute tracker counts 28 attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz in October, a record, and 113 since 28 Feb; BBC Verify tracks an oil slick from the damaged tanker Gem No.2 onto UAE beaches near Umm Al Quwain.

US officials say the State Department is cutting embassy staff and has put personnel on alert after intelligence that Iran is in 'advanced stages' of planning attacks on Americans; not independently confirmed.
Two senior Iranian security officials tell Reuters Tehran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if the US and Israel attack again; not independently verified.
Iran's armed forces chief Ali Abdollahi says US warships will not be allowed into the Gulf 'under any circumstances', according to Iranian state TV.

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: Israel's West Bank operation after two soldiers were killed near Hebron on 23 Oct widened on 24 Oct to raids on at least 15 northern towns, Al Jazeera reports; the military says it will last several days. Israel votes on Tuesday 27 Oct.

timeline.event: A Hamas delegation led by Khalil al-Hayya holds talks with Egypt's intelligence chief in Cairo on a plan for Gaza.
US envoy Jared Kushner meets Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo - a rare direct meeting between a senior US official and the group's leadership - while Israel carries out fresh strikes on Gaza.
The Pope calls for an end to violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Kushner meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem to push Trump's Gaza plan, a day after the Cairo meeting. Israel rejected the plan on 9 August and has not said whether its position has changed.
UNIFIL says Israeli flags placed along a road in southern Lebanon violate UN Security Council Resolution 1701. Israel has not responded publicly.

Kushner's round of talks with Israel and Hamas ends without a breakthrough on Trump's Gaza plan. US officials say Netanyahu and Kushner discussed Hamas handing over weapons under the supervision of an American general, with disarmament possibly beginning within 30 days; Hamas has not publicly accepted disarmament.

An Israeli settler walks onto the land of Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American whose West Bank home in Qusra has been besieged by settlers, in a tense face-to-face confrontation. The Israeli authorities have not commented on the incident.

An Israeli airstrike kills at least six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials say, a day after Jared Kushner's regional trip ended without advancing Trump's plan to end the war. Israel has not commented on the strike.
A US envoy says Washington is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria to avoid clashes as all three operate in Syrian territory.

The United States sanctions ICC president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, extending a campaign that began with the court's warrants against Israeli officials over alleged war crimes in Gaza. The ICC says the measures undermine the rule of law.

Syrian state television reports eight Israeli airstrikes on the disused Abu al-Duhur military airfield in Idlib province, saying there were no casualties. Damascus calls the attack an unjustified act of aggression.
US envoy Tom Barrack says Washington is deeply concerned by Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase and calls them an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Turkey rejects as untenable Israel's claim that it struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase to prevent Turkish forces deploying there. Washington says it is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria.

The Israeli military says it has ordered criminal investigations into the January 2024 killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza City and into the killings of Palestinian paramedics and rescue workers. Israel had previously said its forces were unaware of the vehicle Hind Rajab was in.

The International Criminal Court calls the US sanctions on its president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye a 'flagrant attack' on the tribunal's independence. Japan separately calls the designations 'unfortunate'.
The BBC reports that thousands of people remain missing in Gaza, with recovery and identification work far behind the scale of the task and families still searching for answers.
Syria arrests an Assad-era officer who had fled Austria after being convicted there.

An Israeli airstrike on a Gaza police station kills nine Palestinians, medics say; Al Jazeera reports the strike hit the Gaza City police headquarters and killed the head of the women's police. Israel has not published its account of the target.

Sources tell The Straits Times that the Mossad chief and Syria's foreign minister discussed Turkish military deployments before Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase. Neither government has confirmed the meeting.
Lebanon hands a former Assad-era Syrian army general to Damascus after an arrest warrant, the first such transfer since Assad's fall.

The Israeli military confirms its soldiers fired at the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza City in January 2024, reversing its earlier account, and opens a criminal investigation. Her family says it does not trust the Israeli judiciary.
The United States commits US$206 million towards an international stabilisation force for Gaza, despite its 15-point peace plan remaining deadlocked.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decides not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian World Central Kitchen aid worker in Gaza.

Israel opens bidding for construction in a highly sensitive area of the occupied West Bank; critics say the project would sever the northern West Bank from the south. Britain's foreign minister says he plans sanctions over settlement expansion.
US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee warns Israeli settlers not to take land belonging to Palestinian Americans.
The BBC reports multiple deadly Israeli strikes across Gaza in under 24 hours. Casualty figures are from Gaza health officials and have not been independently verified.

Israel and Turkey step up warnings over Syria after Israel's bombing of the Abu al-Duhur airbase; Syria says no Turkish military build-up is planned there. The Straits Times reports Netanyahu is putting Turkey in Israel's crosshairs as an election approaches.

An Assad-era officer is extradited to Syria to face war crimes charges, the first such extradition since Assad's fall, after Lebanon handed a former Assad-era general to Damascus under an arrest warrant.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

timeline.event: The UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada issue a joint statement demanding Israel withdraw plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, a day after Israel opened bidding. The UN has said the E1 plan poses an 'existential threat' to a contiguous Palestinian state; Israel rejects the criticism.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decided not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian aid worker in Gaza.

Thirty settler families move into Kadim, outside Jenin in the occupied West Bank, 21 years after a previous Israeli government evacuated it under the 2005 Disengagement Plan; the current government has overturned a 20-year ban on settlement around Jenin. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, the Justice Minister and the Knesset Speaker attend the ceremony. All settlements are illegal under international law; Israel disputes this.
ICC president Tomoko Akane, sanctioned by Washington on Aug 18, warns the measures point towards the 'demise of international rule of law'.

The UK, Canada and Australia issue a joint statement calling 'shameful' Israel's decision not to open a criminal investigation into the April 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen convoy that killed seven aid workers. Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, says there was 'no criminal intention' and therefore no criminal responsibility.
Israeli forces shoot dead a Palestinian teenager after settlers entered a West Bank village, according to Palestinian officials. The Israeli military's account has not been reported alongside it.

Israel rejects Turkey's move to seek an Interpol red notice for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the Gaza aid flotilla case, calling it a 'pathetic attempt' to intimidate its leaders and soldiers. Netanyahu calls President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'.
Former French and British ambassadors urge Paris and London to take joint action on the Palestinian territories, where violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank has surged since the Gaza war began.

Israel says it fired at a 'terrorist' in southern Syria; Syria's foreign ministry says an Israeli drone hit a civilian car near Beit Jinn, west of Damascus, calling it a 'blatant violation' of Syrian sovereignty. Syrian state TV reports one person injured. It is the second Israeli strike in Syria in a week, after the Abu al-Duhur airbase attack the US called an 'unnecessary escalation'.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Israeli military, Syrian foreign ministry)

timeline.event: The Straits Times reports that the widening confrontation between Israel and Turkey could reshape the region, with Syria - which physically separates the two - bearing the brunt of their rivalry.

Syria's government condemns the Israeli strike on the village of Beit Jinn, south-west of Damascus, as a violation of its sovereignty and of international law; officials say it hit a civilian vehicle and injured several people. The Israeli military says it targeted a 'terrorist' in the 'final stages' of preparing attacks posing an immediate threat to its soldiers.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Syrian officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: US ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack says the earlier Israeli strike on the Abu al-Duhur airbase could be 'the Israelis baiting the Turks' in an attempt to draw Ankara into a conflict. Washington had already called that strike an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani says he expects security talks with Israel to resume soon despite an absence of trust, with Damascus seeking an Israeli withdrawal from Syrian land and an end to strikes. He says the US is pressing Israel to return to negotiations, and denies Syria allowed Turkish forces at the airbase Israel bombed this week.

Syria and Israel hold high-level US-mediated talks in Jordan, focused on practical mechanisms to halt Israeli strikes, arrests and targeted operations and on reviving negotiations towards a security agreement, Syria's state news agency SANA reports citing a diplomatic source. Israel's prime minister's office did not comment.

At the Jordan talks, Damascus says its immediate priorities remain an Israeli withdrawal to positions held before Bashar al-Assad's overthrow on 8 Dec 2024 and full restoration of the 1974 disengagement agreement, and that it will not accept limits on rebuilding its armed forces, according to SANA.

Syrian state news agency SANA reports that Syria and Israel held further US-mediated talks aimed at easing tensions, following the round held in Jordan on 23 August. Israel's prime minister's office has not commented.

Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz warned of 'forceful actions' after four kites were found in Kibbutz Nahal Oz, about 800m from the Gaza boundary, and several more elsewhere in southern Israel. The Israeli military said the kites carried no suspicious materials and posed no threat. Hamas denied responsibility, called them 'basically children's toys from displacement camps', and accused Israel of using them as a pretext for continued strikes despite the ceasefire agreed last October.
Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked a ship off Saudi Arabia's Yanbu. There was no Saudi confirmation of the claim.

Medics in Gaza said Israeli fire killed two young children. The account comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented on the specific incident.

The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism after 47 years, and removed Hayat Tahrir al-Sham from its list of global terrorist organisations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it recognised Damascus distancing itself from international terrorism; Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani called it a 'historic step'. Syria remains at the centre of tension between Israel and Turkey.

Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa said Syria 'shakes off a dark stain and tears away a painful chapter of its past' after the US removed the country from its state-sponsors-of-terrorism list, thanking President Trump. The Treasury announced corresponding sanctions relief; Hayat Tahrir al-Sham was also delisted as a global terrorist organisation.

Far-right Israeli lawmaker and settler activist Zvi Sukkot took a sledgehammer to a Palestinian memorial in Madama in the northern occupied West Bank while under military escort. The army said the demolition was unauthorised and a misuse of security protection, that soldiers stopped it and removed him, and that it viewed the incident with 'utmost severity'; Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot also criticised him.

Parents in Gaza were urged to stop children flying kites after Israel's warning to Hamas over kites found near the boundary. Israel's defence minister had threatened 'forceful actions'; the Israeli military says the kites carried nothing dangerous and Hamas calls them children's toys.

Medics in Gaza said Israeli attacks killed five people including two children. The figure comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented on the specific incident.

An official on President Trump's US-led 'Board of Peace' said all militant activity in Gaza must stop, including the flying of kites, and added that 'Israel, too, must comply with the ceasefire' and that military action cannot extend beyond genuine and imminent threats. The UN and Hamas called the kite warnings outrageous.

Israeli forces took control of UNRWA's Qalandia vocational training centre between Kafr Aqab in east Jerusalem and the Qalandia refugee camp. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said the evacuation followed the law Israel passed severing ties with the agency; UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the raid. The centre, opened in 1952, trains about 340 West Bank Palestinians a year.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UNRWA, Israeli PM's office)

timeline.event: Syria's Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces announced their dissolution as part of an agreed integration into the Damascus government's structures.
President Trump sent a civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress, while saying Riyadh must recognise Israel.
Israeli forces have taken control of a UN training centre for Palestinians, The Straits Times reports. UNRWA has not said whether courses there will continue.

Israel's seizure of UNRWA's Qalandia vocational training college in East Jerusalem drew international condemnation. Israel's government says the site was evacuated lawfully; UNRWA disputes the basis for the takeover.
A far-right Israeli lawmaker damaged a Palestinian memorial with a sledgehammer, footage of the incident showed.
Lebanon accused Israel of setting fire to forest and farmland in the south of the country. Israel has not commented on the accusation.
US Senate Democrats urged Israel to rein in settler violence in the West Bank.
Turkey said the dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces would help Syrian unity, a day after the SDF announced it was integrating into Damascus government structures.

The United States designated the UK-based group Palestine Action as a foreign terrorist organisation and imposed sanctions on it. The group has previously said its actions target arms manufacturing sites.
An Israeli court acquitted, on grounds of mental health, the man filmed on CCTV attacking a nun in Jerusalem.
A funeral was held in the West Bank for Sliman Mansour, one of the best-known Palestinian artists of his generation.

Israeli strikes killed at least three Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials in Gaza said. The figure comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented.

Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's envoy for Gaza, criticised both Israeli strikes and Hamas's actions and warned that a collapse of last October's ceasefire would be 'a point of no return' for the region.

The UN human rights office condemned the United States' designation of the UK-based group Palestine Action as a foreign terrorist organisation, saying the label risks criminalising protest. The State Department announced the designation, with sanctions, on 26 August.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights)

timeline.event: A former British-Israeli hostage held by Hamas married in Tel Aviv, in one of the more visible personal milestones since last October's ceasefire.
An Israeli air strike killed a Hamas operative and two other people near Jenin in the occupied West Bank, the Israeli military said, in a rare use of air power in the territory.
The BBC published the results of a week spent tracking settler violence in the occupied West Bank, documenting incidents against Palestinian communities.

Druze factions blocked students from sitting examinations in a dispute with the Syrian government, The Straits Times reported, the latest friction between Damascus and communities in the south as the new government consolidates control.

Dozens of Israeli settlers attack the Palestinian village of Qusra near Nablus in the northern occupied West Bank, residents and the Israeli military say. A resident tells AFP a small group approached villagers working on a house, then returned with dozens more, surrounded them and threw stones. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemns the attack, a rare step; Israeli forces deploy to the site.

Israel's military says it struck a Hamas commander "hiding within the compound" of Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah, saying medical facilities must not be used for militant activity. Gaza health officials say Israeli strikes elsewhere in the territory killed four people. Both accounts are contested and not independently verified.
Druze factions in southern Syria block students from sitting state examinations in a dispute with the Damascus government, The Straits Times reports.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemns the settler attack on the West Bank village of Qusra, calling it a criminal act that does not represent Israeli society; the Israeli military says it has opened an investigation. Palestinian residents say the village had been under a supply blockade for weeks before the attack.

The Straits Times reports that killings of Palestinian children and teenagers by Israeli forces and settlers have risen sharply in the occupied West Bank this year. Israel says its forces operate against militants; the two accounts of individual incidents frequently diverge and are rarely independently adjudicated.

An Israeli air strike near a bakery in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza kills a man and a three-year-old boy and wounds several others, Gaza health officials say; the Israeli military says it attacked a Hamas militant. Gazan health officials say more than 1,300 Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect, while the Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed. Both tallies come from parties to the conflict.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Gaza health officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: An AFP investigation reports that Israeli forces and settlers have killed Palestinian children and teenagers in the occupied West Bank at an average of about seven a month since October 2023, against roughly one a month before. Families say Israeli military investigations rarely produce accountability; the Israeli military says it investigates such deaths.
Israel's far-right national security minister publicly boasts of having worsened prison conditions for Palestinian security prisoners.

The Straits Times publishes an analysis of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's position on settler violence, noting he condemned the Qusra attack while continuing to back far-right coalition partners. No new strikes or casualties were reported in Gaza or Lebanon in the preceding 24 hours.

The UK Foreign Office says it has raised with Israeli authorities the detention of Finn Joughin, a 22-year-old British student activist forcibly detained by Israeli settlers in Umm al-Kheir in the occupied West Bank on Saturday before being arrested.

An Israeli strike killed at least five Palestinians in Gaza on Monday, health officials say: two killed and several wounded when a strike hit a crowd near the municipal public park in Gaza City, an area densely populated with displaced families, and at least three more killed later when a strike hit a vehicle in the Tel Al-Hawa neighbourhood. The Israeli military said it targeted Hamas militants in the first strike and did not immediately comment on the second. Casualty figures come from Gaza health officials.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Gaza health officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: Israel and Greece sign a EUR 3 billion (S$4.43 billion) agreement under which Israel will build a multi-layered air defence system for Greece, named "Achilles Shield", to be delivered by 2036. Israel's defence ministry confirmed the signing.

Raam leader Mansour Abbas announces that Yoav Segalovitz, a former Israeli police official and until recently a Yesh Atid member of the Knesset, will run on the moderate Islamist party's list in the 27 October election — the first Jewish Israeli to stand for an explicitly Arab party. Raam will campaign on an anti-crime platform. Segalovitz said there is “a difficult history between Arabs and Jews in this country, but there is also a shared future”.

An Israeli-backed raid to detain a Hamas figure in Gaza City is discovered mid-operation. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz says a senior Hamas member was captured, and an Israeli security official says the man detained heads Hamas's internal security service. Gaza officials and medics say air strikes launched to cover the force's withdrawal killed at least four people near the Katiba area of western Gaza City — two children and a woman among them — with another child killed in central Gaza; witnesses described at least 12 missiles fired into an area crowded with displaced families. Hamas government media office director Ismail al-Thawabta says the Israeli unit was detected before it could finish. Casualty figures come from Gaza medical sources and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Israeli defence ministry, Gaza medics, Hamas media office)

timeline.event: Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Saar warns Israel will retaliate if the UK imposes sanctions over the potential expansion of West Bank settlements. The warning came shortly after British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Parliament he would introduce a 'comprehensive reset' of policy on Israel in the coming weeks, including examining how to stop UK companies financing, constructing or advertising new settlements.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accuses security officials of deliberately failing to wake him on the morning of the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack, insisting the assault would have been contained had he intervened earlier - a day after his wife claimed an opposition figure knew of the attack in advance, prompting a threatened lawsuit. Netanyahu faces close-fought elections later in 2026. The 7 October attack killed more than 1,200 people in Israel and saw 251 taken hostage; Gaza authorities report more than 73,000 Palestinians killed in the offensive that followed.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli and Gaza authorities)

timeline.event: Unifil says the Israeli military has established four new bases in the areas of southern Lebanon it invaded, bringing the number of Israeli positions to nine, and reports consolidation and fortification of those positions along with demolition and engineering work. The strip under Israeli control is about 5 per cent of Lebanese territory and extends up to 10km from the border in places. A Lebanese intelligence official says Lebanon's military has recorded more than 5,000 violations of the June deal by Israel; the Israeli military says the buildings destroyed were used by Hezbollah for military purposes and that it acts in accordance with international law.
timeline.source: BBC (Unifil, Lebanese intelligence official, Israeli military)

timeline.event: More than 10 EU countries say they are willing to contribute to a planned European mission to train the Lebanese army.

Israel says a Hamas security chief was captured during a raid in Gaza City in which strikes killed four people, according to Gaza medics. Hezbollah's leader Naim Qassem last week called the US-brokered framework for the group's disarmament 'surrender with humiliation'.

Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry says Israeli attacks have killed more than 900 people in the territory so far in 2026 despite the ceasefire, taking the total since the 10 October truce past 1,300, including 301 children. The ministry does not separate civilians from combatants. The UN considers the figures reliable and BBC Verify says independent analysis is consistent with them; the Israeli military disputes the count, saying there is no basis to assume all those listed were killed by its activity, and says five of its soldiers have been killed in combat since the ceasefire.

A BBC team travelling with Unifil inside the part of southern Lebanon under Israeli control reports entire villages flattened, with air strikes and demolitions continuing after the ceasefire announced in June. Lebanese officials say Israel is expanding its positions in the zone.

Two Palestinian teenagers are killed in an attack by Israeli settler militants and army troops on their village in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday, local officials and the Palestinian health ministry say, amid an uptick in settler violence in the territory. Israel has not published its own account.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Palestinian health ministry, local officials)

timeline.event: The Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, named after a Shi'ite scholar whose shrine sits at its summit, has become one of the most contested pieces of ground in the Israel-Hezbollah war, according to a Straits Times explainer from Beirut.

Netanyahu visits Israeli forces inside the Gaza Strip, his first trip there since the October 2025 ceasefire, and rejects mediators' push for a US-backed plan requiring withdrawal. 'We control the area. We are not retreating. We are staying on this line,' he says near the Yellow Line, adding that Israel controls 60 per cent of the strip. Hamas has not responded publicly to the visit.
Rights groups urge US lawmakers to drop a provision that would deepen American defence ties with Israel.
Lebanon receives the first of five Lebanese detainees Israel has agreed to free as part of continuing talks between the two governments.
The US House of Representatives passes a bill to penalise university boycotts of Israel. It still requires Senate action.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (US House of Representatives)

timeline.event: Israel's far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, campaigning ahead of close-fought elections, sets out a plan to remove Palestinians from Gaza: 250,000 in the first year and the remaining roughly two million over the following six. He claims unnamed countries are 'ready' to take them and says the plan does not amount to forcing anyone out. No government decision has been announced. Forced displacement of civilians in occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions.

The Israeli military says it has cleared Hezbollah fighters from tunnels beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, one of the most contested positions of the conflict. Hezbollah has not confirmed the account and the claim has not been independently verified.

With Israeli elections approaching, more of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition partners publicly back removing Palestinians from Gaza, after National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir set out a staged plan earlier in the day. Such proposals are opposed by Palestinian officials and by Israel's main mediators.
Thousands of Lebanese students remain displaced as the school year approaches, with schools in the south destroyed or occupied and families still unable to return home.

The Israeli military says it struck southern Lebanon after Hezbollah launched a drone towards Israeli soldiers. Lebanon's health ministry says three people were killed and 23 wounded, including medics, women and children, and Lebanon's state National News Agency reports strikes across the south. Hezbollah did not immediately comment. Both accounts come from parties to the conflict and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA (Israeli military, Lebanese health ministry, Lebanese NNA)

timeline.event: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, visiting the West Bank town of Turmus Ayya, says categorically that there is no Israeli plan to displace Palestinians out of Gaza against their will, after Defence Minister Israel Katz and far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir floated mass removal this week.

Huckabee meets relatives of US citizens killed by Israeli settlers in Turmus Ayya, calling the attackers a 'tiny group' who damage Israel's reputation and urging prosecutions. Palestinian Americans and local officials dispute his characterisation and press for stronger US pressure on Israel.

The Israeli military says it is striking southern Lebanon early on Sunday in retaliation for Hezbollah firing two drones at Israeli soldiers stationed in an area Israel has declared a security zone. Hezbollah has not publicly commented on the launches.

Lebanon's health ministry says Israeli strikes killed at least seven people in southern Lebanon on Sunday - two men near the zone occupied by Israeli troops, two women in Arab Salim and three in a separate drone strike on Nabatieh al-Tahta - with six others wounded, including two girls. Israel says it struck Hezbollah weapons storage sites and a command centre inside a building formerly used as a hospital, in retaliation for Hezbollah drone attacks, and says it used precision munitions and aerial surveillance to limit civilian harm. Figures are the Lebanese ministry's and the targeting account is Israel's; neither has been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA (Lebanese health ministry, Israeli military)

timeline.event: Muslim-majority nations warn that Israeli plans to remove Palestinians from Gaza threaten the US-brokered peace framework. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said on 2 September that the government had such plans.

An Israeli strike on a vehicle in western Gaza City kills Youssef Akila and his eight-year-old daughter Wafaa and wounds six others, says Mohamed Abu Selmia, head of Al Shifa Hospital. An Israeli military spokesperson says forces targeted a Hamas militant and were still reviewing the results. Two further Israeli strikes later on Sunday killed two more people, including a child, medics say. The casualty accounts are from Gaza medical officials and have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Gaza health officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: President Joseph Aoun's office calls the day's Israeli strikes 'a dangerous escalation' that hit 'purely civilian administrations and health centres', saying they destroyed an out-of-service hospital and damaged a finance ministry building, and urges the United States and the international community to act. Israel says its targets were Hezbollah weapons stores and a command centre.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Lebanese presidency, Israeli military)

timeline.event: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu orders unauthorised settler outposts in the occupied West Bank to be dismantled, two people familiar with the matter say, amid US pressure over settler attacks on Palestinians. No start date was given. UN bodies and most governments consider all Israeli settlements illegal under international law; Israel argues the territory is disputed rather than occupied.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA (sources familiar with the matter)

timeline.event: Israeli warplanes strike a residential building in Kfar Rumman in southern Lebanon just after midnight, killing nine people including two children and wounding five, and a separate drone strike on a civilian vehicle in the town kills two medics, Lebanon's National News Agency says - at least 11 dead. The agency says no online evacuation warning was issued; the Israeli military did not immediately respond to questions about the strikes. A warning was issued just after 2am for areas around a building in another southern town where it said it would hit Hezbollah facilities.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Lebanon's National News Agency, Israeli military)

timeline.event: A separate Israeli drone strike on a civilian vehicle in Kfar Rumman kills two medics, taking the town's toll for the night to at least 11 including two children, Lebanon's National News Agency says. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to questions on the strikes or the absence of an evacuation warning.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Lebanon's National News Agency)

timeline.event: Israel says its strikes in Lebanon respond to Hezbollah violations of the June truce, saying they hit weapons stores and a command centre after drone attacks on its troops.

Defence Minister Israel Katz says he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have instructed the military to prepare for 'full-scale war' against the Palestinian Authority if its security bodies initiate an Oct 7-style attack, including targeted killings of senior figures and a permanent military presence in evacuated areas. The statement follows a stabbing attack in the northern West Bank.

Nickolay Mladenov, high representative for Gaza under the US-backed Board of Peace, says at the Hili Forum that a two-state solution is becoming 'practically impossible', citing West Bank violence and a Gaza now more than half under Israeli army control with the remainder held by Hamas.
Germany asks the International Court of Justice to throw out a case brought over its arms exports to Israel.

Israeli troops shoot dead a Palestinian during a village raid by settlers from a nearby outpost in the occupied West Bank, and kill another Palestinian who entered an outpost and stabbed a settler, officials say. Both accounts come from Israeli and Palestinian officials and have not been independently verified.

Two Israeli air strikes on the southern Lebanese village of Kfar Rumman kill at least 12 people, including two children and four women, Lebanon's health ministry says; one strike hit a building and another a car, killing a paramedic with the Islamic Risala Scout Association. The Israeli military says the strikes retaliated for two Hezbollah drone attacks on its troops and targeted a militant moving weapons. The toll is the Lebanese health ministry's.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, AP (Lebanese health ministry; Israeli military)

timeline.event: A UN expert says Israel's clearing of Gaza rubble could destroy evidence of possible atrocity crimes, noting the assault has generated around 61 million tons of wreckage that could take seven years to clear.

Britain prepares to impose a trade ban on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, a measure that goes beyond its previous settlement sanctions though its direct trade impact is expected to be limited.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's main political challenger accuses him of prioritising his own survival over Israel's security, as domestic argument over the widening fronts sharpens.
The BBC reports that Palestinian parents in the occupied West Bank fear for their children's safety on the way to school as settler attacks increase.
Britain says it will announce a trade ban on goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, going beyond its earlier sanctions on individual settlers.
France's foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot says Paris will launch a process to ban products from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, citing rising settler violence.
Netanyahu comes under fire over a Haaretz report that the UAE warned Israel ahead of the October 2023 Hamas attack; the Prime Minister's Office calls the report 'an absolute lie'.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Haaretz; Israeli PM's office)

timeline.event: Netanyahu moves to consolidate Israel's fractious right-wing parties before a Tuesday registration deadline, with opinion polls forecasting an election defeat.

Britain announces sanctions and a trade ban covering goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank; the foreign secretary accuses settlers of carrying out the 'ethnic cleansing' of Palestinians. Israel rejects the characterisation.
Israel's foreign minister says Israel is closing the British consulate in East Jerusalem in response, and accuses Britain of interfering in Israel's upcoming elections.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Israeli foreign ministry)

timeline.event: Ministers from a dozen countries say they will back or consider curbs on trade in goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, saying Israel's actions there are undermining the possibility of a two-state solution. Israel's government calls the move a 'big mistake'.
timeline.source: CNA, BBC (joint ministerial statement; Israeli government)

timeline.event: A UN commission investigating Syria says it is deeply alarmed by Israeli military activity inside Syrian territory and warns that some actions, including detentions, may amount to war crimes. Israel disputes the commission's mandate.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UN commission of inquiry)

timeline.event: The BBC assesses British-Israeli relations to be at their lowest ebb in decades following the settlement trade ban and the consulate closure.

Israel tells the British consulate in East Jerusalem that it must close and that diplomats assigned there will lose their accreditation within 30 days, an Israeli official and two other sources say. The move follows Britain's settlement trade ban.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Israeli official and sources familiar with the matter)

timeline.event: Israel says it will open an embassy in Slovenia as relations thaw, a rare warming on the same day its rift with Britain deepened.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar says the government has no plans to deport Palestinians from Gaza, after two Israeli ministers floated mass-removal proposals earlier this month.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham defends the ban on imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank in parliament, saying Britain has to 'stand for something'. Israel rejects the policy.
The BBC reports from Khan al-Ahmar, a Palestinian community in the West Bank's E1 area that Israel has earmarked for settlement construction and Britain opposes.

An Israeli airstrike kills a man, his wife and their daughters aged eight and 12 in a house in Beit Lahiya in northern Gaza, health officials say, as the military escalates strikes on houses over two days. The Israeli military did not immediately comment. Casualty figures come from Gaza health authorities.

Medics in Gaza say shortages of engine oil and spare parts are causing hospital generators to seize up, with power cuts cascading through one of the territory's largest functioning hospitals. Gaza has had no grid electricity since the start of Israel's offensive, and neighbourhood generator power is becoming unaffordable for families.
A film premiered at the Venice festival features Israeli whistleblowers giving accounts of the civilian toll in Gaza.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says he will sue a newspaper over a report claiming the UAE warned him ahead of the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack. The newspaper stands by its reporting.
The Israeli military says it destroyed a Hezbollah underground complex at Ali al-Taher in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah has not confirmed the loss and the claim has not been independently verified.

The Israeli military says it destroyed a major Hezbollah underground complex at Ali al-Taher in southern Lebanon and is ready to carry out further strikes; the US Geological Survey registered the blast as equivalent to a magnitude 4.1 earthquake. Hezbollah has not confirmed the Israeli account of the site.

German federal prosecutors charge seven suspected Hamas members in Berlin with membership of a foreign terrorist organisation and preparing an attack, including by procuring weapons. The charges have not been tested in court.
A US official says the next round of Israel-Lebanon talks in Rome has been delayed to October. Neither government has commented on the record.

The Israeli military rejects testimonies given by whistleblowers in a documentary, premiered at the Venice festival, about the use of AI systems in targeting decisions in Gaza. The film-makers stand by the accounts; neither version has been independently verified.

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun makes an unannounced visit to Nabatieh, below the Ali al-Taher ridge Israel seized and blew up, and says 'there will be no new negotiations with Israel at the moment'. A US official says the Rome round has slipped to October and the two ambassadors will meet at the State Department next week instead. AFP reports Israeli strikes in the area have killed at least 29 people in recent days; not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Lebanese presidency, US official), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: Israeli forces continue striking southern Lebanon as the next US-mediated round of Israel–Lebanon talks, scheduled for Rome this month, is pushed to October.

An Israeli air strike on a civilian vehicle in the Tal al-Hawa neighbourhood of Gaza City kills two Palestinians, medics say; strikes continue despite the US-brokered ceasefire. The Israeli military has not commented.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera, The Straits Times (Gaza medics)

timeline.event: A US State Department official says Israel and Lebanon will meet in Rome in October for the next round of talks on the US-brokered security agreement, and that the two ambassadors will meet in Washington next week; the August round ended without a breakthrough on territorial issues. Israel holds a roughly 10km 'buffer zone' inside Lebanon; more than 4,300 people have been killed in Lebanon since fighting resumed on March 2, the report says.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; US State Department official)

timeline.event: Medics say the Israeli strike on a vehicle in Gaza City's Tal al-Hawa neighbourhood killed at least two people and wounded 13; the Israeli military says it targeted two Hamas militants. Al Jazeera separately airs footage it says shows an Israeli quadcopter over homes in Gaza City.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Gaza medics, Israeli military), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: Residents say Israeli strikes hit people outside tents in a Gaza City displacement camp, with at least one person killed and several injured across Gaza; the Israeli military had not commented in the report.

Israel’s culture minister calls for the Israeli directors of “Naza”, a documentary in which unnamed soldiers and officers describe AI-assisted targeting in Gaza, to be stripped of their citizenship for “treason”.

UN human rights chief Volker Türk says the recovery of hundreds of bodies, including what appear to be entire families, from buildings destroyed by Israeli strikes raises fresh war-crimes concerns; Israel has repeatedly denied deliberately targeting civilians.

Gaza health officials and Hamas sources say Israeli air strikes killed at least five Palestinians, including two children and a Hamas armed commander, in northern and southern Gaza. Medics describe an apparent 'double tap' strike on a vehicle in Sheikh Radwan that killed two and wounded seven, with some casualties among people who had rushed to help. The Israeli military says it struck a militant in the area and a Hamas Rafah Brigade commander.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Gaza medics, Israeli military)

timeline.event: The British charity Medical Aid for Palestinians says a patient was shot dead by an Israeli quadcopter drone at a health centre it supports in Jabalia, northern Gaza. There was no immediate Israeli comment.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Medical Aid for Palestinians)

timeline.event: A six-storey apartment block in Tal al-Hawa, Gaza City, housing people displaced by the war, collapses onto nearby homes and tents; the Hamas-run civil defence agency says eight bodies including children and 15 injured people have been recovered and more than 60 people are missing, and that the building had structural damage from earlier Israeli strikes. The figures are not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Gaza civil defence agency)

timeline.event: A US official speaking anonymously says the Trump administration plans a US$2.8 billion munitions package for Israel including 20,000 MK 84 and 20,000 BLU-117 2,000-pound bombs, informally notified to the relevant congressional committees; the State Department and Israel's embassy did not respond to requests for comment.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Washington Post first reported)

timeline.event: The toll from the Tal al-Hawa building collapse rises to at least 21, including eight children, with dozens missing, according to Gaza's civil defence and medics; UN agencies and an Egyptian team join a search hampered by a lack of equipment.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA (Reuters), Al Jazeera (Gaza civil defence)

timeline.event: Defence Minister Israel Katz says it is 'only a matter of time' before Israel resumes full-scale war in Gaza and implements a 'migration plan' for its two million residents, claiming 70 per cent of the territory is already emptied; US Ambassador Mike Huckabee has denied any plan to displace people against their will.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Israeli defence ministry, US embassy)

timeline.event: Reuters reporters embedded with French UNIFIL peacekeepers report that the UN force's mandate ends at year-end, leaving residents of Rmeich and other Christian towns inside Israel's self-declared 'security zone' in southern Lebanon fearing they will be cut off; the zone was established after more than six months of Israeli bombardment triggered by a Hezbollah rocket attack in early March.

Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, says he will not back the US$2.8 billion sale of 2,000lb bombs to Israel over international-law concerns; the administration can proceed without his clearance.

Netanyahu vows to legislate to strip citizenship from anyone who defames Israeli soldiers, escalating threats against the Israeli directors of NAZA, a documentary alleging the military accepted mass civilian deaths in Gaza.
Britain's Trades Union Congress, representing more than 5.3 million workers, backs the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement against Israel for the first time.
Israel and Morocco agree at a US-hosted meeting in New York to upgrade their missions to embassies and appoint ambassadors, the Israeli government says.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters; Israeli government), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: The US denies Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas a visa to attend next week's UN General Assembly for a second year, as the State Department extends visa bans on PLO and Palestinian Authority officials it accuses of failing to reform; Palestinian officials reject the accusations.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (AFP; US State Department)

timeline.event: European and Arab military chiefs meet in Paris, opened by Macron with Lebanon's President Aoun and Jordan's King Abdullah, to assess the Lebanese army's needs before UNIFIL's roughly 7,500 peacekeepers begin drawing down in January; options include a non-UN mission backed by France and Italy.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters; French presidency, diplomats)

timeline.event: Gaza rescuers end searches at the bomb-damaged building that collapsed a day earlier, where a Palestinian official says 21 people were killed and 45 rescued from the rubble.
Israeli rights groups say Israel has added a tender for 2,167 housing units to its E1 settlement plan near Jerusalem, a project critics say endangers a future Palestinian state.
Serbia opens an Israeli drone assembly plant, deepening defence-industrial ties with Israel at a time when several European governments are restricting arms cooperation over Gaza.

An algae bloom that crippled several of Israel's desalination plants raises questions about the country's water security, the BBC reports, with supply from the affected plants curtailed while operators work to restore output.
Syria's government warns that Israel poses 'the greatest threat' to stability in the Middle East, in one of its sharpest public statements since the change of government in Damascus.
Two people are injured by Israeli shelling as Israeli troops advance in southern Lebanon, Al Jazeera reports.
Syria's government arrests five former officers of the al-Assad era over strikes on civilians.
A mural of rapper Macklemore is painted in Gaza following the furore over Ed Sheeran's tour.
A UK court clears a woman of voicing support for Hamas in a university speech.
An Israeli strike on a motorcycle in Gaza City kills a Palestinian man and injures a child, Al Jazeera reports.
The European Union urges the United States to reconsider its visa denial to the Palestinian delegation for next week's UN General Assembly meeting in New York.
Gaza health officials say four people, including a child, were killed in Israeli strikes.
The UN's peacekeeping chief in Lebanon says a smooth handover to the Lebanese state is critical before UNIFIL withdraws, warning against a security vacuum in the south.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog pardons a former combat medic convicted of manslaughter over the 2016 shooting of a wounded Palestinian attacker in Hebron, a case that divided Israeli opinion; Palestinian officials and rights groups criticise the decision.

Israeli police say a Palestinian gunman shot dead an Israeli man at a spring near the West Bank settlement of Neve Tzuf and was arrested hours later at a Ramallah hospital. Separately, the Israeli military says soldiers killed a Palestinian driver who tried to ram them near Ganim, east of Jenin; the Palestine Red Crescent says its medics were prevented from reaching him. Netanyahu orders reinforcements and arrests; Hamas praises the shooting without claiming it.

Hundreds of thousands of children in Gaza have returned to in-person classes, which resumed on Sept 19 for the first time in nearly three years, mostly in tents and damaged buildings with few supplies. About 660,000 pupils missed regular schooling during the war, and UNICEF says 98 per cent of school buildings were damaged or destroyed.

Medical sources at Nasser hospital tell Al Jazeera that three Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire in Gaza on Sept 21 - a child in the al-Mawasi zone in the south, a man in Jabalia and a woman in Deir el-Balah - with nine others reported wounded in Bureij and Khan Younis. The account comes from Palestinian medical sources and Al Jazeera; no Israeli military response was carried in the report, and the figures are not independently verified.

Al Jazeera reports that Israeli forces have detained at least 53 Palestinians in a raid on the West Bank town of Biddu, north-west of Jerusalem, citing the Jerusalem Governorate and the town's mayor, who says homes have been turned into interrogation centres and shops and schools are shut. It is the third incursion since the Israeli military said it arrested a man from the town suspected of the Sept 20 shooting that killed an Israeli near Neve Tzuf (Halamish).

Defence Minister Israel Katz, speaking at a Yom Kippur War memorial, vows that if any Israeli is abducted in future Israel will force all of Gaza City's residents out, displacing about a million people, and destroy infrastructure; forced displacement of civilians is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions. Netanyahu says he will use his UN speech to defend Israel's military actions after New York's mayor called him a 'war criminal'.

Macron, in his final UN address, says not one humanitarian corridor has reopened in Gaza despite Trump's proclaimed peace and calls the situation 'a spectacle that should shame everyone'; Netanyahu's office calls Macron's claim that Hamas is not active in the West Bank a 'grotesque absurdity', saying Hamas attacks Jews there 'almost every day'. Netanyahu addresses the UN on Thursday.

Al Jazeera reports Israeli forces killed at least three Palestinians in Gaza City on Sept 22 despite the US-brokered ceasefire, as France, Canada and the UK back a Palestinian state at the UN; Canada's Carney pledges US$71 million for two-state efforts and Burnham vows not to 'stand by' as Palestinians suffer. The UN Population Fund reports a 123 per cent rise in early and forced marriage in Gaza in the second quarter and escalating gender-based violence in displacement camps.
