Netanyahu calls Macron's UN remarks on West Bank violations a 'grotesque absurdity' and says Hamas members there attack Jews almost daily; Macron's office does not respond. Axios reports, per ST, that Trump's Board of Peace will unveil a six-month US$2.45 billion, 66-project Gaza recovery plan on Sept 23 that estimates physical damage at US$35.2 billion (unconfirmed by the White House). US Senate Democrats introduce a bill to sanction those facilitating Israel's E1 settlement project.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Reuters, citing Axios)

timeline.event: Trump's Board of Peace unveils a US$2.45 billion, six-month, 66-programme Gaza recovery plan; it says US$18 billion is pledged but only US$280 million delivered and full reconstruction will cost about US$71.4 billion. Gaza officials say more than 2,000 buildings are at risk after the Sept 16 Al-Saada collapse killed 21.

In the West Bank, Israeli military bulldozers uproot olive groves near Ramallah days before the harvest, villagers say; a Palestinian man is shot dead after what Israeli police call a car-ramming that injured a soldier, whom Israel's US ambassador identifies as his son. UNRWA's acting chief says Israel is 'squeezing' the agency ahead of elections.
Israel's Central Elections Committee votes to bar both main Arab lists, Ra'am and the Joint List, from the Oct 27 election; the bans need Supreme Court review and are not final.

Israel's US ambassador Yechiel Leiter says his reservist son was critically injured when a Palestinian attacker rammed a car into him at a West Bank checkpoint, and criticises Macron's UN address for focusing on settler violence.
Netanyahu travels to New York for a UN visit of under eight hours, with meetings listed with nine leaders but none with US officials, as Western allies adopt trade measures against settlements.

Netanyahu tells the UN General Assembly Israel will keep fighting in Iran, Gaza and across the region, 'we're going to win, we have no other choice', as dozens of delegates walk out; he invites any remaining 'moral cowards' to leave too. Police arrest actors and politicians protesting outside the UN.

Mahmoud Abbas, addressing the UN by recorded video from Ramallah after US visa restrictions, reaffirms Palestinian legislative elections for Nov 28, the first since 2006, amid serious domestic doubts they will be held.

The Committee to Protect Journalists removes 22 people from its list of media workers killed in the Gaza war after Hamas and Islamic Jihad obituaries identified some as combatants; it now attributes 191 journalist and media-worker deaths to Israel since Oct 7, 2023.
More than 100 people are arrested in New York as protesters march on UN headquarters during Netanyahu's General Assembly speech, demanding accountability over Gaza and an end to US military support.
The UN adds 61 companies to its database of firms linked to Israeli settlements, taking the list to 214 businesses in 11 countries, most of them Israeli.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera, The Straits Times (Reuters), The Guardian

timeline.event: Hamas condemns the US-created Board of Peace's decision not to work with UNRWA and its statement that the agency will have no role in Gaza, accusing the Board of aligning with Israel.

Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich tells Ynet the army should 'go to war' in the occupied West Bank and 'do there what we did in Gaza' to dismantle the Palestinian Authority, as Israeli authorities impose a week-long military closure across the West Bank for Sukkot, Al Jazeera reports.

Israel revokes the diplomatic status of Dutch diplomats posted to the Palestinian Authority in Ramallah, giving them seven days to return their documents, in retaliation for Dutch sanctions on West Bank settlements; it closed Britain's East Jerusalem consulate earlier in September on the same grounds.

Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem tells a Beirut rally marking two years since Nasrallah's killing that Israel has been 'unable to break the resistance' and pledges funds for housing thousands of displaced Lebanese; Lebanon says Israel's campaign since March 2026 has killed more than 4,300 people. Separately, a senior Israeli official says Netanyahu met UAE President Sheikh Mohamed in Abu Dhabi, with no comment from either government.

Israel's military says a strike in Gaza's Nuseirat area killed Saher Nidal Latfi Sakr, the Hamas-affiliated militant filmed abducting Noa Argamani and Avinatan Or from the Nova festival on Oct 7, 2023; Argamani was rescued in June 2024 and Or freed in October 2025 under the ceasefire. No Palestinian account of the strike was reported.

Defence Minister Israel Katz orders a week-long closure of the occupied West Bank, shutting crossings until Saturday and barring Palestinians with Israeli work permits; troops block entrances to several villages in the Ramallah area.

National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir posts a video from the cell of Hamas prisoner Salama, jailed for 30 years over 1996 bus bombings, telling him 'I want you executed'; the Palestinian Authority's detainees commission and Hamas condemn it on Monday, and Palestinian groups call it an election stunt before Israel's Oct 27 vote.
Gaza health officials say Israeli strikes killed two women, in Gaza City and Nuseirat; the Israeli military says it struck a militant in Nuseirat.

Lebanese state media report a large Israeli detonation in the occupied southern village of Mansouri; Israel says it completed an operation there and has destroyed more than 600 'terrorist infrastructure sites'.

Lebanese PM Nawaf Salam presses Secretary of State Rubio in Washington for further implementation of the framework agreement with Israel; Lebanon says Israel's campaign since March has killed more than 4,300 people.
The UAE confirms Netanyahu made an unannounced visit to Abu Dhabi on Sunday to meet President Mohamed bin Zayed, a month before Israel's election.
More than 100 Israeli settlers attack Jalud, south of Nablus, burning two homes of the al-Tubasi family, who were trying to return under an Israeli court ruling, the BBC reports.
An Israeli strike on a Gaza City apartment building kills Izz al-Din al-Beik, head of Hamas's armed wing in northern Gaza; Hamas confirms his death and Israel says he planned attacks.
Netanyahu says there are 'indications' enemies may attack before the Oct 27 election and Defence Minister Katz threatens Hamas leaders abroad; opposition leader Lapid calls it fear-mongering.
Qatar's PM, a Gaza mediator, says 'nothing is justifying' Israel's conduct in Gaza, while condemning the Oct 7 attack.
The US Senate blocks a resolution requiring a report on violence in the occupied West Bank, including the deaths of US citizens; Reuters gives the vote as 47-51 and Al Jazeera as 47-53.

After an urgent security briefing, opposition leader Lapid says the Oct 27 election will take place on time and 'there is no reason to panic the public', rejecting Netanyahu's warning of a pre-election attack as fear-mongering.

A flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv makes an emergency landing at Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, after what Israeli officials describe as an attack on the captain by the co-pilot; Security Minister Ben Gvir calls it a terrorist attempt to crash the plane, a motive not independently established.
Israeli strikes kill five people in Gaza, medics say, according to a Straits Times (Reuters) report; further details could not be read this edition.
Israeli attacks across Gaza kill at least eight civilians, including six in a strike on a minibus in Gaza City's Tel al-Hawa area, Palestinian medical officials say.

Israeli officials say passengers and crew overpowered a flydubai co-pilot who stabbed the captain and tried to crash the flight; Israel says it will tighten security checks on pilots flying into the country.
Netanyahu says it is too early to say what motivated the flydubai pilot who stabbed his captain and tried to crash the flight; the pilot is being questioned by Saudi authorities.
The bodies of 105 Palestinians recovered from the rubble of a residential block destroyed early in the war are prepared for burial in Gaza, Al Jazeera reports.
The UAE opens a criminal investigation into a possible 'terrorist' link in the flydubai cockpit attack; Netanyahu says the co-pilot underwent 'Islamist radical indoctrination'.
Six sources tell Reuters that Syrian officials and Hezbollah held their first known face-to-face talks, in Turkey last month, to ease tensions; no government has confirmed the meeting.
Saudi Arabia's interior ministry says a preliminary probe with a UAE team found the flydubai co-pilot assaulted the captain before the emergency landing in Tabuk.
An Israeli drone strike on a tent in al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, kills one man and wounds three, according to Nasser Medical Complex.

Settlers shoot dead Mashour Yassin, 51, and wound another man in Yasuf in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials say; the UN says more than 80 Palestinians have been killed in the West Bank this year.
Syria and Turkey deny Reuters' report that Syrian officials and Hezbollah met in Turkey last month.
Residents of Ras al-Ahmar in the occupied West Bank say no water has reached them for three days after Israeli forces sealed access points while building a barrier and patrol road.

The WHO says repeated Israeli delays to medical supplies entering Gaza, which can come in only through Kerem Shalom, risk 'devastating consequences'; one prosthetics shipment has been rejected four times in six months.

An Israeli air attack on the al-Asala apartment building in Gaza City's Remal neighbourhood kills at least five Palestinians without warning, Al Jazeera reports (ST earlier reported four); Israel says Hamas is rearming in violation of the ceasefire, which Hamas denies.

Settlers attack Palestinian olive pickers and burn trees at several West Bank sites including Beita and Awarta, and Israeli forces detain and assault journalists in Beita, Al Jazeera reports, citing its correspondents and a volunteer activist at the scene.

The Israeli military says the strike on the Gaza City apartment targeted Ali al-Amoudi, whom it calls the 'right-hand man' of the late Yahya Sinwar, and that it is reviewing whether he was killed; local officials say five people died, four of them women.

Al Jazeera reports that two Christian women, Maysa Abu Daoud and her daughter Mary al-Najjar, were among the five people killed in the 3 Oct Israeli strike in Gaza City's Remal neighbourhood; the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, expressed 'deep sorrow and grief'.
Israel holds a national day of remembrance three years after the 7 October 2023 attack; Netanyahu vows there will be no Hamas rule in Gaza.
Israeli forces kill at least one Palestinian after opening fire on a vehicle near Bani Naim, east of Hebron, and injure several others in incidents across the West Bank.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemns the Hamas attack and calls for a permanent Gaza ceasefire ahead of its third anniversary; Israel says it will not withdraw troops until Hamas disarms.
Israeli strikes kill at least two Palestinians in Gaza, one near Al Shifa Hospital, health officials say; Israel's military says it targeted militants.

Defence Minister Israel Katz puts the military on high alert for the 7 October anniversary, citing intelligence on Hamas plans to attack troops in Gaza, and warns Gazans would pay a 'heavy price' if forces are harmed.
Israeli settlers beat AFP photographer Jaafar Ashtiyeh while he was covering violence in the West Bank, according to the news agency.
Britain makes a last-ditch effort to stop Israel closing its East Jerusalem consulate, which Israel has threatened over UK sanctions on settlements.

Israelis mark three years since the 7 October 2023 attack, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage by Israeli tallies; Gaza's health authorities say Israel's offensive has killed more than 74,000 people, and strikes have continued despite the October 2025 ceasefire.

Israeli strikes kill at least four Palestinians across Gaza, including a Civil Defence rescue volunteer near Kamal Adwan Hospital in Beit Lahiya, according to medical sources cited by Al Jazeera and Anadolu.

The Palestinian health ministry says a 44-year-old man was killed and 16 people wounded when settlers attacked olive harvesters near Burqa, west of Nablus; Palestinian authorities say Israeli forces protected the settlers.
Palestinian officials say Israeli strikes killed five people in Gaza as Israel marked the third anniversary of the 7 October attack.
UNIFIL says several rounds of small-arms fire targeted one of its positions near Kfar Shouba along the Blue Line on Wednesday; it is investigating.

Israel says 20 British diplomats, including the Consul General, will leave the East Jerusalem consulate it ordered shut over UK settlement sanctions; the UK says the building will stay open as a 'UK Mission'.
Britain and Israel agree the East Jerusalem consulate will stay open as a slimmed-down 'UK Mission' with seven staff after 20 diplomats leave.
Islamic Relief says at least 1,454 Palestinians, including 320 children, have been killed in Gaza in the year since the ceasefire, citing health ministry figures.
The Palestinian Authority will postpone the 28 November legislative election, possibly to September 2027, citing worsening conditions, according to a letter seen by Reuters.
The UN migration agency says almost all of Gaza's nearly 2 million people need tents or shelter help before winter, with El Niño threatening floods and supplies limited by Israeli restrictions.
More than 100 humanitarian, rights and civil-society groups say Gaza's year-old ceasefire 'exists in name only', with Israeli forces still killing Palestinians daily and aid restricted.
An Israeli drone strike wounds six people, five of them Syrians, in Lebanon's Hermel district near the Syrian border, the Lebanese health ministry says.
Israeli strikes kill at least five Palestinians in Gaza City, four near Panda Mall and one in Tuffah, medics say; Israel says it targeted militants.

Palestinian President Abbas postpones legislative elections due next month and sets legislative and presidential polls for 11 Sep 2027, blaming Israeli measures; Israel's foreign minister calls that 'yet another ridiculous lie'.

One year after the US-brokered ceasefire was announced, displaced Gazans tell AFP the truce has not brought peace; Israel has reduced the intensity of its strikes but keeps them up and controls about 70% of the territory, and reconstruction has not begun.

Two men are killed in southern Lebanon's Bint Jbeil district during the olive harvest, one by shelling near Yater and one by leftover ordnance in Froun, Lebanon's National News Agency says; the Lebanese army blames Israeli tank fire and calls it a 'flagrant breach' of existing agreements.

An Israeli strike kills at least two Palestinians in southern Gaza, health officials say; the Israeli military says it targeted a militant. Gaza health officials say at least 1,400 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since last October's ceasefire.

A 14-year-old Israeli boy is killed and 24 people are injured when what was most likely unexploded ordnance goes off during a school hiking trip near the Lebanon border, Israel's ambulance service says.

Israeli forces raid the Ramallah offices of the Union of Palestinian Women's Committees and the Addameer prisoner-rights group and deploy snipers around the Palestine Medical Complex, Al Jazeera reports.

Hezbollah says it will pay up to US$14,000 to families in Beirut and its southern suburbs whose homes were destroyed in this year's war with Israel; the US disputes reports that Iran sent US$200 million for such aid.

An Israeli strike on a car in Gaza City's Tuffah neighbourhood kills one person, emergency services tell Al Jazeera, and a four-year-old boy dies of earlier wounds in central Gaza; journalists are wounded during Israeli operations in the occupied West Bank.
Israel's army chief says troops are being reinforced on all fronts because the risk of border incidents has grown ahead of the election.
UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix urges the Security Council to start talks on the future of the UNIFIL mission in Lebanon, whose mandate expires at the end of the year.
The EU says it regrets Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas's decision to postpone legislative and presidential elections by almost a year.
COGAT says commercial goods have stopped entering Gaza because merchants suspended coordination over a fee it says Hamas imposed on each truck; Hamas denies the claim.
BBC Verify identifies 254 incidents in Gaza, Lebanon, the West Bank and Israel that the IDF said it was investigating but that have no public outcome.
The Palestinian Prisoner's Society says Israel has detained more than 2,000 Palestinian children since October 2023, with at least 350 currently held; a claim by the Palestinian rights group.
A Hezbollah lawmaker says explosives seized at a Bekaa checkpoint last week belonged to the group and were meant for use against Israel, amid Beirut's push to disarm it.
Rubio tells Lebanon's President Aoun that returning the seized explosives to Hezbollah 'should be out of the question'.
China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi tells Israeli President Isaac Herzog that Israel should stop and reverse the 'forced establishment' of West Bank settlements, Beijing says.
About 80 masked Israeli settlers attack Palestinian olive pickers in Abu Falah near Ramallah, burning trees and injuring at least two people, including a journalist.
UNICEF says gains against malnutrition in Gaza are fragile and urges all crossings to stay open after Israel said commercial goods have stopped entering.

Masked settlers attack Palestinian olive harvesters near Abu Falah in the West Bank; a local official says 12 Palestinians are hurt, and a foreign journalist is also injured, the BBC reports from the scene.
Italian prosecutors place Defence Minister Israel Katz and senior officials under investigation over the treatment of detained Gaza flotilla activists.

Masked settlers attack a delegation of European diplomats from Belgium, France, Poland and the Holy See in Taybeh near Ramallah; the IDF condemns it and opens an investigation, while Netanyahu's office casts doubt on the account. Rubio says the US has asked Israel to 'crack down' on settler violence.
Israeli drone strikes kill at least six Palestinians in northern, central and southern Gaza, including near Jabalia, Palestinian medical and emergency workers say.
A mass funeral is held in Gaza City for 75 Palestinians whose remains were recovered from the rubble of destroyed homes in recent weeks, Gaza's Health Ministry says.
US diplomats led by Assistant Secretary of State Riley Barnes visit Taybeh after Israeli settlers attacked European diplomats and a US photojournalist there.
Israeli police say they have arrested 10 suspects (eight reported earlier in the day) over weekend West Bank attacks on European diplomats in Taybeh and on a US photojournalist.
timeline.source: BBC, Al Jazeera, The Straits Times

timeline.event: The World Food Programme says funding shortages will force it to cut the number of people it feeds in Gaza from 1.6 million to 1.1 million as winter approaches.
COGAT says Israel will resume allowing commercial goods into Gaza after a days-long halt, saying merchants report Hamas has withdrawn its payment demands
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth meets Netanyahu during an unannounced visit to Israel, Axios reports citing two sources; Reuters could not immediately verify it
timeline.source: Al Jazeera, The Straits Times (citing Axios)

timeline.event: Israeli strikes and gunfire kill at least four Palestinians in Gaza, including a couple in Gaza City and a 17-year-old in Khan Younis, medics say; Israel's military says it struck a militant in Gaza City

Al Jazeera reports Gaza families facing shortages of eggs and milk and rising prices after Israel halted commercial shipments on 14 Oct; Israel said on 19 Oct shipments would gradually resume, and WFP has cut the number of people it feeds from 1.6 million to 1.1 million because of funding shortfalls
US congressional candidate Brad Lander is among about 90 volunteers detained by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank, according to American and Israeli rights groups.

Israeli strikes and gunfire kill at least four people in Gaza in separate incidents in Gaza City, Khan Younis and near Jabalia, health officials in the enclave say; the Israeli military did not immediately comment.

An Israeli court releases nine of 10 settlers arrested over attacks on a US journalist and European diplomats in the occupied West Bank, placing them under house arrest; UN chief Antonio Guterres says the situation in the occupied Palestinian territory is 'out of control'.

Israeli forces arrest 36 Palestinians in raids across the occupied West Bank, including 14 in Masafer Yatta, Wafa reports citing the Palestinian Prisoner's Society, as attacks on farmers during the olive harvest increase.

Two suspected Palestinian gunmen kill two Israeli soldiers and wound three Israelis at a checkpoint at Hebron before being shot dead, the Israeli military says; Netanyahu orders the army to prepare a full closure of the West Bank ahead of Tuesday's election.

Netanyahu announces a major West Bank operation after the Hebron attack, and Israeli forces launch a 'targeted' operation in Hebron; Italy calls for the release of five Italian activists detained by Israeli police in Kiryat Arba.
Israeli forces raid at least 15 towns in the northern West Bank and detain dozens, Al Jazeera reports; the military says its operation will last several days and include demolitions.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: No new outbreak figures arrived between editions, so WHO's 23 Oct Ebola update is still the latest word: DR Congo is adding hundreds of confirmed cases a week, and the outbreak's first vaccine trial is under way in Bunia. Kenya's cluster looks closed for now, because its second death was a relative of the first patient who was already in quarantine, and the health ministry still sees no community spread. Nigeria's case is the open question, as its virus is genetically close to Kenya's but investigators have not found how the two connect. The vaccine on trial, Ervebo, is licensed only against the Zaire strain, so a result would matter beyond this epidemic. Outside Africa, US measles cases are still rising week on week. For readers the risk stays travel-linked: check advisories for East and Central Africa and mention recent trips if a fever follows.

outbreaks.name: DR Congo - Ebola (Bundibugyo virus)
outbreaks.status: Still growing in DR Congo, where a first vaccine trial began on 23 Oct; Kenya reports a second death and Nigeria one imported case
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO DON622 (23 Oct), data as of 20 Oct: 9,704 confirmed cases and 4,687 deaths in DR Congo; ECDC's 23 Oct update gives the same. Countries = DRC + Kenya (nine confirmed cases per ECDC as of 22 Oct; a second death reported by its health ministry on 23 Oct) + Nigeria (one imported case). WHO counts five countries since May, including Uganda (now Ebola-free) and France.

outbreaks.name: United States - measles
outbreaks.status: CDC lists 4,588 cases and three deaths in 2026, as of 22 Oct
outbreaks.scope_note: US CDC data as of 22 Oct (page updated 23 Oct): 4,588 confirmed cases in 2026, 43 outbreaks. CDC lists 3 deaths, flagged as subject to change. Pennsylvania's officials separately report at least five measles-linked deaths in the state, so tallies diverge.

stories.headline: WHO: DR Congo's Ebola count reaches 9,704 confirmed cases and 4,687 deaths, with Nigeria the fifth country affected
stories.summary: WHO's Disease Outbreak News of 23 Oct reports 976 more confirmed cases and 482 more deaths in DR Congo since its 8 Oct update, bringing the total to 9,704 cases and 4,687 deaths as of 20 Oct, a crude fatality rate of 48.3%. Cases have been found in 66 health zones across eight provinces, and Ituri remains the epicentre with 7,040 cases. Since May the outbreak has reached DR Congo, Uganda, France, Kenya and Nigeria. ECDC's page, updated on 23 Oct, gives the same DR Congo figures.

stories.headline: First Ebola vaccine trial in DR Congo's outbreak begins in Bunia, testing Ervebo against the Bundibugyo strain
stories.summary: WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on 23 Oct that the first participants were vaccinated in Bunia, capital of Ituri province, the epicentre of the outbreak, Al Jazeera (AFP) and The Straits Times report. Ervebo is approved against the more common Zaire strain; the Tumaini trial uses ring vaccination of high-risk contacts and includes pregnant women and children aged 12 and older, ST reports. No vaccine is approved for Bundibugyo.
stories.source: The Straits Times, Al Jazeera (AFP), WHO

stories.headline: Kenya reports a second Ebola death and says there is 'no evidence' of community spread
stories.summary: The 65-year-old woman developed symptoms in quarantine and was a close relative of the Kenyan man who died of Ebola on 5 Oct, the health ministry said on 23 Oct, The Straits Times (Reuters) and Al Jazeera report. Kenya has seven patients in treatment at two isolation facilities, all linked to the first case.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Reuters), Al Jazeera (AFP), BBC

stories.headline: Nigeria says its Ebola case is genetically close to the virus in Kenya's first case
stories.summary: Genomic analysis shows the virus in Nigeria's only confirmed case is closely related to the strain detected in Kenya's index case, Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said on 23 Oct, The Straits Times reports; there is no evidence the two patients had direct contact. Contacts are being traced and tested.

stories.headline: US measles cases reach 4,588 this year across 43 outbreaks, CDC says
stories.summary: CDC's weekly update, as of 22 Oct and published on 23 Oct, adds 178 cases in a week; it still lists three deaths in 2026, flagged as subject to change.

stories.headline: Switzerland says Nigeria's Ebola patient did not travel to DR Congo, contradicting Uganda
stories.summary: The Swiss foreign ministry said on 23 Oct that the patient, the wife of a Swiss diplomat in Abuja, had not been to DR Congo, The Straits Times reports (Reuters); Ugandan authorities had said she travelled to eastern Congo, and Uganda says it has no cases. WHO incident manager Catherine Smallwood told a UN briefing that WHO staff in Congo had no information showing the patient had been there, and investigations into the source of infection continue. Africa CDC now puts confirmed deaths across Congo, Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria at about 4,700, above the ECDC tally on the tile.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Reuters, WHO, Africa CDC)

stories.headline: Nigeria's and Kenya's first Ebola patients may have crossed paths at Uganda's Entebbe airport, Africa CDC says
stories.summary: Both patients travelled through Entebbe on 3 October, and investigators are checking whether they could have been exposed through shared equipment or other contact, Africa CDC's Dr Wessam Mankoula said, calling it 'one of the possible scenarios' but stressing no link has been established, the BBC reports. Kenya has confirmed nine infections, including one death; Nigeria's patient is improving in isolation, according to WHO.

stories.headline: WHO says the Ebola outbreak is becoming 'more complex', with Bundibugyo cases now in East and West Africa
stories.summary: WHO's Africa director Mohamed Janabi said on 22 Oct that Kenya, DR Congo and Nigeria have active or recent cases, while Uganda, which had cases earlier in the year, has been declared Ebola-free, Al Jazeera reports (AFP, AP, Reuters). WHO and Africa CDC said they had no confirmed information that Nigeria's patient travelled to DR Congo; Switzerland says she is believed to have been infected in Uganda.

stories.headline: Nigeria says its Ebola case is a 'contained, single case' with no evidence of community spread
stories.summary: Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said there was 'no need for any panic' as officials stepped up contact tracing, and there was no reason for now to change plans for large public gatherings, The Straits Times reports (Reuters).

stories.headline: Nigeria's first Ebola patient was not tested until 13 days after falling ill, and WHO says it was not told she had been to Congo
stories.summary: The delay raises questions about containment as the Bundibugyo outbreak spans four African countries, The Straits Times (Reuters) reports, counting Uganda as well as DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria. Uganda's health ministry said the woman had travelled to Congo; WHO's representative in Nigeria said on 22 Oct the agency had not been told.

stories.headline: France reports the first known human case of Shamonda, a livestock virus, in a severely immunocompromised patient who died
stories.summary: French health and agriculture ministries said on 22 Oct there is no health risk to the general public identified at this time and described it as an exceptional case, CNA (Reuters) and the BBC report. The virus usually affects livestock.
stories.source: CNA (Reuters), BBC, Al Jazeera, The Straits Times

stories.headline: Nigeria's first Ebola patient is a diplomat's wife who holidayed in Uganda, and her infection matches the DR Congo Bundibugyo strain
stories.summary: The 42-year-old, originally from Uganda and based in Abuja, fell ill three days after returning home on 3 Oct from two and a half weeks in Kampala, Africa CDC's Jean Kaseya and Nigeria's health minister told the BBC. Health officials say her case matches the Bundibugyo strain behind DR Congo's outbreak (Al Jazeera), which has now reached West Africa for the first time; Nigeria is the fourth African country with a case.
stories.source: BBC, Al Jazeera, The Straits Times

stories.headline: DR Congo's Ebola count reaches 9,552 confirmed cases and 4,602 deaths, ECDC's 20 Oct update shows
stories.summary: ECDC's 20 Oct update, using DRC data to 18 Oct, counts 9,552 confirmed cases and 4,602 deaths as of 19 Oct, with 97 new cases and 41 deaths since the previous update, mostly in North Kivu and Ituri; 66 of 178 health zones across eight provinces are affected. ECDC also lists eight confirmed cases and one death in Kenya. These figures are ahead of WHO's latest formal update, DON619 (8 Oct), which had 8,728 cases and 4,205 deaths as of 6 Oct.

stories.headline: Kenya confirms a ninth Ebola case, a close relative of its first patient, and says all cases belong to one cluster
stories.summary: The new patient was already in quarantine, Kenya's health ministry said on 20 Oct; 'all nine cases belong to one cluster, and as of today there is no evidence of transmission outside this group,' director-general for health Patrick Amoth said, The Straits Times reports. The BBC also reports nine confirmed cases.

stories.headline: Tshwane tells residents to stop drinking tap water after more than 400 people fall ill from E. coli contamination near Pretoria
stories.summary: Residents of neighbourhoods in Tshwane, the municipality that includes Pretoria, were told on 20 Oct to stop drinking tap water after waterborne pathogens led hundreds of people to seek treatment, The Straits Times reports. More than 400 people, mostly children under four, fell ill with stomach cramps and diarrhoea over two weeks near Bronkhorstspruit, where high levels of E. coli were found, officials told the BBC. No deaths have been reported.

stories.headline: US CDC confirms a third measles death of 2026 as cases reach 4,410
stories.summary: CDC's measles page now lists three deaths, marked as subject to change, with 4,410 confirmed cases as of 15 Oct, The Straits Times reports; CDC has not named the states involved. Pennsylvania, the worst-hit state with 1,286 cases, has reported at least five linked deaths through its own officials, so tallies still diverge.

stories.headline: US raises its Kenya travel advisory to 'reconsider travel', citing health risks as Ebola spreads
stories.summary: The US State Department raised its advisory for Kenya from Level 2 to Level 3, asking Americans to reconsider travel, 'due to health risks', The Straits Times (Reuters) reports. Kenya confirmed its eighth Ebola case on 18 Oct as the epidemic centred in DR Congo spreads across the region.

stories.headline: Kenya confirms an eighth Ebola case, a hospital patient attendant who was already in quarantine
stories.summary: Kenya has confirmed one more Ebola case, bringing its total to eight, Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth said on 18 Oct, The Straits Times (Reuters) reports. The new patient is a 49-year-old man, not a health worker, who cleaned utensils and linens as a patient attendant and was probably exposed to Kenya's first case, the man who travelled from DR Congo and died in a Nairobi hospital on 5 Oct. He developed symptoms on 17 Oct while in quarantine and tested positive on 18 Oct; 38 people were tested that day.

stories.headline: Kenya's Ebola count rises to seven confirmed cases, including three health workers who treated its first patient
stories.summary: Kenya's Health Ministry said on 17 Oct that four more people had tested positive for the Bundibugyo virus: three health workers, aged 29, 35 and 32, who managed the index patient on 3 and 4 Oct, and a male relative of that patient, CNA (Reuters) and Al Jazeera (AP) report. They are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya. All four were in quarantine before they developed symptoms, and the ministry says nearly all contacts have been traced and there is no evidence of community spread.

stories.headline: Kenya confirms a third Ebola case, a close relative of its first two patients
stories.summary: The 65-year-old woman was a primary contact of the first two cases and had been in quarantine, Kenya's Health Ministry said on 16 Oct, Al Jazeera (AFP/Reuters) reports. The ministry says there is no community spread and 127 of 130 listed contacts are in quarantine. Kenya's first patient, who had been ill in DR Congo and travelled via Uganda, died in Nairobi on 5 Oct.

stories.headline: Africa CDC and Congo's health authorities say more than US$700 million in Ebola response funds is unaccounted for
stories.summary: Financial information from aid organisations leaves more than US$700 million of donor money yet to be accounted for, Africa CDC and Congolese health officials said this week, calling for more transparency, The Straits Times (Reuters) reports. The concerns could complicate a response already hampered by mistrust of health workers.

stories.headline: ECDC's weekly threats report for 10-16 Oct (week 42) keeps Ebola and the unexplained Russian pneumonia death on its watch list
stories.summary: ECDC's Communicable Disease Threats Report for week 42 covers Ebola, the pneumonia of unknown cause in Russia, mpox and West Nile virus in the EU/EEA, Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, dengue, chikungunya and diphtheria, as well as respiratory viruses. The detailed figures are in the report itself.

stories.headline: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak reaches an eighth province, North Ubangi on the border with the Central African Republic, health officials say
stories.summary: Two health officials said on 15 Oct that two cases have been confirmed in North Ubangi, though Congolese authorities have not yet announced them officially, The Straits Times (Reuters) reports. Ituri remains the epicentre, with cases rising recently in North Kivu; the outbreak has more than 9,000 confirmed cases.

stories.headline: WHO reports eight MERS cases, including one death, in Saudi Arabia so far this year
stories.summary: Between 1 Jan and 5 Oct 2026 Saudi Arabia reported eight laboratory-confirmed MERS-CoV cases from six locations, five of them in people aged 70 or older, WHO said in a Disease Outbreak News published on 15 Oct (UTC). Seven had underlying conditions, two reported direct camel contact, and no epidemiological link was found between cases. WHO says sustained community transmission has not been observed and there is no licensed vaccine.

stories.headline: Belgium reports its first two deaths from West Nile virus
stories.summary: Flanders confirmed the two deaths on 15 Oct from the mosquito-borne virus, which has been spreading across Europe this season, The Straits Times reports. Most infections cause mild or no symptoms; rare severe cases cause encephalitis or meningitis.

stories.headline: Kenya confirms a second Ebola case and says there is 'no evidence' of wider spread
stories.summary: The patient, a relative of the Kenyan man who died last week after living in DR Congo, is being treated in isolation; authorities have identified 128 contacts linked to the first case and traced 113, CNA (Reuters) and the BBC report.

stories.headline: DR Congo's confirmed Ebola cases pass 9,000, with 4,381 deaths, as efforts to curb transmission falter
stories.summary: The Health Ministry reported 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths on Tuesday, a fatality rate of nearly half of known cases, Al Jazeera (AP) reports. That is 88 cases and 45 deaths above the ECDC relay of 11 Oct data; WHO's latest formal count (DON619, 8 Oct) was 8,728 and 4,205.

stories.headline: DR Congo's Ebola epidemic reaches a new health zone, Alimbongo in North Kivu, as Kenya's imported case underlines cross-border risk
stories.summary: Citing WHO's 8 Oct update, Al Jazeera reports Alimbongo recorded four confirmed cases including two deaths, and that North Kivu accounts for a growing share of new infections, while Ituri remains worst hit overall. WHO says Kenya identified 28 contacts of its fatal imported case, a Kenyan who fell ill in DR Congo and flew to Nairobi via Kampala; Kenyan officials have given different contact-tracing figures.

stories.headline: WHO says it still does not know what caused the pneumonia that killed a worker at Russia's Irkutsk anti-plague institute, and that no plague case was registered
stories.summary: In Disease Outbreak News 620, WHO said Russian authorities reported negative tests for plague and the other high-threat pathogens tested in the worker and her contacts, who remain without symptoms, and no further linked severe pneumonia cases. With no confirmed cause, WHO says it cannot independently judge whether contact monitoring was long enough, and a laboratory-associated exposure 'cannot be fully excluded'.
stories.source: WHO, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Patch HPE Aruba controllers and gateways first: eight maximum-severity ArubaOS flaws allow unauthenticated code execution, and a separate campaign has already harvested more than 70,000 firewall and VPN credentials. Web stacks come second: PHP's new session-handling RCE has only a one-setting mitigation so far, and OpenAI says its agents found a code-execution bug in the Brotli library that Node.js, Bun and Envoy rely on. Ruby has fixed the regex-engine bugs behind GitLab's critical flaws, so update the runtime as well as GitLab itself. On the threat side, a suspected APT41 UEFI bootkit shows why Secure Boot revocations matter, and ransomware affiliates are now steering intrusions through AI agents. The weekend order is edge devices, then web runtimes and libraries, then firmware revocations on Windows fleets.

stories.headline: OpenAI says its agents found a code-execution flaw in the Brotli compression library used by Node.js, Bun and Envoy
stories.summary: OpenAI said on 23 Oct that AI agents testing its defences found a flaw in Brotli that lets attackers run code by sending malicious data, affecting systems built on Node.js, Bun and Envoy, The Straits Times reports. The root cause was fixed in Brotli's source in February without a release, and Brotli has now shipped updated versions and published a public record. OpenAI also said it resumed frontier training on 1 Oct after a research model gained limited internet access in September. No CVE or CVSS score was given in the report; update Brotli and runtimes that bundle it.

stories.headline: Abandoned Popcorn Time fork's updater let anyone holding a lapsed domain run code as SYSTEM or root
stories.summary: Eye Security found that Time4Popcorn's Windows and macOS updaters fetched updates over plain HTTP from the lapsed domain popcorntimeupd.xyz and ran them without signature checks (CVE-2026-30612), BleepingComputer reports. After registering the domain, Eye saw up to 3 million Windows and 350,000 macOS client connections, and used the updater to disable it, cutting requests by 98%; the domain now sits with the Shadowserver Foundation. Android users remain exposed. Remove the app.

stories.headline: China-linked APT41 suspected behind 'BlackX', a UEFI bootkit that beats Secure Boot on Windows systems missing revocations
stories.summary: Kaspersky says the bootkit targeted diplomatic organisations in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan in early 2026, The Hacker News reports, and works on patched Windows systems that have not applied the Secure Boot revocation updates. Apply the revocations (DBX updates), not just the patches.

stories.headline: Ruby patches three Onigmo regex-engine bugs that sat behind four critical GitLab RCE flaws
stories.summary: Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 fix the bugs, which GitLab found could corrupt memory while Ruby compiles a crafted regular expression and potentially lead to code execution, The Hacker News reports. GitLab patched its four critical flaws over the past month. Update Ruby on any service that compiles user-supplied patterns.

stories.headline: PHP shares a mitigation for a new, unpatched session-handling RCE flaw (CVE-2026-115560)
stories.summary: The flaw only affects sites that set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize, switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before session_start(), and keep session upload progress enabled, BleepingComputer reports. Until a patch ships, PHP advises setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0. No exploitation of this CVE is known; the exploit attempts in the wild target the separate PHP2Shell flaws, which are patched. No CVSS score has been published.

stories.headline: INC and The Gentlemen ransomware affiliates used an AI 'kill chain' framework called Phantom, exposed infrastructure shows
stories.summary: Researchers found an AI-driven intrusion set-up run by affiliates of the two ransomware groups, assessed to be Russian-speaking, which acts as both an intrusion and data-extortion operation, The Hacker News reports.

stories.headline: Quest Diagnostics confirms a breach of its Quanum LSM ordering system exposed patient records
stories.summary: Quest said it learned of unauthorised access on 21 Oct and reported it to the SEC; the number of people affected and the data types are not yet known, and the system has been taken offline, with clients told to use paper requisitions or Quanum eLabs, BleepingComputer reports. No group has claimed the attack.

stories.headline: HPE patches eight maximum-severity ArubaOS flaws that allow unauthenticated remote code execution
stories.summary: HPE fixed 72 vulnerabilities in ArubaOS (AOS-8 and AOS-10) for Aruba mobility conductors, controllers, gateways and access points, eight of them rated maximum severity: authentication bypasses, command and SQL injection, and buffer overflows that a remote, unauthenticated attacker could use to run code, BleepingComputer reports, citing HPE advisory HPESBNW05162. HPE says it knows of no public exploit code or in-the-wild exploitation. Until patched, it advises restricting CLI and web management interfaces to a dedicated layer-2 segment or VLAN, or behind layer-3 firewall policies.

stories.headline: Large campaign against exposed FortiGate and GlobalProtect firewalls exposes more than 70,000 credentials
stories.summary: Researchers say operators targeting internet-facing Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks edge devices gained access to numerous organisations worldwide and tried to compromise some victims further, The Hacker News reports. Check edge devices for compromise and rotate VPN credentials.

stories.headline: Critical flaw in Python's Pillow image library allows code execution via a crafted image
stories.summary: The Hacker News reports a critical flaw in Pillow, the widely used Python imaging library, that can lead to code execution when an application opens a crafted image. Upgrade Pillow in any service that processes user-supplied images; the CVE and fixed version were not in THN's feed at publication.

stories.headline: Russian-linked hackers used a new mesh-network backdoor in a destructive attack in Ukraine
stories.summary: The Hacker News reports that a Russia-linked group deployed a previously unseen backdoor that communicates over a mesh network during a destructive attack on a Ukrainian target. THN's feed gave no victim or vendor details at publication.

stories.headline: Critical x402 SDK flaw could let malicious APIs drain AI agents' token balances
stories.summary: The Hacker News reports a critical flaw in the x402 software development kit, used for machine-to-machine payments by AI agents, that could let a malicious API take more from an agent's token balance than intended. Developers using x402 should check for an updated SDK release.

stories.headline: PHP2Shell: Amazon saw an exploit attempt four days before disclosure, as attempts climb into the millions
stories.summary: Amazon's threat intelligence team said its MadPot honeypots logged an attempt to exploit the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) on 17 Oct, from an IP linked to a commercial anonymisation network, four days before PHP published fixes on 21 Oct, The Hacker News reports. Cloudflare saw millions of attempts after disclosure (The Straits Times, CNA), and Singapore's CSA chief said working exploits exist. Patch every PHP install now and check hosting providers. By 23 Oct, exploit attempts had reached millions and attackers were trying to install Mirai botnet malware, The Hacker News reports.
stories.source: The Hacker News (Amazon), The Straits Times, CNA, BleepingComputer, BBC

stories.headline: Node.js fixes a Brotli decoder flaw that can allow remote code execution in all supported versions
stories.summary: CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the bundled Brotli decoder, is the most serious of 10 flaws fixed on 21 Oct in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1, The Hacker News reports. Apps that decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data, including via fetch(), are exposed; Node.js 20.x and older get no fix, and Brotli 1.2.1, 1.1.1 and 1.0.10 carry the same patch for other software. On 23 Oct researchers demonstrated a working exploit, dubbed Node2Shell, against a Node.js build using crafted Brotli data, The Hacker News reports.

stories.headline: Arista patches a VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL injection zero-day (CVE-2026-114625, CVSS 9.9) already exploited in attacks
stories.summary: Any authenticated user of an on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator, even with a read-only customer account, can gain operator privileges and act as a 'superuser operator', Arista says, The Hacker News and BleepingComputer report. Fixed releases are 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12 or later; Arista published attacking IP addresses to block and advises restricting the web interface to admin networks until patched. NVD lists Arista's CVSS 3.1 score of 9.9; it is not yet in CISA's KEV catalogue.

stories.headline: eMudhra will exit the global SSL/TLS certificate business after eight of its intermediate CA keys were found recoverable
stories.summary: eMudhra's board decided on 22 Oct to withdraw from its global SSL/TLS business, five days after a researcher reported recovering the private keys of eight of its intermediate CA certificates; it says it will replace affected customers' certificates with free ones from partners, The Hacker News reports. The P-384 keys, generated in April 2025, could be recovered by checking only 256 candidate values, and Mozilla, Google and Apple have blocked the certificates (BleepingComputer).

stories.headline: Capcom confirms hackers accessed more than 11.7 million CAPCOM ID account email addresses
stories.summary: Capcom says attackers reached email addresses plus account creation dates, login counts and last-login IP addresses; 43 accounts also lost birth dates, gender, nicknames and countries, and attackers changed passwords on 196 accounts to lock owners out, BleepingComputer reports. Capcom says other passwords and card data were not exposed; it confirmed the intrusion on 19 Oct and has reported it to police and Japan's privacy regulator. Watch for phishing aimed at CAPCOM ID users.

stories.headline: Two Linux KSMBD remote code execution flaws rated 9.0 were disclosed publicly before kernel fixes landed
stories.summary: Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative rates both flaws in KSMBD, the kernel's built-in SMB server, at 9.0; ZDI-CAN-33774 can be triggered before authentication, and ZDI-CAN-33549 needs the SMB Direct transport over an RDMA-capable network, The Hacker News reports. No fix is yet in the mainline kernel and no CVEs are listed, so servers that do not need KSMBD should disable it.

stories.headline: GitLab patches CVE-2026-110264, a CVSS 10.0 regex-compiler flaw letting unauthenticated attackers run code, back to version 7.0
stories.summary: The integer overflow in GitLab's Regular Expression Compiler affects CE/EE from 7.0, released in 2014, and is fixed in 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10 and 18.11.13, according to NVD and BleepingComputer; GitLab scores it 10.0. The Hacker News notes admins who patched a separate CVSS 10 flaw on 12 Oct still need these versions. No in-the-wild exploitation has been reported.

stories.headline: Railway says an intruder may have reached customer environment variables and urges users to rotate credentials
stories.summary: The platform-as-a-service provider disclosed anomalous activity in systems that store customer environment variables, and said an unauthorised party may have accessed encrypted values and, in some cases, their decrypted contents, The Hacker News reports. Railway says a subset of users is affected but has not given a number.

stories.headline: OpenCode flaw let a malicious MCP server run code on Windows and WSL machines when developers signed in
stories.summary: Anomaly fixed the bug in OpenCode 1.18.33 on 28 Sep but did not request a CVE or publish an advisory, so scanners will not flag old versions, The Hacker News reports. Code would run with the developer's own access; update OpenCode manually.

stories.headline: LiteLLM says a suspected GitHub token leak in AI gateway logs let attackers push its malicious 1.107.0 release
stories.summary: LiteLLM said attackers got past 'multiple independent security controls' to publish 1.107.0 to PyPI and Docker Hub on 21 Oct, The Hacker News reports. Users who installed an unpinned version between 11:39 and 13:23 UTC, or pulled Docker tags v1.107.0, latest, main-latest or main-stable between 11:46 and 14:20 UTC, are affected; the build stole credentials and AI tool secrets and fetched remote code hourly. Rotate all secrets on affected hosts.

stories.headline: QPACK flaws let one connection crash many HTTP/3 servers with up to 4,000-fold memory amplification
stories.summary: FoxIO found the flaw class in seven of 10 HTTP/3 stacks and released proof-of-concept code, The Hacker News reports. Fixes are out for quic-go (Caddy, Traefik, cloudflared), Cloudflare quiche, lsquic (LiteSpeed; CVE-2026-12523) and Wireshark, while Bun, the h3 Rust library and aioquic were unpatched at disclosure. Denial of service only; no attacks seen.

stories.headline: Interpol's Operation Serengeti III disrupts nearly 11,000 cybercrime networks in Africa and makes 1,462 arrests
stories.summary: The operation across 21 countries, from 29 Jun to 31 Aug, targeted business email compromise, ransomware and online scams, recovered more than US$105 million and identified 65,929 victims, BleepingComputer reports, citing Interpol.

stories.headline: Microsoft ties the ConnectWise supply-chain attack to China-aligned Storm-0940, which used the ARTEX AI agent framework against hundreds of organisations
stories.summary: Microsoft said on 21 Oct that Storm-0940 compromised the ConnectWise Cloud Backup application and used ARTEX, a Go-based agentic AI penetration-testing framework, to automate reconnaissance, password spraying and OAuth app abuse at downstream victims since September, The Hacker News reports. Targets span aerospace and defence, energy, finance, government, semiconductors and think tanks; The Straits Times also reported the attribution. ConnectWise customers should rotate credentials and review OAuth app access.
stories.source: The Hacker News (Microsoft), The Straits Times, BleepingComputer

stories.headline: Japan's Onamae Desktop Cloud VPS service hacked, with malware planted on up to 26,739 customer servers
stories.summary: Attackers breached the Japanese VPS provider's infrastructure and installed malware on as many as 26,739 customer servers, BleepingComputer reports. Customers of the service should check their servers and rotate credentials.

stories.headline: CISA says attackers are chaining four Plex Media Server flaws ('Plex2Shell') to breach servers
stories.summary: CISA reports active exploitation of four Plex Media Server vulnerabilities chained to compromise servers, BleepingComputer reports, after adding them to KEV on 20 Oct. Earlier reports showed the patched chain being used to install crypto miners. Update Plex Media Server and check internet-exposed instances.
stories.source: BleepingComputer, CISA KEV, The Hacker News

stories.headline: North Korea's Lazarus hackers use post-quantum cryptography to protect malware delivery
stories.summary: Lazarus operators are encrypting malicious payloads with a post-quantum method in campaigns that mix older and newer malware, BleepingComputer reports.

stories.headline: Sophos details 'Bronze Sandcastle', a China-aligned group using Sandboxie DLL sideloading against targets in Asia and Africa
stories.summary: The previously undocumented cluster has targeted organisations in Asia and Africa since mid-2025, and its most distinctive marker is consistent abuse of Sandboxie DLL sideloading to deploy backdoors, Sophos researcher Gabor Szappanos said, The Hacker News reports.

stories.headline: Attackers hijacked more than 300 Tor exit relays in early October to intercept SSH logins and steal passwords
stories.summary: Attackers took control of more than 300 Tor exit relays and redirected SSH connections to servers that harvested login passwords, a researcher found, The Hacker News reports. Only password logins to SSH servers made through Tor between 1 and 5 Oct, where the user accepted the changed host key, were exposed. Anyone who did that should rotate those passwords and move to key-based SSH authentication.

stories.headline: CISA and FBI say SafePay ransomware has hit at least 600 critical infrastructure organisations since August 2024
stories.summary: A joint advisory (AA26-293A) from CISA, the FBI, the US Secret Service and UK and German police says SafePay gets in through exposed or brute-forced credentials, VPN access, phished accounts and scripts that exploit known edge-device flaws, then steals data before encrypting and may wipe shadow copies and NAS backups, BleepingComputer reports. Victims span North America, South America, Europe and Australia, and the real count is likely higher because the leak site lists only those that did not pay. Prioritise MFA, restrict admin tools and patch the VPN and firewall flaws in CISA's KEV catalogue.

stories.headline: State Bank of India confirms a data leak after 3,897 customer records turned up in a dark-web set of about 375,000
stories.summary: India's largest bank said in a 21 Oct stock-exchange filing that it had 'experienced an incident involving the loss of certain data' and does not yet know where the data came from, The Hacker News reports.
